1672731.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
1672731.action_summary: Conduct a study to determine the feasibility of utilizing alternative fuels and alternative fuel technologies in city ferries.

1680979.action_summary: Notify parents of current students and current employees of any public school that has been the subject of a reportable environmental inspection or environmental report.

1680979.deadline_text: within ten days of receipt of the results that trigger such notification requirement; provided that if such results are received during a scheduled school vacation period exceeding five days, such notification shall occur no later than ten days following the end of such period

1680979.action_summary: Make reasonable efforts to notify parents of former students and former employees of any school for which notification is required.
1680979.quote: The department shall also make reasonable efforts to notify the parents of former students and former employees of any school for which notification is required pursuant to this subdivision.
1680979.deadline_text: within ten days of receipt of the results that trigger such notification requirement; provided that if such results are received during a scheduled school vacation period exceeding five days, such notification shall occur no later than ten days following the end of such period

1680979.action_summary: Notify directors of all afterschool programs under the department's jurisdiction that utilize school buildings or property for which notification is required.
1680979.quote: The department shall notify the directors of all afterschool programs under the jurisdiction of the department, including but not limited to, any athletic programs, known to utilize any school building or other school property for which notification is required pursuant to subdivision b of this section.
1680979.deadline_text: within ten days of receipt of the results that trigger such notification requirement; provided that if such results are received during a scheduled school vacation period exceeding five days, such notification shall occur no later than ten days following the end of such period

1680979.action_summary: Notify all local elected officials, community education councils, and local community boards representing the district of any school for which notification is required.
1680979.quote: The department shall notify all local elected officials, community education councils and local community boards representing the district of any school for which notification is required pursuant to subdivision b of this section.
1680979.deadline_text: within ten days of receipt of the results that trigger such notification requirement; provided that if such results are received during a scheduled school vacation period exceeding five days, such notification shall occur no later than ten days following the end of such period

1680979.action_summary: Post a conspicuous link to any environmental report or reportable environmental inspection on the department's website, searchable by school, community school district, council district, and borough.
1680979.quote: The department shall conspicuously post a link to any environmental report or reportable environmental inspection on the department's website within ten days of receipt of such report or inspection. Such reports or reportable inspections shall be searchable by school, community school district, council district and borough.
1680979.deadline_text: within ten days of receipt of such report or inspection

1680979.action_summary: Submit to the council and post to its website an annual report regarding the results of any reportable environmental inspection and environmental report concerning any public school, including summaries, investigative and remedial work, air quality progress, and status of consent orders, disaggregated by school, district, council district, and borough.
1680979.quote: Not later than November first, two thousand fifteen and annually thereafter, the department shall submit to the council and conspicuously post to its website a report regarding the results of any reportable environmental inspection and environmental report concerning any public school
1680979.deadline_text: Not later than November first, two thousand fifteen and annually thereafter

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Compile and publish a pilot program list of multiple dwellings with six or more units meeting specified criteria, and maintain such list on the websites of the department and the department of buildings.
1681072.quote: The department shall compile and publish a pilot program list. The criteria used to select buildings to be included on the pilot program list shall be promulgated by the department in rules

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing criteria for selecting buildings to be included on the pilot program list, limited to specified categories of buildings located in designated community districts and city-sponsored rezoning areas.
1681072.quote: The criteria used to select buildings to be included on the pilot program list shall be promulgated by the department in rules and shall be limited to:

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Establish a method of identifying buildings where there have been adjudications of harassment and add such buildings to the pilot program list within 30 days after identification.
1681072.quote: The department shall establish a method of identifying buildings where there have been adjudications of harassment after the effective date of the local law that added this section, and may request the cooperation of the tenant harassment prevention task force to establish and effectuate such method. The department shall add a building to the pilot program list within 30 days after it is identified in accordance with such method.
1681072.deadline_text: within 30 days after it is identified

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Publish notice of applications for certification of no harassment in a publication of general circulation for seven consecutive days and mail notice to specified parties including the owner, occupants, community board, city council member, and government agencies.
1681072.quote: Upon the receipt of an application for a certification of no harassment, the department shall publish notice in a publication of general circulation for a period of seven consecutive days, shall mail notice to the owner at the address provided on the application and the address provided in the last registration with the department

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Publish notices in English and in any other language prevalent in the district, as determined by the commissioner, and ensure notice is available in any covered language as defined in section 8-1002.
1681072.quote: The notice shall be published in English and in any other language prevalent in the district, as determined by the commissioner, and shall include a statement that such notice is available in any covered language, as defined in subdivision j of section 8-1002.

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Post notice in a conspicuous place at each pilot program building for which a certification of no harassment is sought.
1681072.quote: shall post notice in a conspicuous place at the pilot program building for which the certification of no harassment is sought

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Grant or deny a certification of no harassment within 45 days after the office of administrative trials and hearings issues a report and recommendation.
1681072.quote: Within 45 days after the office of administrative trials and hearings issues a report and recommendation, the department shall either grant or deny such certification of no harassment.
1681072.deadline_text: Within 45 days after the office of administrative trials and hearings issues a report and recommendation

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Mail notice of denial of certification accompanied by written findings to the applicant and owner of record and file such notice with the office of the city register or Richmond county clerk.
1681072.quote: If a certification of no harassment is denied, notice of such denial accompanied by written findings indicating the grounds for such denial shall be mailed to the applicant and owner of record and shall be filed in the office of the city register or the Richmond county clerk.

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Establish criteria in rules for cure agreements to ensure effective implementation, including a requirement that lawful tenants residing in the building during the 60-month period preceding the denial or rescission have priority in allocation of low income units.
1681072.quote: The department shall promulgate rules providing for the administration and enforcement of such an agreement, and shall establish criteria for such an agreement to ensure the effective implementation thereof. 1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Ensure that floor area of low income housing required under cure agreements is in addition to and not in substitution for floor area used to satisfy real property tax abatement, exemption, or zoning resolution floor area ratio requirements.
1681072.quote: The department shall ensure that floor area of low income housing required under paragraph (1) of this subdivision is in addition to and not in substitution for floor area of low income housing that may be used by the owner to satisfy an eligibility requirement of any real property tax abatement or exemption program

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Ensure that city, state, or federal subsidy is not used for construction of low income housing required under cure agreements.
1681072.quote: The department shall ensure that a city, state or federal subsidy shall not be used for the construction of low income housing required under paragraph (1) of this subdivision.

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Suspend a certification of no harassment and request that the department of buildings issue a stop-work notice and order upon reasonable cause to believe harassment has occurred during the certification period.
1681072.quote: If the department has reasonable cause to believe that harassment has occurred during the effective period of a certification of no harassment, the commissioner shall suspend the certification of no harassment for the pilot program building. Upon the request of the department, the department of buildings shall not approve any construction documents or issue an initial or reinstated permit in connection with covered categories of work or, if such documents have been approved or such permit has been issued, issue a stop-work notice and order pursuant to section 28-505.6.

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Mail notice of suspension of a certification of no harassment to the applicant, owner of record, and known tenants, and file such notice with the city register or Richmond county clerk.
1681072.quote: Notice of such a suspension of a certification of no harassment shall be mailed to the applicant, the owner of record of such pilot program building and known tenants of such building and shall be filed with the city register or Richmond county clerk.

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Commence a proceeding at the office of administrative trials and hearings not later than 30 days after a suspension of certification to determine whether to rescind the certification.
1681072.quote: As soon as reasonably possible after a request for a hearing by an owner who has received a notice of suspension, but not later than 30 days after such suspension, the department shall commence a proceeding at the office of administrative trials and hearings by filing the required pleadings.
1681072.deadline_text: not later than 30 days after such suspension

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Determine whether to rescind a certification of no harassment within 45 days of receiving the report and recommendation from the office of administrative trials and hearings.
1681072.quote: The department shall determine whether to rescind the certification of no harassment within 45 days of receiving the report and recommendation from the office of administrative trials and hearings.
1681072.deadline_text: within 45 days of receiving the report and recommendation from the office of administrative trials and hearings

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Notify the department of buildings if the department determines not to rescind a certification of no harassment.
1681072.quote: If the department determines not to rescind such certification of no harassment, the department shall notify the department of buildings of such determination and any stop work notice and order issued by the department of buildings pursuant to section 28-505.6 shall be vacated immediately.

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Mail notice of determination to rescind a certification of no harassment to the owner of record and file such notice with the city register or Richmond county clerk.
1681072.quote: If the department determines that such certification of no harassment shall be rescinded, notice of such determination accompanied by written findings indicating the grounds for such determination shall be provided to the department of buildings and shall be mailed to the owner of record of such pilot program building and filed with the city register or the Richmond county clerk.

1681072.actor_raw: the department of housing preservation and development
1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Conduct a study to evaluate the effectiveness of the pilot program in reducing harassment of tenants in designated areas and submit a report to the Speaker containing specified information no later than 6 months prior to the expiration of this local law.
1681072.quote: The department, with the advice and assistance that may be provided by any community group described in paragraph (4) of subdivision d of section 27-2093.1 of the administrative code of the city of new york, as added by section two of this local law, shall conduct a study to evaluate the effectiveness of the program in reducing harassment of tenants in the areas described in paragraph (1) of subdivision b of section 27-2093.1 of the administrative code of the city of new york, as added by section two of this local law. Such study shall be completed and a report shall be submitted to the Speaker no later than 6 months prior to the expiration of this local law.

1681072.agency_full: Department of Buildings
1681072.action_summary: Not approve construction documents, nor issue an initial or reinstated permit for alteration or demolition of a pilot program building except as set forth in article 505, and subject applications for post-approval amendments to article 505 where the application proposes a change within a covered category of work.
1681072.quote: The commissioner shall not approve construction documents, nor issue an initial or reinstated permit in connection therewith, for the alteration or demolition of a pilot program building identified by the department of housing preservation and development pursuant to section 27-2093.1 except as set forth in this article.

1681072.agency_full: Department of Buildings
1681072.action_summary: Not issue temporary or permanent certificate of occupancy for any structure on a lot subject to a restrictive declaration under the pilot program, except for low income housing, until the department of housing preservation and development certifies that required low income housing has been completed in compliance with the restrictive declaration.
1681072.quote: The department shall not issue any temporary or permanent certificate of occupancy for any new or existing structure or portion thereof on a lot subject to an restrictive declaration pursuant to subdivision e of section 27-2093.1 of the housing maintenance code, other than for any low income housing located on such lot, until the department of housing preservation and development certifies that the low income housing required by such restrictive declaration has been completed in compliance with the restrictive declaration and the department has issued a temporary or permanent certificate of occupancy for each unit of low income housing covered by such restrictive declaration.

1681072.actor_raw: the department of housing preservation and development
1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Establish a form and information requirements for applications for certification of no harassment.
1681072.quote: An application for a certification of no harassment shall be in such form and shall contain such information as shall be prescribed by the department.

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Promulgate rules prescribing a sworn statement form to be submitted by all building owners representing that there will be no harassment of occupants by or on behalf of such owners.
1681072.quote: Before a certification of no harassment may be granted, an applicant shall submit a sworn statement, in such form as the department shall prescribe, by all the owners of the pilot program building representing that there will be no harassment of the occupants of such building by or on behalf of such owners.

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Designate a community group to conduct surveys of pilot program building occupants regarding harassment and report findings to the department.
1681072.quote: The department may designate a community group to conduct a survey of the occupants of the pilot program building with respect to harassment in the pilot program building and to report its findings to the department.

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Conduct investigations and determine whether no harassment has occurred, grant a certification of no harassment, deny certification, or hold a hearing to determine if harassment occurred based on survey and investigation findings.
1681072.quote: Upon the completion of any such survey and further investigation, the department may: (A) determine that no harassment has occurred within the stated period of time and forthwith grant such certification of no harassment. (B) deny a certification of no harassment without a hearing

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Rescind a certification of no harassment if it finds that harassment occurred at a pilot program building while the certification was in effect.
1681072.quote: The department may rescind a certification of no harassment that was granted for a pilot program building if it finds that harassment has occurred at such building while such certification was in effect

1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Establish by rule reasonable fees from applicants for administrative expenses incurred in issuing certifications of no harassment, including costs for publication and notices.
1681072.quote: The department is authorized to establish by rule reasonable fees from applicants for the administrative expenses incurred by the department for issuing the certification of no harassment pursuant to this section, including costs for publication and notices.

1681072.agency_full: Department of Buildings
1681072.action_summary: Issue a stop-work notice or order or rescind approval of construction documents at the request of the commissioner of housing preservation and development pursuant to section 27-2093.1.
1681072.quote: The commissioner shall be empowered to issue a stop-work notice or order with respect to an alteration or demolition permit or to rescind approval of construction documents at the request of the commissioner of housing preservation and development pursuant to section 27-2093.1 of the housing maintenance code.

1681072.actor_raw: the departments of housing preservation and development and the department of buildings
1681072.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1681072.action_summary: Promulgate rules or take other administrative action for implementation of this local law prior to the effective date.
1681072.quote: the departments of housing preservation and development and the department of buildings may promulgate rules or take other administrative action for the implementation of this local law prior to such date
1681072.deadline_text: prior to the effective date (270 days after enactment)

1709613.action_summary: Establish an advisory committee including representatives from the restaurant industry, construction industry, environmental protection communities, and experts on health effects of cooking device pollutants to provide advice on emissions control technologies for commercial char broilers.
1709613.citation: Section 24-105(b) of the administrative code (amended by section 4)
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall appoint an advisory committee, which shall include but need not be limited to representatives of the restaurant industry and related industries, representatives of the construction industry, representatives of the environmental protection and environmental justice communities, persons with expertise regarding the health effects of pollutants associated with cooking devices

1709613.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing procedures for safeguarding public health and safety, including procedures for persons working at or near asbestos projects.
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall promulgate rules establishing procedures for the safeguarding of the health and safety of the public, including procedures to be followed by persons who work at or in the vicinity of an asbestos project.

1709613.action_summary: Promulgate rules in consultation with the fire commissioner and commissioner of buildings providing guidance to contractors on how to maintain egress at asbestos projects.
1709613.quote: The commissioner, in consultation with the fire commissioner and the commissioner of buildings, shall promulgate rules which give further guidance to contractors on how to maintain egress at asbestos projects, as such projects are defined in the rules of the department, in accordance with all applicable laws, codes, rules and regulations.

1709613.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing criteria for certifying individuals as eligible to receive an asbestos handling certificate and restrict such certificates as to supervisory and nonsupervisory functions.
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall promulgate rules establishing criteria for certifying individuals as eligible to receive an asbestos handling certificate. The commissioner may restrict the asbestos handling certificate as to certain supervisory and nonsupervisory functions and responsibilities.

1709613.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing criteria for certifying individuals as asbestos investigators.
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall promulgate rules establishing criteria for certifying individuals as asbestos investigators.

1709613.action_summary: Prescribe forms for and the content of asbestos project notifications to be submitted to the department.
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall prescribe forms for and the content of asbestos project notifications to be submitted to the department. Such notifications shall require the furnishing of information deemed relevant by the commissioner for evaluating the scope, complexity and duration of the project and the compliance with the provisions of this section

1709613.action_summary: Establish a procedure in coordination with the commissioner of buildings and fire commissioner to share information regarding violations issued under asbestos provisions.
1709613.quote: The commissioner, in coordination with the commissioner of buildings and the fire commissioner, shall establish a procedure to share information regarding violations issued pursuant to this section, in accordance with the requirements of section 28-103.7.1 of the code.

1709613.action_summary: Establish a permit requirement for asbestos projects affecting building safety and provide a date for implementation via rules.
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall establish a permit requirement for asbestos projects affecting the safety of a building. On and after a date to be provided in the rules establishing such a permit requirement, it shall be unlawful to commence or engage in such a project unless the commissioner has issued an abatement permit for such project.

1709613.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
1709613.action_summary: Post signs relating to prohibited idling at specified locations including bridge/tunnel exits, truck route intersections, bus layover areas, and bus terminals in compliance with manual standards.
1709613.quote: The department of transportation shall post signs relating to prohibited idling that shall comply with the standards set forth in the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices and, where practicable, include the maximum penalty that may be imposed for a violation of subdivision a of this section

1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to city council stating the number of engine idling violation notices issued and total penalties imposed.
1709613.quote: A report shall be submitted to the city council on an annual basis by: (1) the environmental control board that states the number of notices of violation issued for engine idling violations returnable to the environmental control board, including the total amount of penalties imposed for such notices of violations
1709613.deadline_text: on an annual basis

1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to city council stating the number of engine idling violation summonses issued and total penalties imposed.
1709613.quote: A report shall be submitted to the city council on an annual basis by: (2) the department of finance that states the number of summonses issued for engine idling violations pursuant to subdivision (p) of section 4-08 of title 34 of the rules of the city of New York, including the total amount of penalties imposed for such summonses.
1709613.deadline_text: on an annual basis

1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to comptroller and city council regarding the city's purchase of light-duty and medium-duty vehicles, including fuel economy and alternative fuel compliance data.
1709613.quote: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter, the mayor shall submit to the comptroller and the speaker of the council a report regarding the city's purchase of light-duty vehicles and medium-duty vehicles during the immediately preceding fiscal year.
1709613.deadline_text: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter

1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to comptroller and city council regarding fuel economy of light-duty vehicles purchased by the city.

1709613.deadline_text: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter

1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to comptroller and city council regarding use-based fuel economy for the city's fleet.

1709613.deadline_text: Not later than January 1, 2016, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter

1709613.action_summary: Publish annually on its website and include in the mayor's management reports the estimated total amount of fuel consumed by the city's fleet and equivalent carbon dioxide emitted, disaggregated by fuel type.

1709613.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
1709613.action_summary: Implement a program for testing the mechanical reliability and operational feasibility of alternative fuel street sweeping vehicles including a pilot project in at least four sanitation districts.
1709613.quote: Beginning no later than March 1, 2006, the commissioner of sanitation shall implement a program for testing the mechanical reliability and operational feasibility of alternative fuel street sweeping vehicles. 1709613.deadline_text: Beginning no later than March 1, 2006

1709613.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
1709613.action_summary: Collect and analyze data on alternative fuel sanitation vehicles to develop initiatives and assess feasibility of incorporating new alternative fuel vehicles into its fleet.
1709613.quote: The department of sanitation shall collect and analyze data to further develop its initiatives for and assess the feasibility of incorporating new alternative fuel sanitation vehicles and technology into its fleet.

1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to comptroller and city council regarding the city's purchase of alternative fuel buses.
1709613.quote: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter, the mayor shall submit to the comptroller and the speaker of the council a report regarding the city's purchase of alternative fuel buses during the immediately preceding fiscal year.
1709613.deadline_text: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter

1709613.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to mayor, comptroller and city council on the department's alternative fuel street sweeping vehicle pilot project, testing results, and assessment of feasibility of incorporating alternative fuel vehicles.
1709613.quote: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter, the commissioner of sanitation shall report to the mayor, the comptroller and the speaker of the council on the department of sanitation's alternative fuel street sweeping vehicle pilot project and all testing, analyses and assessments completed
1709613.deadline_text: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter

1709613.action_summary: Make determinations and publish a list of best available technology for reducing emissions from diesel-powered nonroad vehicles, reviewing and updating at least every six months.
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall make determinations, and shall publish a list containing such determinations, as to the best available technology for reducing the emission of pollutants to be used for each type of diesel-powered nonroad vehicle to which this section applies for the purposes of paragraph two of subdivision b and paragraph two of subdivision c of this section.

1709613.action_summary: Make determinations and publish a list of best available retrofit technology for diesel fuel-powered motor vehicles, reviewing and updating at least every six months.
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall make determinations, and shall publish a list containing such determinations, as to the best available retrofit technology to be used for each type of diesel fuel-powered motor vehicle to which this section applies.

1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to comptroller and city council regarding the use of ultra low sulfur diesel fuel and best available retrofit technology by diesel fuel-powered motor vehicles owned by city agencies.
1709613.quote: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter, the commissioner shall submit a report to the comptroller and the speaker of the council regarding, among other things, the use of ultra low sulfur diesel fuel and the use of the best available retrofit technology by diesel fuel-powered motor vehicles owned or operated by city agencies during the immediately preceding calendar year.
1709613.deadline_text: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter

1709613.actor_raw: the commissioner of citywide administrative services
1709613.action_summary: Establish a B20 winter pilot program to test feasibility of utilizing twenty percent biodiesel blend in city diesel vehicles during December to March.
1709613.quote: Not later than December 1, 2016, the commissioner of citywide administrative services shall establish a pilot program to determine the feasibility of utilizing an ultra low sulfur diesel fuel blend containing at least twenty percent biodiesel (B20) by volume in city-owned diesel fuel-powered motor vehicles during the months of December to March, inclusive.
1709613.deadline_text: Not later than December 1, 2016

1709613.actor_raw: the commissioner of citywide administrative services
1709613.action_summary: Issue report to mayor and city council detailing findings of the B20 winter pilot program including emissions reduction data and cost-benefit analysis.
1709613.quote: within four months of the conclusion of such pilot program, the commissioner of citywide administrative services shall issue a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council detailing the findings of such pilot program with recommendations for the use of an ultra low sulfur diesel fuel blend containing at least twenty percent biodiesel (B20) by volume in city-owned diesel fuel-powered motor vehicles during the months of December to March, inclusive.
1709613.deadline_text: within four months of the conclusion of such pilot program

1709613.action_summary: Make determinations and publish a list of best available retrofit technology for diesel-powered motor and nonroad vehicles used in solid waste and recyclable materials contracts, reviewing at least every six months.
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall make determinations, and shall publish a list containing such determinations, as to the best available retrofit technology to be used for each type of diesel fuel-powered motor vehicle and diesel fuel-powered nonroad vehicle to which this section applies.

1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to comptroller and city council regarding use of ultra low sulfur diesel fuel and best available retrofit technology by vehicles used in solid waste and recyclable materials contracts.
1709613.quote: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter, the commissioner shall submit a report to the comptroller and the speaker of the council regarding, among other things, the use of ultra low sulfur diesel fuel and the use of the best available retrofit technology by diesel fuel-powered motor vehicles and diesel fuel-powered nonroad vehicles used in the performance of a solid waste contract or recyclable materials contract during the immediately preceding fiscal year.
1709613.deadline_text: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter

1709613.action_summary: Make determinations and publish a list of best available retrofit technology for diesel-powered sight-seeing buses, reviewing and updating at least every six months.
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall make determinations, and shall publish a list containing such determinations, as to the best available retrofit technology to be used for each type of diesel fuel-powered sight-seeing bus to which this section applies.

1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to comptroller and city council regarding use of best available retrofit technology by diesel-powered sight-seeing buses.
1709613.quote: Not later than January 1, 2008, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter, the commissioner shall submit a report to the comptroller and the speaker of the council regarding, among other things, the use of the best available retrofit technology by diesel fuel-powered sight-seeing buses during the immediately preceding fiscal year.
1709613.deadline_text: Not later than January 1, 2008, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter

1709613.action_summary: Make determinations and publish a list of best available retrofit technology for diesel-powered school buses, reviewing and updating at least every six months.
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall make determinations, and shall publish a list containing such determinations, as to the best available retrofit technology to be used for each type of diesel fuel-powered school bus to which this section applies.

1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to comptroller and city council regarding use of ultra low sulfur diesel fuel and best available retrofit technology by school buses.
1709613.quote: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter, the commissioner shall submit a report to the comptroller and the speaker of the council regarding, among other things, the use of ultra low sulfur diesel fuel and the use of the best available retrofit technology by school buses during the immediately preceding fiscal year.
1709613.deadline_text: Not later than January 1, 2007, and not later than January 1 of each year thereafter

1709613.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
1709613.action_summary: Develop and implement a pilot project lasting at least one year to test benefits and reliability of auxiliary power units in ambulances.
1709613.quote: Not later than January 1, 2014, the fire department shall develop and implement a pilot project for a period of not less than one year to ascertain the benefits and reliability of utilizing auxiliary power units in ambulances operated by the city of New York.
1709613.deadline_text: Not later than January 1, 2014

1709613.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
1709613.action_summary: Submit report to mayor and city council detailing findings of the auxiliary power unit pilot project including emissions reduction data and cost-benefit analysis.
1709613.quote: Not later than July 1, 2015, the fire department shall submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council detailing the findings of such pilot project, including but not limited to data on actual reduction in vehicular emissions, and a cost-benefit analysis for equipping the entire ambulance fleet with auxiliary power units.
1709613.deadline_text: Not later than July 1, 2015

1709613.action_summary: Review technology verified by EPA and California Air Resources Board and promulgate rules setting forth best available retrofit technology for heavy duty trade waste hauling vehicles.
1709613.quote: On or before June 30, 2018, the commissioner shall review the technology verified by the United States environmental protection agency and the California air resources board for reducing the emission of pollutants that achieves reductions in particulate matter emissions at the highest classification level for diesel emission control strategies that is applicable to a particular engine and application and shall promulgate rules setting forth the best available retrofit technology to be used by heavy duty trade waste hauling vehicles to which this section applies.
1709613.deadline_text: On or before June 30, 2018

1709613.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing procedures for safeguarding public health and safety and procedures for persons working at asbestos projects.
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall promulgate rules establishing procedures for the safeguarding of the health and safety of the public and all, including procedures to be followed by persons who work at or in the vicinity of an asbestos project.

1709613.actor_raw: the commissioner of citywide administrative services
1709613.action_summary: Ensure all no. 2, no. 4 and no. 6 heating oil purchased for city buildings contains not less than five percent biodiesel (B5) by volume, except for emergency generators.
1709613.quote: After October 1, 2014, all no. 2, no. 4 and no. 6 heating oil purchased for use in any building owned by the city shall be bioheating fuel containing not less than five percent biodiesel (B5) by volume except that the provisions of this subdivision shall not apply to the use of emergency generators.
1709613.deadline_text: After October 1, 2014

1709613.actor_raw: the commissioner of citywide administrative services
1709613.action_summary: Institute a pilot program requiring not less than five percent of city-owned buildings to use heating oil containing at least ten percent biodiesel (B10) by volume beginning October 1, 2014 through October 1, 2015.
1709613.quote: The commissioner of citywide administrative services shall institute a pilot program to use greater amounts of biodiesel in city-owned buildings. Such pilot program shall require that beginning October 1, 2014, the heating oil burned in not less than five percent of city-owned buildings shall contain at least ten percent biodiesel (B10) by volume.
1709613.deadline_text: beginning October 1, 2014

1709613.actor_raw: the commissioner of citywide administrative services
1709613.action_summary: Issue report to mayor and city council detailing findings of the B10 biodiesel pilot program including recommendations on use of ten percent biodiesel in all city buildings.
1709613.quote: within six months of the conclusion of such pilot program, the commissioner of citywide administrative services shall issue a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council detailing the findings of such pilot program, including the utility of and any impediments to the use of ten percent biodiesel (B10) by volume in city-owned buildings and any recommendations for the use of ten percent biodiesel (B10) by volume in all city-owned buildings.
1709613.deadline_text: within six months of the conclusion of such pilot program

1709613.actor_raw: the commissioner of citywide administrative services
1709613.action_summary: Undertake a one-year study on the feasibility of using five percent biodiesel (B5) in all buildings throughout the city and issue recommendations to the mayor and city council.
1709613.quote: The commissioner of citywide administrative services in conjunction with the office of long-term planning and sustainability shall undertake a one year study on the feasibility of the use of five percent biodiesel (B5) by volume in all buildings throughout the city. Such study shall include recommendations on whether and when the city should require the use of five percent biodiesel (B5) by volume in heating oil in all buildings and shall be issued to the mayor and the speaker of the council
1709613.deadline_text: by April 2, 2015

1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to mayor and city council regarding waivers issued for bioheating fuel requirements and renewable biomass determinations.
1709613.quote: No later than September 1, 2013, and no later than September 1 of every year thereafter, the commissioner shall submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council, which shall include: (i) all waivers, findings and renewals of such findings issued pursuant to this section during the immediately preceding calendar year
1709613.deadline_text: No later than September 1, 2013, and no later than September 1 of every year thereafter

1709613.action_summary: Require persons who supply heating oil to buildings to annually disclose to the department information regarding fuel oil supplied by grade, location, biodiesel percentage and feedstock types.
1709613.quote: The commissioner shall require persons who supply heating oil directly to buildings in the city to disclose annually to the commissioner the following information regarding fuel oil supplied: (i) the amount in gallons of each fuel oil grade supplied by such person to buildings by zip code; and (ii) the average percentage of biodiesel blended into each fuel oil grade supplied by such person within the city and the types of feedstock used in the creation of such biodiesel.
1709613.deadline_text: annually

1709613.action_summary: Submit annual report to mayor and city council on compliance with school bus age and retrofit requirements including data on age and crankcase ventilation retrofit status of every school bus.
1709613.quote: No later than December 31, 2011, and no later than December 31 of every year thereafter, the department of education shall submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council on compliance with this section. Such report shall include, but not be limited to, data on the age and crankcase ventilation retrofit status of every school bus pursuant to a school bus contract.
1709613.deadline_text: No later than December 31, 2011, and no later than December 31 of every year thereafter

1709613.action_summary: Perform yearly reviews of a sample of school buses from at least ten vendors to verify accuracy of reported data on age and retrofit status.
1709613.quote: The department of education shall also perform yearly reviews on a sample of school buses from at least ten different vendors to verify the accuracy of data reported.
1709613.deadline_text: yearly

1709613.action_summary: Require by rule additional notification to the department prior to the start of asbestos projects as determined necessary.
1709613.quote: In addition to submission of the asbestos project notification, the commissioner may by rule require additional notification to the department prior to the start of the asbestos project.

1709613.action_summary: Prescribe by rule the circumstances under which an asbestos project notification may be amended and when a new project notification must be submitted.
1709613.quote: The commissioner may prescribe by rule the circumstances under which an asbestos project notification may be amended, and the circumstances under which a new project notification shall be submitted to the department.

1709613.action_summary: Authorize use of renewable fuels in heating systems if such fuel meets applicable ASTM standards and emissions are equal to or less than fuel oil grade no. 2.
1709613.quote: The commissioner may authorize the use of any renewable fuel in heating systems if he or she determines that such fuel meets an applicable ASTM International standard or other standard as determined by the commissioner, and the emissions from such fuel contain equal or lesser amounts of particulate matter, sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides than the emissions from fuel oil grade no. 2.

1739325.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
1739325.action_summary: Remove snow and ice and other obstructing material from fire hydrants and fire hydrant street areas at the cost and expense of the owner, lessee, or tenant of the premises fronting such hydrant.
1739325.quote: All material or things found obstructing any fire hydrant may be forthwith removed by the officers or employees of the department, at the risk, cost and expense, of the owner, lessee or tenant of the premises fronting such hydrant.

1739325.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
1739325.action_summary: Enforce the provisions of section 15-205 regarding obstruction of fire hydrants.
1739325.quote: In addition to the department, the department of sanitation may enforce the provisions of this section.

1739325.actor_raw: the commissioner of sanitation and the commissioner of the fire department
1739325.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
1739325.action_summary: Take measures necessary for implementation of the local law, including the promulgation of rules.
1739325.quote: the commissioner of sanitation and the commissioner of the fire department may take such measures as are necessary for its implementation, including the promulgation of rules, before such date
1739325.deadline_text: before 90 days after it becomes law

1739325.actor_raw: the commissioner of the fire department
1739325.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
1739325.action_summary: Take measures necessary for implementation of the local law, including the promulgation of rules.
1739325.quote: the commissioner of sanitation and the commissioner of the fire department may take such measures as are necessary for its implementation, including the promulgation of rules, before such date
1739325.deadline_text: before 90 days after it becomes law

1796997.actor_raw: Each participating agency, other than community boards and the city clerk
1796997.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
1796997.action_summary: Submit semi-annual reports on implementation of voter registration requirements, including the number of registration forms distributed, completed at agency offices, and transmitted to the board of elections.
1796997.quote: Each participating agency, other than community boards and the city clerk, shall submit semi-annual reports on their implementation of this section to the mayor's office of operations. Such reports shall include the number of registration forms distributed, the number of registration forms completed at an agency office to the extent readily ascertainable, and the number of registration forms transmitted to the board of elections.
1796997.deadline_text: by January 15 and July 15 of each year, with the first reports due by July 15, 2015

1796997.action_summary: Compile semi-annual reports from participating agencies into a single disaggregated report and deliver it to the speaker.
1796997.quote: The mayor's office of operations shall compile such reports into a single report that disaggregates such data by agency, and shall deliver such compiled report to the speaker by February 15 and August 15 of each year, with the first such report due by August 15, 2015.
1796997.deadline_text: by February 15 and August 15 of each year, with the first such report due by August 15, 2015

1812831.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1812831.action_summary: Provide appropriate training for indoor allergen inspection and for supervisory personnel, including continuing education on federal, state, and local laws and guidance documents.
1812831.quote: The department shall provide appropriate training for indoor allergen inspection and for supervisory personnel. The department shall provide for the continuing education of inspection and supervisory personnel regarding changes in applicable federal, state, and local laws

1812831.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1812831.action_summary: Promulgate a comprehensive written procedure to guide department personnel in implementing and enforcing this article, including methodology and forms for conducting inspections.
1812831.quote: The department, with the approval of the department of health and mental hygiene, shall promulgate a comprehensive written procedure to guide department personnel in implementing and enforcing this article. Such procedures shall include a methodology and a form to be used by department personnel when conducting an inspection

1812831.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1812831.action_summary: Promulgate rules for the implementation and enforcement of this article, establishing procedures for postponement requests and procedures to enforce compliance with violation corrections and work practice requirements.
1812831.quote: The department shall promulgate rules for the implementation and enforcement of this article and to effect compliance with all applicable provisions of this article, rules promulgated thereunder, and all applicable city, state or federal laws, rules or regulations. Such rules shall be subject to the approval of the department of health and mental hygiene

1812831.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1812831.action_summary: Conduct inspections and make diligent efforts to ascertain whether cockroaches, mice, rats, or visible mold are present in dwelling units when entering for code violation investigations.
1812831.quote: When entering a dwelling unit in a multiple dwelling for the purpose of investigating the existence of any violation of the code, the department shall make diligent efforts to ascertain whether there are cockroaches, mice, rats, or visible mold in the dwelling unit and shall inquire of the occupant whether cockroaches, mice, rats or mold are present

1812831.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1812831.action_summary: Conduct an inspection no later than thirty days after receipt of a complaint describing a condition that would constitute a visible mold or pest violation.
1812831.quote: In any dwelling unit in a multiple dwelling the department shall conduct an inspection pursuant to subdivision a of this section no later than thirty days after the department's receipt of a complaint describing a condition that would constitute a violation under subdivision a of section 27-2017.3 or subdivision b of section 27-2017.4.
1812831.deadline_text: no later than thirty days after the department's receipt of a complaint

1812831.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1812831.action_summary: Serve a notice of violation within ten additional days of conducting an inspection where a violation is determined to exist.
1812831.quote: Where, upon conducting an inspection, the department determines the existence of a condition constituting a violation of this article, the department shall serve a notice of violation within ten additional days of such inspection.
1812831.deadline_text: within ten additional days of such inspection

1812831.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1812831.action_summary: Leave the pamphlet developed by the department of health and mental hygiene at the premises during inspections and deliver it with all notices of violation.
1812831.quote: The pamphlet developed by the department of health and mental hygiene pursuant to section 17-199.7 shall be left at the premises of the dwelling unit at the time of an inspection made by the department pursuant to this section. Such pamphlet shall be delivered by the department in conjunction with all notices of violation issued pursuant to paragraph one of subdivision o of section 27-2115.

1812831.actor_raw: the department of health and mental hygiene
1812831.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1812831.action_summary: Certify conditions to the department of housing preservation and development within ten days after the date set for correction where an owner fails to comply with a department of health and mental hygiene order.
1812831.quote: Where the owner of the dwelling or relevant dwelling unit within such dwelling fails to comply with an order of the department of health and mental hygiene to correct a violation placed by the department of health and mental hygiene pursuant to section 17-199.6, the department of health and mental hygiene shall certify such conditions to the department of housing preservation and development within ten days after the date set for correction in said order.
1812831.deadline_text: within ten days after the date set for correction in said order

1812831.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1812831.action_summary: Provide to the council a written annual report on the department's implementation of this article, including analysis of the program, revenue and expenditures, and enforcement statistics.
1812831.quote: Within four months after the close of the first fiscal year that begins after the effective date of the local law that added this section, and within four months after the close of each fiscal year thereafter, the commissioner shall provide to the council a written report on the department's implementation of this article during the preceding fiscal year.
1812831.deadline_text: Within four months after the close of the first fiscal year that begins after the effective date

1812831.actor_raw: the department of health and mental hygiene
1812831.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1812831.action_summary: Annually prepare and publicly post on the Environmental and Health Data Portal a statistical profile on asthma rates, including asthma-related hospitalizations and emergency department visits, citywide and by neighborhoods.
1812831.quote: The department of health and mental hygiene shall annually prepare and publically post on the Environmental and Health Data Portal a statistical profile on asthma rates in the population, including asthma-related hospitalizations and asthma-related emergency department visits, city wide and by neighborhoods, based on the most recently available data.

1812831.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1812831.action_summary: Report to the council no later than 18 months from the effective date on activities undertaken to educate physicians and health care providers about indoor allergens and the availability of inspections.
1812831.quote: The department shall report to the council no later than 18 months from the effective date on activities it has undertaken to educate physicians and other health care providers who treat persons with asthma about the role of indoor allergens in asthma exacerbation and the availability of inspections for asthma triggers in their patients' primary residence
1812831.deadline_text: no later than 18 months from the effective date

1812831.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1812831.action_summary: Establish procedures to permit health professionals to request department investigations of possible indoor allergen hazards in dwellings of persons with moderate persistent or severe persistent asthma.
1812831.quote: The department shall establish procedures to permit doctors, nurses, or other health professionals, upon the consent of their patients, to request a department investigation of possible indoor allergen hazards in dwellings where persons reside who have been medically diagnosed with moderate persistent or severe persistent asthma.

1812831.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1812831.action_summary: Order owners to correct indoor allergen hazards and underlying causes within twenty-one days when an investigation determines such hazards exist.
1812831.quote: In the event that the department determines that an indoor allergen hazard exists, the department shall order the owner to correct the condition and the underlying causes of such a condition within twenty-one days, in a manner and under such safety conditions as it may specify

1812831.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1812831.action_summary: Refer orders to the department of housing preservation and development when an owner fails to substantially comply with a correction order within twenty-one days.
1812831.quote: In the event that the department determines that the owner or other person having the duty or liability to comply with an order issued pursuant to this section fails to substantially comply therewith within twenty-one days after service thereof, the department shall, in accordance with section 27-2017.10, refer such order to the department of housing preservation and development.
1812831.deadline_text: within twenty-one days after service thereof

1812831.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1812831.action_summary: Report to the council and mayor no later than 24 months from the effective date on activities undertaken under this section regarding adult asthma referrals, orders issued, and apartment remediations completed.
1812831.quote: The department shall report to the council and mayor no later than 24 months from the effective date on activities it has undertaken under this section as they relate to adults with asthma diagnoses, including but not limited to the number adult asthma referrals by type to the department for inspection
1812831.deadline_text: no later than 24 months from the effective date

1812831.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1812831.action_summary: Develop a pamphlet in English and covered languages explaining hazards associated with indoor allergens and describing tenant rights and owner responsibilities.
1812831.quote: The department shall develop a pamphlet which shall be in English and in the covered languages set forth in section 8-1002, explaining the hazards associated with indoor allergens and describing tenant rights and owner responsibilities under this law

1812831.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1812831.action_summary: Develop a training curriculum for educating owners and building maintenance personnel on appropriate work methods for controlling and removing indoor allergen hazards in rental housing.
1812831.quote: The department shall also develop a training curriculum for educating owners and building maintenance personnel on the appropriate work methods for controlling and removing indoor allergen hazards in rental housing, including integrated pest management.

1812831.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1812831.action_summary: Respond to complaints of unsafe work practices related to indoor mold hazard remediation and refer complaints of unsafe pest control to the New York state department of environmental conservation.
1812831.quote: The department shall respond to complaints of unsafe work practices related to the correction of indoor mold hazard violations that result in chemical vapors, dust, or other environmental hazards, and promptly refer complaints of unsafe pest control to the New York state department of environmental conservation.

1812831.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1812831.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing work practices for assessing and correcting indoor mold hazards and underlying defects, and from time-to-time review and revise such rules.
1812831.quote: The department shall promulgate rules, with the approval of the department of health and mental hygiene, establishing work practices when assessing and correcting indoor mold hazards, and underlying defects including violations cited by the department pursuant to this article.

1812831.actor_raw: the department of housing preservation and development
1812831.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1812831.action_summary: Conduct a final inspection to verify that visible mold violations have been corrected when a notice of violation is issued.
1812831.quote: Whenever the department shall issue a notice of violation to correct a condition that constitutes a hazardous or immediately hazardous violation of subdivision a of section 27-2017.3 the department shall conduct a final inspection to verify that the violation has been corrected.

1812831.actor_raw: the department of housing preservation and development
1812831.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1812831.action_summary: Take enforcement action as necessary, including performing or arranging for the performance of work to correct violations certified by the department of health and mental hygiene.
1812831.quote: The department of housing preservation and development may take such enforcement action as it deems necessary, including performing or arranging for the performance of work to correct the certified condition.

1812831.actor_raw: the department of housing preservation and development
1812831.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
1812831.action_summary: Take enforcement action, including performing or arranging for work to correct visible mold violations that have not been corrected as verified by final inspection.
1812831.quote: Where the department determines that the violation has not been corrected, the department may take such enforcement action as is necessary, including performing or arranging for the performance of the work to correct the violation.

1825177.action_summary: Provide written notification of capital project change orders to council members who allocated funds for the project.
1825177.quote: the department shall provide written notification of such change order by facsimile, regular mail, electronic mail or by personal delivery to each council member, if any, who allocated funds for such capital project
1825177.deadline_text: Within 30 days after the registration of a capital project change order

1853950.action_summary: Prepare and submit an annual report to the speaker of the council and the mayor, and publish it on the mayor's office of contract services website, containing the number and total dollar value of city contracts awarded to worker cooperatives disaggregated by agency and type of business, the number and total dollar value of all city contracts disaggregated by agency and type of business, and the percentage of city contracts awarded to worker cooperatives disaggregated by agency and type of business.
1853950.quote: No later than six months after the end of each fiscal year, beginning with the 2016 fiscal year, the city chief procurement officer shall, with the cooperation of all relevant agencies, prepare and submit to the speaker of the council and the mayor, and publish on the mayor's office of contract services website, a report containing, at a minimum, the following information for such fiscal year
1853950.deadline_text: No later than six months after the end of each fiscal year, beginning with the 2016 fiscal year

1853950.action_summary: Submit an annual report to the speaker of the council and the mayor, and make it publicly available online, containing the number of worker cooperatives that applied for and received assistance from the department, the industries and community districts where they operate, and specific actions taken to assist worker cooperatives including services to enhance their ability to compete for city contracts.
1853950.quote: No later than six months after the end of each fiscal year, beginning with the 2016 fiscal year, the commissioner, in consultation with the city chief procurement officer, shall submit to the speaker of the council and the mayor, and shall make publicly available online, a report containing, at a minimum, the following information
1853950.deadline_text: No later than six months after the end of each fiscal year, beginning with the 2016 fiscal year

1853950.action_summary: For each worker cooperative assisted by the department in the previous fiscal year, furnish the name and address, the number of new worker-members, the number of non-member workers hired, and a summary of services provided by the department.
1853950.quote: for each of the worker cooperatives assisted by the department in the previous fiscal year as described in subparagraph (a) of this paragraph, the department shall furnish the name and address of such worker cooperative; the number of natural persons who became worker-members during the previous fiscal year, where made available to the department; the number of non-member workers who were hired during the previous fiscal year, where made available to the department; and a summary of the services provided by the department to such worker cooperative in the previous fiscal year
1853950.deadline_text: No later than six months after the end of each fiscal year, beginning with the 2016 fiscal year

1853950.action_summary: Submit a triennial report to the speaker of the council and the mayor, and make it publicly available online, describing difficulties or obstacles that worker cooperatives encounter when competing for city contracts, recommending measures to lessen such difficulties, and describing the impact of services provided by the department to worker cooperatives in the previous three fiscal years.
1853950.quote: No later than six months after the end of every third fiscal year, beginning with the 2016 fiscal year, the commissioner, in consultation with the city chief procurement officer, shall submit to the speaker of the council and the mayor, and shall make publicly available online, a report containing, at a minimum, the following information
1853950.deadline_text: No later than six months after the end of every third fiscal year, beginning with the 2016 fiscal year

1853950.action_summary: Submit a report to the speaker of the council and the mayor by January 1, 2016, and make it publicly available online, that includes for each entity that received funding from the department in connection with the worker cooperative business development initiative a summary of the actions taken to assist worker cooperatives development.
1853950.quote: By January 1, 2016, the commissioner, in consultation with the city chief procurement officer, shall submit to the speaker of the council and the mayor, and shall make publicly available online, a report that shall include, for each entity that received funding from the department in connection with the worker cooperative business development initiative as described in schedule C of the fiscal year 2015 adopted expense budget, a summary of the actions taken by such entity, using such funding, to assist the development of worker cooperatives, including but not limited to a description of any workshops, technical assistance or financial assistance provided

1853950.action_summary: In preparing the triennial report, consult with worker cooperatives and entities that provide advice or services for worker cooperatives located in the city to the extent feasible, and include in the report a summary of findings from such consultations.

2597317.action_summary: Forward notice of intent to designate a pedestrian plaza to affected council members, community boards, and borough presidents at least 60 days before designation.

2597317.deadline_text: No less than 60 days before designating a pedestrian plaza

2597317.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
2597317.action_summary: Consider comments submitted by council members, community boards, and borough presidents regarding proposed pedestrian plazas within 45 days of receipt of notice.
2597317.quote: Within 45 days of receipt of such notice, such council members, community boards, and borough presidents may submit comments regarding such proposed pedestrian plaza. The department shall consider such comments before making a determination
2597317.deadline_text: Within 45 days of receipt of such notice

2597317.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
2597317.action_summary: Issue a response to applications and proposals for designation of areas as pedestrian plazas within 90 days of receipt.
2597317.quote: Within 90 days of the receipt of such application, the department shall issue a response to such a proposal.
2597317.deadline_text: Within 90 days of the receipt of such application

2597317.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
2597317.action_summary: Notify affected council members, community boards, borough presidents, and pedestrian plaza partners at least 90 days before rescinding the designation of a pedestrian plaza.
2597317.quote: At least 90 days before the department rescinds the designation of a pedestrian plaza, the department shall notify the affected council members, community boards, borough presidents, and any pedestrian plaza partner.
2597317.deadline_text: At least 90 days before the department rescinds the designation of a pedestrian plaza

2597317.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation

2597317.quote: If any such council member, community board, borough president, or pedestrian plaza partner so requests, the department shall hold a public hearing on the proposed designation rescission no more than 45 days after sending such notice.
2597317.deadline_text: no more than 45 days after sending such notice

2597317.quote: In addition to uniform rules promulgated pursuant to paragraph 1 of this subdivision, the commissioner may promulgate pedestrian plaza-specific rules to regulate the use of, and activities within, an individual pedestrian plaza and sidewalks directly adjacent to such pedestrian plaza.

2599062.action_summary: Promulgate rules defining critical infrastructure and establishing the procedures for notification and permitting of soil and foundation work.
2599062.quote: Within 10 business days of receiving such notification, the department shall determine whether the location of such activity is in close proximity to critical infrastructure, as defined in rules promulgated by the department

2599062.action_summary: Determine within 10 business days of receiving notification whether a proposed soil or foundation work location is in close proximity to critical infrastructure and notify the applicant of the determination.
2599062.quote: Within 10 business days of receiving such notification, the department shall determine whether the location of such activity is in close proximity to critical infrastructure, as defined in rules promulgated by the department, and notify the owner of the premises, engineer, architect or contractor of such determination.
2599062.deadline_text: Within 10 business days of receiving such notification

2599062.action_summary: Post stop work orders at the site and serve them personally or by mail to the owner, developer, or person executing the work.
2599062.quote: Such order shall be posted at the site of the soil or foundation work and served personally on or mailed to the owner or developer or to the person executing the work at the site or the agent of any of them.

2599062.action_summary: Rescind a stop work order upon application and finding that the condition giving rise to the order has been corrected and penalties paid or secured, or that the order was issued in error.
2599062.quote: Upon application in accordance with the rules of the department, the commissioner shall rescind the stop work order where the commissioner finds (i) that the condition that gave rise to its issuance has been corrected and either all civil penalties or criminal fines assessed for any violation of such order have been paid or, where a violation is pending, security for the payment of such penalties or fines has been posted or, (ii) where the stop work order was issued in error or conditions are such that the order should not have been issued.

2599062.action_summary: Issue a stop work order whenever the department finds that soil or foundation work violates this section or rules and creates a danger to critical infrastructure.
2599062.quote: The department may issue a stop work order whenever the department finds that any soil or foundation work in violation of this section or any rules promulgated thereunder creates a danger to critical infrastructure.

2599062.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing procedures for rescinding stop work orders and authorizing fees for inspection and administrative expenses related to stop work orders.
2599062.quote: The commissioner may by rule require the payment of a fee in the amount of the expense of additional inspection and administrative expense related to such stop work order.
