2735148.action_summary: Create a medical treatment report whenever an arrestee is treated by a health care provider while in custody, including the arrestee's medical condition, name, identifying information, and provider identity.
2735148.quote: Whenever an arrestee is treated by a health care provider while in the custody of the department, the department shall create a report. Such report shall include a brief description of the arrestee's medical condition, to the extent known by the department, the arrestee's name and other identifying information regarding that arrestee, including but not limited to the arrestee's New York state identification number and date of birth, when available, and identity of the health care provider.

2735148.action_summary: Transmit medical treatment reports to the department of health and mental hygiene or its designee whenever an arrestee is taken into the custody of the department of correction.
2735148.quote: Such report shall be transmitted to the department of health and mental hygiene or its designee whenever an arrestee is taken into the custody of the department of correction.

2735148.action_summary: Oversee screening of every arrestee held at the central booking area of a local criminal court prior to arraignment for medical or mental health conditions that may require immediate attention.
2735148.quote: Every arrestee held at the central booking area of a local criminal court prior to their arraignment at such court shall be screened for medical or mental health conditions that may require immediate attention. The department or its designee shall oversee such screening.

2735148.action_summary: Establish procedures to make available medical treatment reports received from the New York city police department to any health care provider in a department of correction facility conducting a health evaluation at the time such evaluation is conducted.
2735148.quote: The department or its designee shall establish procedures to make available reports received from the New York city police department pursuant to section 14-163 to any health care provider in a department of correction facility conducting a health evaluation, at such time as a health evaluation is conducted.

2735148.action_summary: Establish procedures to obtain the pre-arraignment screening record and any medical records created by hospitals in connection with treatment of an arrestee who subsequently enters the custody of the department of correction, at the request of any health care provider conducting a health evaluation.
2735148.quote: The department or its designee shall establish procedures to obtain the pre-arraignment screening record created pursuant to section 17-1802 and any medical records created and maintained by any hospital in connection with treatment provided to an arrestee who subsequently enters the custody of the department of correction, at the request of any health care provider conducting a health evaluation of such inmate.

2735475.action_summary: Review requests for modification or removal of deed restrictions in accordance with the procedures set forth in the chapter.
2735475.quote: A request for modification or removal of a deed restriction submitted to the department shall be reviewed in accordance with the procedures set forth in this chapter.

2735475.action_summary: Obtain mayoral approval before modifying or removing any deed restriction.
2735475.quote: The department shall not modify or remove any deed restriction without the approval of the mayor, or the mayor's designee, pursuant to section 3-119.

2735475.action_summary: Conduct a preliminary review of requests for modification or removal of deed restrictions following submission of an intake package.
2735475.quote: Following the submission of an intake package pursuant to subdivision a of section 25-803, the department shall conduct a preliminary review of a request that the department modify or remove a deed restriction.

2735475.action_summary: Notify property owners in writing that their request for modification or removal is under review upon receipt of the intake package.
2735475.quote: Upon receipt of the intake package required pursuant to subdivision a of section 25-803, the department shall notify the property owner in writing that the request for modification or removal is under review.

2735475.action_summary: Send notice of review along with the intake package to the community board, council member, and borough president at the time the property owner is notified.
2735475.quote: At the time the property owner is notified in writing that the request for modification or removal is under review pursuant to paragraph 1 of this subdivision, the department shall send notice of such review, along with the intake package for such request submitted pursuant to subdivision a of section 25-803, by mail and electronic mail to the community board for the community district in which the property is located, council member representing the council district in which the property is located, and borough president representing the borough in which the property is located.

2735475.action_summary: Perform a land use analysis including history of property use, deed restriction description, land use implications, and analysis of whether modification or removal furthers the best interests of the city.
2735475.quote: The department shall perform a land use analysis, which shall include a description of the history of the use of the property, the deed restriction that is the subject of the request, the land use implications of such deed restriction, and an analysis of whether such modification or removal furthers the best interests of the city pursuant to the factors set forth in subdivision a of section 25-802.

2735475.action_summary: Assist the department of citywide administrative services in land use analysis by providing information concerning zoning, land use, urban design, public transit access, land use policies and initiatives, and prior land use actions.
2735475.quote: The department of city planning shall assist the department in such analysis by providing information concerning the zoning and land use of the property and surrounding area, including urban design characteristics, public transit access, any existing and planned land use policies and initiatives, and any prior land use actions affecting the property.

2735475.action_summary: Inform the property owner, community board, council member, and borough president if the department determines that the proposed modification or removal does not further the best interests of the city and take no further action.
2735475.quote: if the department determines that such modification or removal does not further the best interests of the city, the department shall take no further action on such request and shall inform the property owner, community board for the community district in which the property is located, council member representing the council district in which the property is located, and borough president representing the borough in which the property is located of such determination.

2735475.action_summary: Conduct a due diligence review to determine whether there are outstanding obligations owed to the city by the property owner or proposed property owner.
2735475.quote: The department shall conduct a due diligence review to determine whether there are outstanding obligations owed to the city in connection with the properties identified in the VSTA forms, or by the current property owner or any proposed property owner, which shall include but not be limited to review of the following information related to such properties, current property owner, or any proposed property owner

2735475.action_summary: Appraise the market value of the property with and without the deed restriction based on two appraisals, at least one by an independent licensed appraiser.
2735475.quote: The department shall appraise the market value of the property with and without the deed restriction based on two appraisals, at least one of which must be performed by an independent real estate appraiser licensed in the state who is not an employee of the department.
2735475.deadline_text: within 60 days prior to the date the department submits its preliminary recommendation to the committee

2735475.action_summary: Determine the method of calculation of any consideration to be proposed for the modification or removal of a deed restriction, in consultation with relevant city agencies and the law department.
2735475.quote: The method of calculation of any consideration to be proposed in connection with the modification or removal of the deed restriction shall be determined by the department in consultation with relevant city agencies and experts, including, but not limited to, the law department.

2735475.action_summary: Propose a consideration amount, if any, required for modification or removal of the deed restriction based on appraisals and calculation method, including reasoning for the proposed amount.
2735475.quote: Based on the appraisals and in accordance with the calculation method determined pursuant to paragraph 3 of this subdivision, the department shall propose a consideration amount, if any, that would be required for the modification or removal of the deed restriction, and shall include the department's reasoning for proposing such consideration amount.

2735475.action_summary: Prepare a written summary of reasons if the department determines that an appraisal is not required pursuant to specified exemptions.
2735475.quote: If the department determines that an appraisal is not required pursuant to paragraph 5 of this subdivision, the department shall prepare a written summary of its reasons for reaching such determination.

2735475.action_summary: Consult with other city, state, or federal agencies including the department of housing preservation and development, department of city planning, department of small business services, and any agency involved in providing services at the property.
2735475.quote: Following the preliminary review and performance of any appraisals, the department shall consult with other city, state, or federal agencies as appropriate, including, but not limited to, the department of housing preservation and development, the department of city planning, the department of small business services, and any agency involved in providing services at the property

2735475.action_summary: Prepare a summary of findings based on the land use analysis, due diligence review, agency consultation, and appraisal determinations.
2735475.quote: Following such consultation, the department shall prepare a summary of findings based on the land use analysis, due diligence review, consultation conducted pursuant to this section, and, if applicable, its determination pursuant to paragraph 4 or 6 of subdivision b of this section.

2735475.action_summary: Post online and send notice of the proposed modification or removal to the community board, council member, and borough president no later than three business days after the summary is completed and at least 60 days prior to any modification or removal.
2735475.quote: No later than three business days after such summary is completed and at least 60 days prior to any modification or removal of such deed restriction, the department shall post online and send notice of the proposed modification or removal as set forth in this paragraph. Such notice shall identify the property by its address and any commonly known name and include the summary prepared pursuant to paragraph 2 of this subdivision and shall be sent by mail and electronic mail to the community board for the community district in which the property is located, council member representing the council district in which the property is located, and borough president representing the borough in which the property is located.
2735475.deadline_text: No later than three business days after such summary is completed and at least 60 days prior to any modification or removal

2735475.action_summary: Establish a process in consultation with the law department for determining whether a proposed modification or removal is subject to the uniform land use review procedure.
2735475.quote: The department, in consultation with the law department, shall establish a process for determining whether a proposed modification or removal is subject to the uniform land use review procedure set forth in section 197-c of the charter.

2735475.action_summary: Prepare an application for modification or removal to be reviewed pursuant to the uniform land use review procedure if the department determines the request is subject to such procedure.
2735475.quote: If, pursuant to such process, the department determines that a proposed modification or removal is subject to the uniform land use review procedure set forth in section 197-c of the charter, the department shall prepare an application for such modification or removal to be reviewed pursuant to such procedure.

2735475.action_summary: Conduct at least one public hearing on the requested modification or removal at least 45 days but no more than 120 days prior to such removal or modification.
2735475.quote: The department shall conduct at least one public hearing on such requested modification or removal pursuant to the procedures set forth in this subdivision. A public hearing shall occur at least 45 days but no more than 120 days prior to such removal or modification.
2735475.deadline_text: A public hearing shall occur at least 45 days but no more than 120 days prior to such removal or modification

2735475.action_summary: Publish a public notice of any hearing online and in the city record for at least seven consecutive business days commencing at least 30 days and no more than 40 days before any hearing.
2735475.quote: The department shall publish a public notice of any hearing online and in the city record for at least seven consecutive business days commencing at least 30 days and no more than 40 days before any such hearing.
2735475.deadline_text: for at least seven consecutive business days commencing at least 30 days and no more than 40 days before any such hearing

2735475.action_summary: Send notice of any hearing by mail and electronic mail to the community board, council member, and borough president.
2735475.quote: The department shall send notice of any hearing by mail and electronic mail to the community board for the community district in which the property is located, council member representing the council district in which the property is located, and borough president representing the borough in which the property is located.

2735475.action_summary: Hold any public hearing in the community district in which the property is located.
2735475.quote: Any public hearing shall be held in the community district in which the property is located.

2735475.action_summary: Post online and send to the community board, council member, and borough president a public file containing copies of calendar documents and public documents including the summary no later than 20 days before any hearing.
2735475.quote: A public file containing copies of the calendar document and other public documents, including the summary prepared pursuant to paragraph 2 of subdivision c of this section, shall be posted online and sent to the community board for the community district in which the property is located, council member representing the council district in which the property is located, and borough president representing the borough in which the property is located no later than 20 days before any hearing.
2735475.deadline_text: no later than 20 days before any hearing

2735475.action_summary: Prepare and post online a summary of public comments received at any hearing along with responses to such comments.
2735475.quote: The department shall prepare and post online a summary of public comments received at any such hearing, along with responses to such comments, on the request for modification or removal of the deed restriction.

2735475.action_summary: Submit a preliminary recommendation to approve the request to the committee established pursuant to section 3-119 if the department finds the modification or removal is appropriate and furthers the best interests of the city.
2735475.quote: If, based on the information obtained pursuant to this section, the department finds that the requested modification or removal of a deed restriction is appropriate and furthers the best interests of the city, the department shall submit a preliminary recommendation to approve the request to the committee established pursuant to section 3-119.

2735475.action_summary: Issue a letter to the property owner within three business days of committee approval setting forth the recommendation, required consideration, and further actions needed to obtain the requested modification or removal.
2735475.quote: If the committee approves the department's preliminary recommendation, within three business days of such approval, the department shall issue a letter to the property owner setting forth such recommendation; any required consideration, as approved or modified by the committee; and any further actions the property owner must take to obtain the requested modification or removal of the deed restriction
2735475.deadline_text: within three business days of such approval

2735475.action_summary: Cease further action if the property owner does not respond within 30 calendar days after receipt of the letter, and treat failure to respond within 60 days as a new request.
2735475.quote: If the property owner does not respond to such letter within 30 calendar days after the receipt of such letter, the department shall cease any further action with regard to the requested modification or removal until a response is received; provided, however, if a property owner fails to respond or fails to request more time to respond within 60 days following receipt of such letter, the department shall treat such response as a new request.
2735475.deadline_text: within 30 calendar days after the receipt of such letter

2735475.action_summary: Submit to the mayor a final written recommendation for approval including the intake package, appraisals, summaries, public comments, agreements, and other relevant documents if the department determines the modification or removal is appropriate and furthers the best interests of the city.
2735475.quote: If the department determines that such modification or removal is appropriate and furthers the best interests of the city, it shall submit to the mayor a final written recommendation for approval of such request. Such written recommendation shall include the intake package submitted pursuant to subdivision a of section 25-803, any appraisals conducted pursuant to subdivision b of section 25-804, the summary prepared pursuant to paragraph 2 of subdivision c of section 25-804, the summary of public comments prepared pursuant to paragraph 6 of subdivision e of section 25-804, any and all agreements with the property owner pursuant to paragraph 2 of subdivision f of section 25-804, and any other documents or information the department deems relevant.

2939936.action_summary: Establish by rule a program for reducing the amount of any fee or civil penalty for a violation, other than an immediately hazardous violation, where a person has paid for or arranged for workers to obtain construction site safety training required by section 3321 of the New York city building code.
2939936.quote: The commissioner shall establish by rule a program for reducing the amount of any fee to be imposed upon a person or any civil penalty to be imposed upon a person for a violation, other than an immediately hazardous violation, where one or more of the following conditions is satisfied

The commissioner shall issue a notice of violation to the owner of such site, each permit holder responsible for ensuring that such worker complies with such section at such site and the person who employed or otherwise engaged such worker at such site if such person can reasonably be identified.

2939936.action_summary: Conduct at least one unannounced inspection of a building site at least once every three months to determine compliance with section 3321 of the New York city building code following a finding of a second or subsequent violation at such site, continuing until at least two consecutive inspections do not result in issuance of a notice of violation.
2939936.quote: Upon a finding by the office of administrative trials and hearings, acting pursuant to section 1049-a of the New York city charter, or a court of competent jurisdiction that a second or subsequent violation of section 3321 of the New York city building code has occurred at a building site, the commissioner shall conduct at least one unannounced inspection of such site at least once every three months to determine compliance with such section.

2939936.action_summary: Conduct at least one unannounced inspection of each building site owned, worked at, or employing workers for a person found to have committed a second or subsequent violation of section 3321 of the New York city building code.
2939936.quote: Upon a finding by the office of administrative trials and hearings, acting pursuant to section 1049-a of the New York city charter, or a court of competent jurisdiction that the owner of a building site, a permit holder at such site or a person employing or otherwise engaging workers at such site has violated section 3321 of the New York city building code and such violation is a second or subsequent violation of such section by such owner, permit holder or person, the commissioner shall conduct at least one unannounced inspection of (i) each building site owned by such owner, if such violation is a second or subsequent violation by such owner, (ii) each building site where such permit holder works, if such violation is a second or subsequent violation by such permit holder and (iii) each building site where such person works, if such violation is a second or subsequent violation by such person.

3509899.action_summary: Review incident data to assess and improve effectiveness of sexual abuse and sexual harassment prevention, detection, and response policies, practices, and training, and provide a semiannual assessment report to the council on findings and corrective actions.

3509899.deadline_text: within 90 days following the end of each reporting period starting on July 1, 2019 and every six months thereafter

3509899.action_summary: Ensure that all data collected pursuant to this section is securely retained and retain such data indefinitely after the date of initial collection unless federal or state law requires otherwise.

3509899.action_summary: Before making data collected pursuant to this section available to the speaker of the council, board of correction, and the public, remove an individual's name, all personal identifying information as defined by section 10-501, and any other information the disclosure of which would violate any federal or state laws.
3509899.quote: Before making data collected pursuant to this section available to the speaker of the council, board of correction, and the public, the department shall remove an individual's name, all personal identifying information as defined by subdivision (a) of section 10-501, and any other information the disclosure of which would violate any federal or state laws.

3509926.action_summary: Provide eligible incarcerated individuals with written information about bail amount, identification number, payment options and locations, and other relevant bail-posting assistance information within 24 hours of custody.
3509926.quote: Within 24 hours of taking custody of an eligible incarcerated individual, the department shall provide to such individual the following information in written form: (i) the individual's amount of bail or bond, (ii) the individual's New York state identification number or booking and case number or other unique identifying number, (iii) options for all forms of bail payment and all steps required for such payment, including the locations at which a surety may post bail and the requirements for so posting, and (iv) any other information relevant to assisting the individual in posting bail or bond.
3509926.deadline_text: Within 24 hours of taking custody of an eligible incarcerated individual
affected_groups: incarcerated individuals held on bail or bond

3509926.action_summary: Notify eligible incarcerated individuals that they may post their own bail within 24 hours of custody.
3509926.quote: Within 24 hours of taking custody of eligible incarcerated individuals, the department shall notify such individuals that they may post their own bail.
3509926.deadline_text: Within 24 hours of taking custody of eligible incarcerated individuals
affected_groups: incarcerated individuals held on bail or bond

3509926.action_summary: Offer eligible incarcerated individuals the opportunity to obtain personal property stored by the department, including contact information and financial resources, to facilitate bail posting within 24 hours of custody.
3509926.quote: Within such time period, the department shall, to the extent practicable and in a manner consistent with officer safety and all applicable laws, offer such individuals the opportunity to obtain property, including personal contact information and financial resources, that such individuals may require for the purpose of posting bail
3509926.deadline_text: Within 24 hours of taking custody of eligible incarcerated individuals
affected_groups: incarcerated individuals held on bail or bond

3509926.action_summary: Ensure bail facilitators meet with all eligible incarcerated individuals within 48 hours of admission, provide continued access to bail facilitators, and furnish bail facilitators with reasonable resources to fulfill their duties.
3509926.quote: The department shall ensure that bail facilitators meet with all eligible incarcerated individuals within 48 hours of their admission to the custody of the department, that eligible incarcerated individuals have continued access to bail facilitators, and that bail facilitators are provided with reasonable resources necessary to fulfill their duties.
3509926.deadline_text: within 48 hours of their admission to the custody of the department
affected_groups: incarcerated individuals held on bail or bond

3509926.action_summary: Generate twice daily a list of eligible incarcerated individuals held solely due to bail amounts less than $10 and provide notice to each such individual within 24 hours of receiving bail status information from the office of court administration.
3509926.quote: the department shall generate a list of eligible incarcerated individuals who are held solely due to a bail amount of less than $10 once before noon and once after noon every day of the week. Within three hours of generation of such a list, but no later than 24 hours after receipt of information from the office of court administration regarding the bail status of eligible incarcerated individuals, the department shall provide each eligible incarcerated individual who is held solely due to a bail amount of less than $10 with notice that such eligible incarcerated individual is held solely due to a bail amount of less than $10.
3509926.deadline_text: Within three hours of generation of such a list, but no later than 24 hours after receipt of information from the office of court administration
affected_groups: incarcerated individuals held on bail less than $10

3509926.action_summary: Consult a New York state unified court system website within 90 minutes of list generation to identify legal representatives and contact information for eligible incarcerated individuals held solely due to bail amounts less than $10.
3509926.quote: Within ninety minutes of generation of such a list, the department shall consult a website maintained by the New York state unified court system that may contain information relating to such individual's legal representative.
3509926.deadline_text: Within ninety minutes of generation of such a list
affected_groups: incarcerated individuals held on bail less than $10

3509926.action_summary: Telephone legal representatives identified on the New York state unified court system website within 90 minutes of list generation to inform them that their client is held solely due to a bail amount less than $10.
3509926.quote: If such website identifies the legal representative of such individual and contains a telephone number for such legal representative, the department shall telephone such legal representative to inform them that such individual is held solely due to a bail amount of less than $10.
3509926.deadline_text: Within ninety minutes of generation of such a list
affected_groups: legal representatives of incarcerated individuals held on bail less than $10

3509926.action_summary: Telephone or email institutional defense providers within 90 minutes of list generation to inform them that their client is held solely due to a bail amount less than $10.
3509926.quote: If such website identifies an institutional defense provider as the legal representative of such individual, the department shall telephone or email such institutional defense provider within ninety minutes of generation of such a list to inform them that such individual is held solely due to a bail amount of less than $10, regardless of whether a telephone number or email address is identified on a website maintained by the New York state unified court system.
3509926.deadline_text: within ninety minutes of generation of such a list
affected_groups: incarcerated individuals held on bail less than $10

3521915.action_summary: After opportunity for a hearing, exclude, suspend, or otherwise condition the participation of registered design professionals who knowingly or negligently submit false or non-compliant professionally certified applications or submit two such applications within 12 months containing errors resulting in permit revocation or demonstrating incompetence.
3521915.quote: The commissioner shall, after the opportunity for a hearing before the office of administrative trials and hearings in accordance with department rules, exclude, suspend, or otherwise condition the participation of a registered design professional

3521915.quote: The department shall create and maintain a database of all registered design professionals who have been excluded, suspended or otherwise sanctioned by the department.

parents and guardians of students on special education school bus routes

3704327.action_summary: No later than January 31, 2020 and every January 31 thereafter, submit to the speaker of the council a report on the usage of installment agreements in the prior calendar year, including data on new agreements executed, agreements in effect, application approvals, agreement types, default rates, terminations, renewals, and liens exceeding net equity thresholds.
3704327.quote: No later than January 31, 2020 and every January 31 thereafter, the department shall submit to the speaker of the council a report on the usage of the installment agreements set forth in this section in the prior calendar year, including, but not limited to the following data, disaggregated by installment agreement type

3704327.action_summary: Publicize the availability of the installment agreements so as to maximize public awareness of such agreements.

3704327.action_summary: After a property owner fails to make a payment pursuant to an installment agreement, mail a letter or send an email to the property owner stating that such owner is at risk of being in default, to be sent after the first missed payment if payment has not been received within two weeks of the due date.

3704327.action_summary: Pay the cost of a title search upfront when an installment agreement applicant elects to roll that cost into the agreement, and recover it through the agreement.

3704342.action_summary: Prepare and submit an annual report to the mayor and speaker of the council on the activities of the office and recommendations developed by the director.

3704342.action_summary: Submit to the council and post to the office's website in machine readable format a report on multi-agency response to community hotspots operations containing specified data elements.
3704342.quote: The office shall submit to the council and post to the office's website, in a machine readable format, a report on multi-agency response to community hotspots operations

3704342.action_summary: Provide written notice to establishments at least 30 days prior to commencing a multi-agency response to community hotspots operation, containing information about alleged conduct or complaints and providing a means for the establishment owner to provide relevant information.
3704342.quote: Before an establishment becomes the subject of a multi-agency response to community hotspots operation, as defined in subdivision e of section 20-d of the charter, the department shall provide written notice to such an establishment at least 30 days prior to commencing such an operation

3762647.action_summary: Send an annual notification to registered design professionals currently participating in the program notifying them of the grounds upon which they may be excluded, suspended or otherwise sanctioned.
3762647.quote: The commissioner shall send an annual notification to registered design professionals who are currently participating in this program notifying them, in a manner to be determined by the commissioner, of the grounds upon which they may be excluded, suspended or otherwise sanctioned.

3762647.action_summary: After opportunity for a hearing, exclude, suspend or otherwise condition the participation of a registered design professional who knowingly or negligently submits a professionally certified application containing false information or non-compliance, or submits two non-compliant applications within 12 months, or knowingly directs another professional to submit false information.
3762647.quote: The commissioner shall, after the opportunity for a hearing before the office of administrative trials and hearings in accordance with department rules, exclude, suspend or otherwise condition the participation of a registered design professional who (i) knowingly or negligently submits a professional certification of an application and/or construction and other related document that contains false information or is not in compliance with all applicable provisions of law, (ii) submits two professionally certified applications for construction document approval within any 12-month period containing errors that result in revocation of an associated permit or that otherwise demonstrate incompetence or a lack of knowledge of applicable laws, or (iii) knowingly orders or directs another registered design professional to submit a professional certification of an application and/or construction and any other related document that contains false information or is not in compliance with all applicable provisions of law or that otherwise demonstrates incompetence or a lack of knowledge of applicable laws, or with knowledge of such specific conduct, ratifies or assents to such conduct or with knowledge of such specific conduct and while acting as a supervisor otherwise fails to prevent it.

3762647.action_summary: Permanently revoke, without opportunity of restoration, the professional certification privileges of an engineer or architect who, while on probation, professionally certifies an application or document containing false information or non-compliance.
3762647.quote: The commissioner (i) shall permanently revoke, without the opportunity of restoration, the professional certification privileges of an engineer or architect who, while on probation, professionally certifies an application, plans, construction or other related document that contains false information or is not in compliance with all applicable provisions of law or who otherwise demonstrates incompetence or a lack of knowledge of applicable laws

3762647.action_summary: Create and maintain a database of all registered design professionals who have been excluded, suspended or otherwise sanctioned, including their names, firms of employment or affiliation, and sanction status.
3762647.quote: The department shall create and maintain a database of all registered design professionals who have been excluded, suspended or otherwise sanctioned by the department, all current firms of employment or affiliation of such professionals, if known or readily ascertainable, and the firm that employed such professionals, or with which such professional was affiliated, at the time such professionals were sanctioned, and the status of such sanction or sanctions.

3762647.action_summary: Within 7 business days of imposing a sanction, post on its website in a non-proprietary machine-readable format the name of the sanctioned professional, firm, sanction description, dates, premises address, and whether imposed after hearing or settlement.
3762647.quote: Within 7 business days of the date a sanction is imposed, the department shall post on its website, in a non-proprietary machine-readable format that permits automated processing, and shall make available upon request, the name of the registered design professional and the firm that employed such professionals, or with which such professionals were affiliated, at the time such professionals were sanctioned, and a description of the sanction, the initial date of the sanction, the reinstatement date, if applicable, the address of the premises for which the application associated with the sanction was submitted, and whether the sanction was imposed after a hearing or a settlement.
3762647.deadline_text: Within 7 business days of the date a sanction is imposed

3762647.action_summary: Provide requested information concerning the exclusion, suspension or other sanction of a specific registered design professional and their firm of employment within 30 days of such request.
3762647.quote: The department shall provide requested information concerning the exclusion, suspension or other sanction of a specific registered design professional and the firm of employment of such professionals, or the firm with which such professionals were affiliated, when such professionals were sanctioned, within 30 days of such request.

3835708.action_summary: Utilize an electronic tracking system to record all grievable and non-grievable complaints handled by the office of constituent and grievance services and provide the board of correction access to such system.
3835708.quote: The department shall utilize an electronic tracking system to record all grievable and non-grievable complaints handled by the office of constituent and grievance services and shall provide the board of correction access to such system.

3835708.action_summary: Ensure equal access to the office of constituent and grievance services by evaluating the need for and strategically placing grievance boxes in facilities, placing dedicated personnel in each housing unit to conduct outreach, and developing caseload guidelines for grievance coordinators and officers.
3835708.quote: The department shall ensure equal access to the office of constituent and grievance services, including the following procedures: 1. Evaluating the need for grievance boxes and strategically placing a number of boxes in locations where individuals in department custody frequently congregate, and at least one box in each facility. 2. Placing a number of dedicated personnel in each housing unit to conduct outreach. 3. Developing caseload guidelines for grievance coordinators and officers.

3835708.action_summary: Install grievance kiosks in each facility where incarcerated individuals may file grievances electronically, with accessibility in multiple languages, physical receipts, and information about redirecting non-grievable requests.
3835708.quote: The department shall install grievance kiosks in each facility where incarcerated individuals may file grievances electronically by January 2026. Such kiosks shall be accessible in multiple languages and shall provide incarcerated individuals physical receipts confirming filing.

3835708.action_summary: Provide assistance to incarcerated individuals unable to read, access, or understand the grievance process to enable them to meaningfully engage in such process.
3835708.quote: Incarcerated individuals unable to read, access, or understand the grievance process shall be provided with assistance necessary to meaningfully engage in such process.

3860318.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3860318.action_summary: Determine the state-of-the-art thermometer specifications for measuring air temperature and the state-of-the-art hygrometer or equivalent device specifications for measuring relative humidity.
3860318.quote: air temperatures shall be those measured by a state-of-the-art thermometer, as determined by the commissioner. Relative humidity shall be determined by a state-of-the-art hygrometer or any other device having the same capability to measure relative humidity, as determined by the commissioner.
3860318.deadline_text: before such date [60 days after the local law becomes law]

3860318.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3860318.action_summary: Measure air temperatures and relative humidity at street level at one of the stands designated pursuant to section 19-174, or authorize a designee to do so.
3860318.quote: Air temperatures and relative humidity shall be measured by the commissioner or the commissioner's designee at street level at one of the stands designated pursuant to section 19-174 of the code.

3860318.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3860318.action_summary: Promulgate rules as necessary for the implementation of this local law concerning carriage horse work restrictions and enforcement procedures.
3860318.quote: the commissioner shall take such measures as are necessary for the implementation of this local law, including the promulgation of rules, before such date.
3860318.deadline_text: before such date [60 days after the local law becomes law]

3860342.action_summary: Evaluate no fewer than 25 blocks or intersections experiencing improper use of parking permits and no fewer than 25 blocks or intersections experiencing obstruction of bicycle lanes, bus lanes, sidewalks, crosswalks, and fire hydrants by vehicles each week for six months beginning no later than January 1, 2020.
3860342.quote: the police department shall, each week, evaluate no fewer than 25 blocks or intersections that are experiencing a prevalence of improper use of parking permits, and no fewer than 25 blocks or intersections that are experiencing obstruction of bicycle lanes, bus lanes, sidewalks, crosswalks, and fire hydrants by vehicles.

3860342.action_summary: Conduct detailed evaluations of selected blocks or intersections including descriptions, complaint and summons counts, violation timing, photographs of parked vehicles, parking permit photographs, license plate photographs, and enforcement action summaries.
3860342.quote: Each evaluation conducted pursuant to this section shall include a description of each such block or intersection and why it was selected for evaluation; the number of complaints, summonses, traffic crashes, and moving violations associated with such block or intersection; the times at which such violations historically occur; photographs of all vehicles parked in such location demonstrating vehicles parked both legally and illegally; and for any vehicle parked illegally, a photograph of any city-issued parking permit or other parking permit displayed in each such vehicle, a photograph of the license plate of each such vehicle, and a summary of enforcement actions taken regarding each such vehicle and, if an enforcement action is not taken regarding each such vehicle, the reasons why.

3860342.action_summary: Submit a monthly report to the department of investigation, the mayor, and the speaker of the council identifying evaluated blocks or intersections, analyses, determinations, and the department's response including actions taken.
3860342.quote: No later than 30 days following the end of each month in which the police department conducts evaluations pursuant to subdivision a of this section, the police department shall submit a report identifying the blocks or intersections evaluated, the analyses and determinations made pursuant to paragraph 2 of subdivision a of this section, the department's response to such evaluation, including actions taken, if any.
3860342.deadline_text: No later than 30 days following the end of each month in which the police department conducts evaluations pursuant to subdivision a of this section

3860342.action_summary: Conduct an investigation and issue a report regarding the issuance of parking permits and enforcement of parking laws, including analysis of police department reports, patterns and trends in enforcement and permit use, and recommendations.
3860342.quote: The department of investigation shall conduct an investigation and issue a report regarding the issuance of parking permits and enforcement of parking laws. No later than September 30, 2020, the department of investigation shall submit such report to the police department, the department of transportation, the mayor, and the speaker of the council and post such report on its website.

3860342.action_summary: Post the parking permits and enforcement of parking laws report on its website.
3860342.quote: the department of investigation shall submit such report to the police department, the department of transportation, the mayor, and the speaker of the council and post such report on its website.

3913893.deadline_text: no later than January 30 and July 30 of each year beginning in 2020

3927503.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website an annual report on the demographics of school staff disaggregated by school, staff category, gender, race or ethnicity, length of employment, and years of experience, with aggregated data by community school district and borough.
3927503.quote: the department shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a report for the previous school year including the following for each school

3927505.action_summary: Establish a working group for every community school district to develop recommendations and a plan to foster and increase school diversity.
3927505.quote: The mayor shall establish a working group, for every community school district, to develop recommendations and a plan to foster and increase school diversity, according to the timeframe set forth in subdivision k of this local law.
3927505.deadline_text: No later than 5 years after the effective date of this local law

3927505.action_summary: Appoint members to each working group, including teachers, principals, parents, students, community district education council representatives, and the superintendent or designee.
3927505.quote: Members of each working group shall be appointed by the mayor, and shall include teachers from elementary and middle schools from the respective community school district who are currently employed by the department; principals from such district who are currently employed by the department; parents of students attending public schools in such district; students currently enrolled in public middle schools in such district; at least one representative of the community district education council within such district and the superintendent, or superintendent's designee, with jurisdiction over such district.
3927505.deadline_text: No later than 5 years after the effective date of this local law

3927505.action_summary: Appoint a department representative to serve as a co-facilitator for each working group.
3927505.quote: For each working group, the mayor shall appoint a department representative to serve as a co-facilitator.
3927505.deadline_text: No later than 5 years after the effective date of this local law

3927505.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
3927505.action_summary: Hold at least one public hearing to solicit public comment and recommendations on improving diversity in schools within the respective community school district.
3927505.quote: No later than 3 months after the establishment of each working group, such working group shall be required to hold at least 1 public hearing to solicit public comment and recommendations on improving diversity in schools within the respective community school district.
3927505.deadline_text: No later than 3 months after the establishment of each working group

3927505.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
3927505.action_summary: Create a website to solicit public comment and recommendations on improving school diversity.
3927505.quote: Each working group shall also create a website to solicit public comment and recommendations.
3927505.deadline_text: No later than 3 months after the establishment of each working group

3927505.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
3927505.action_summary: Examine school diversity issues in the respective community school district and develop recommendations and a plan to foster and increase school diversity, including examination of admissions policies, transfer trends, language access, gifted and talented programs, screened programs, and student transportation.
3927505.quote: Each working group shall examine the issue of school diversity in its respective community school district and develop recommendations and a plan to foster and increase school diversity. Areas to be examined shall include, but are not limited to: admissions policies, transfer trends, language access, gifted and talented programs, screened programs and student transportation.
3927505.deadline_text: No later than 2 years after the establishment of a working group

3927505.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
3927505.action_summary: Submit a report of findings, recommendations, and plan to the mayor, chancellor of the city school district, and the speaker of the council, including cost estimates and an explanation if a community-based organization co-facilitator was not selected.
3927505.quote: No later than 2 years after the establishment of a working group, such working group shall submit a report of its findings, recommendations and plan required pursuant to subdivision i of this local law to the mayor, chancellor of the city school district of the city of New York and the speaker of the council. Such report shall also include (i) an estimate of costs associated with implementation of such plan and (ii) if such working group chose not to have a community based organization co-facilitate pursuant to subdivision d of this local law, an explanation why a co-facilitator was not necessary.
3927505.deadline_text: No later than 2 years after the establishment of a working group

3927505.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council a report on the activities and recommendations of working groups that were not required to be established due to prior diversity planning or engagement.
3927505.quote: No later than 2 years after the effective date of this local law, the mayor shall submit to the speaker of the council a report on the activities and recommendations of such working groups.
3927505.deadline_text: No later than 2 years after the effective date of this local law

3927505.action_summary: Post all reports required by this local law on the department's website.
3927505.quote: All reports required by this local law shall be posted on the department's website.

3927505.action_summary: Establish a list of community-based organizations that each working group may select to serve as a co-facilitator.
3927505.quote: Each working group may, at such working group's discretion, select a community based organization, from a list established by the mayor, to serve as a co-facilitator.
3927505.deadline_text: No later than 5 years after the effective date of this local law

4770945.action_summary: Define what constitutes a severe act of bias and, in consultation with covered entities, what constitutes a covered entity's final determination of an act of bias or severe act of bias.
4770945.citation: Section 3, § 441(b)(2) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: For the purposes of initiating such investigations, the board shall define what constitutes a severe act of bias and, in consultation with each covered entity, what constitutes a covered entity's final determination

4770945.action_summary: Communicate definitions of severe acts of bias and final determinations to each covered entity and make such definitions publicly available online within 10 days after making or changing them.
4770945.citation: Section 3, § 441(b)(3) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: Within 10 days after making or changing a definition made pursuant to paragraph 2 of this subdivision, the board shall communicate such definition or change to each covered entity and shall make such definition or change publicly available online.
4770945.deadline_text: Within 10 days after making or changing a definition

4770945.action_summary: Conduct investigations of past conduct by current or former police department members whom a covered entity has found, in a final determination, to have engaged in a severe act of bias, regardless of duty status, if the investigation date is less than five years after the final determination.
4770945.citation: Section 3, § 441(b)(1)(i) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: the board: (i) shall conduct an investigation of past conduct in the course of performance of official duties by a current or former member of the police department whom a covered entity has found, in a final determination reached after such member was afforded an opportunity to respond to the relevant allegations, to have engaged in a severe act of bias

4770945.action_summary: Obtain from each covered entity that is an agency a written list of members found to have engaged in acts of bias or severe acts of bias before the effective date and on or after January 1, 2016, to the extent practicable.
4770945.citation: Section 3, § 441(b)(5) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: Within 120 days after the effective date of sections one through four of the local law that added this section, each covered entity that is an agency shall, to the extent practicable, provide the board with a written list of such members whom such covered entity has finally determined to have engaged in an act of bias or severe act of bias
4770945.deadline_text: Within 120 days after the effective date of sections one through four of the local law that added this section

4770945.action_summary: Request information from each covered entity that is not an agency, except courts, about final determinations that members engaged in acts of bias or severe acts of bias, including determinations made on or after January 1, 2016, at least once every 4 months.
4770945.citation: Section 3, § 441(b)(6) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: At least once every 4 months after the effective date of sections one through four of the local law that added this section, the board shall request from each covered entity that is not an agency, except a court with jurisdiction within the state of New York, information about final determinations made by such entity that such a member engaged in an act of bias or severe act of bias

4770945.action_summary: Consult with the law department to obtain information about final determinations by courts with jurisdiction within the state of New York that members engaged in acts of bias or severe acts of bias, including determinations made on or after January 1, 2016.
4770945.citation: Section 3, § 441(b)(7) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: The board shall consult with the law department to obtain information about final determinations by a covered entity that is a court with jurisdiction within the state of New York that such a member has engaged in an act of bias or severe act of bias, including final determinations made on or after January 1, 2016.

4770945.action_summary: Determine the scope of past conduct by rank, assigned roles, and nature of the act of bias, and investigate all or a representative sampling of the member's past conduct from date of hire through last employment date or investigation initiation date.
4770945.citation: Section 3, § 441(c) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: The board shall determine the scope of past conduct in the course of performance of official duties by such member to investigate based on the member's professional rank and assigned roles and the nature of the member's act of bias. The board shall investigate all or a representative sampling of such member's past conduct

4770945.action_summary: Provide written notice to the member being investigated and to the relevant covered entity within 10 days after initiating an investigation.
4770945.citation: Section 3, § 441(d)(1) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: Within 10 days after the board initiates such investigation, the board shall provide written notice to the member being investigated and to the relevant covered entity.
4770945.deadline_text: Within 10 days after the board initiates such investigation

4770945.action_summary: Provide a written statement of final determination to the member being investigated within 10 days after completing the investigation, including investigation details, findings, recommendations for remedial action, and explanation of any termination.
4770945.citation: Section 3, § 441(d)(2) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: Within 10 days after the completion of such investigation, the board shall provide a written statement of final determination to the member being investigated. Such statement shall include (i) the investigation's details, when it was initiated and concluded, the identity of its subject and a summary of the materials reviewed by the board during the investigation; (ii) the board's investigative findings, including the identification of any threat to the safety of an individual or the public and whether the board found evidence of any additional past acts of bias committed in the course of performance of official duties; (iii) if applicable, any recommendations of the board for remedial action, including training, discipline, where consistent with section 75 of the civil service law, or both; and (iv) if applicable, a statement that the board has determined to terminate the investigation and an explanation why.
4770945.deadline_text: Within 10 days after the completion of such investigation

4770945.action_summary: Provide an opportunity for the member being investigated to submit a written answer to any findings or recommendations, establish a time period by rule, and consider and determine whether to revise findings or recommendations in response.
4770945.citation: Section 3, § 441(d)(3) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: The board shall provide an opportunity for the member being investigated to answer in writing, within a time period established by rule, any findings or recommendations made by the board. If such member timely submits such an answer, the board shall consider it and determine whether to revise any such findings or recommendations in response.

4770945.action_summary: Submit the written statement of final determination to the police commissioner, parties who received notice, and any other appropriate agency or official within 10 days after finalizing it.
4770945.citation: Section 3, § 441(d)(4) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: Within 10 days after finalizing the written statement of final determination pursuant to paragraphs 2 and 3 of this subdivision, the board shall submit such written statement to the police commissioner, any other parties to whom notice was sent pursuant to paragraph 1 of this subdivision and any other appropriate agency or official as determined by the board.
4770945.deadline_text: Within 10 days after finalizing the written statement of final determination

4770945.action_summary: Promulgate rules that prescribe the manner of conducting investigations, presenting findings, making recommendations, providing notice, and providing an opportunity for the member being investigated to be heard.
4770945.citation: Section 3, § 441(f) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: The board shall, in accordance with subdivisions b, c and d of this section, promulgate rules that further prescribe the manner in which the board is to conduct investigations, present findings, make recommendations, provide notice and provide an opportunity for the member being investigated to be heard.

4770945.action_summary: Issue a semi-annual report to the mayor and city council describing board activities and summarizing actions, including investigation dates, status, completion or termination dates, investigative findings, recommendations, and police commissioner responses for each investigation initiated.
4770945.citation: Section 1, § 440(c)(6) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: The board shall issue to the mayor and the city council a semi-annual report which shall describe its activities and summarize its actions. Such report shall include, for each investigation initiated pursuant to section 441, such investigation's date of initiation, current status and any date of completion or termination, a description of any investigative findings and recommendations set forth in a written statement of final determination and a description of any written reports from the police commissioner in response to a written statement of final determination.

4770945.action_summary: Provide such assistance as the civilian complaint review board may reasonably request, cooperate fully with board investigations, and provide records and materials necessary for investigations, except where prohibited by law.
4770945.citation: Section 2, § 440(d)(1) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: It shall be the duty of the police department to provide such assistance as the board may reasonably request, to cooperate fully with investigations by the board, and to provide to the board upon request records and other materials which are necessary for investigations undertaken pursuant to this chapter, except such records or materials that cannot be disclosed by law.

4770945.action_summary: Ensure that police department officers and employees appear before and respond to inquiries of the civilian complaint review board and its civilian investigators in connection with investigations, in accordance with department interrogation procedures.
4770945.citation: Section 2, § 440(d)(2) of the New York City Charter
4770945.quote: The police commissioner shall ensure that officers and employees of the police department appear before and respond to inquiries of the board and its civilian investigators in connection with investigations undertaken pursuant to this chapter, provided that such inquiries are conducted in accordance with department procedures for interrogation of members.

4770945.action_summary: Maintain a centralized system to record, track, review, and evaluate officer activity and identify officers needing enhanced training, monitoring, or reassignment, including results of civilian complaint review board investigations conducted pursuant to section 441 of the charter.
4770945.citation: Section 4, NYC Admin. Code § 14-190(a)
4770945.quote: The department shall maintain a centralized system that is used to record, track, review[,] and evaluate officer activity and to identify officers who may be in need of enhanced training, monitoring[,] or reassignment. Such system shall collect and utilize, at a minimum, the following: (xiv) results of investigations conducted by the civilian complaint review board pursuant to section 441 of the charter.

4770945.action_summary: Engage an independent external consultant to perform a full and complete review of all or a statistically significant sampling of work performed and cases handled by the equal employment opportunity division between October 1, 2017 and October 31, 2020, to determine compliance with the division's purpose, mission, and protocols.
4770945.citation: Section 5(a) of the Local Law
4770945.quote: The police department shall, in accordance with this section, engage an independent, external consultant to perform an independent, full and complete review of all, or a statistically significant sampling of, work performed and cases handled by the equal employment opportunity division of the police department between October 1, 2017 and October 31, 2020, inclusive, to determine whether such work performed and cases handled by such division were done in accordance with the purpose, mission and protocols of such division

4770945.action_summary: Fully cooperate with the external consultant's review and provide all requested assistance, including policies describing the purpose, mission, and protocols of the equal employment opportunity division, and ensure all members respond to consultant inquiries.
4770945.citation: Section 5(b) of the Local Law
4770945.quote: The police department shall fully cooperate with such review and provide such assistance as such external consultant may request, including by providing such external consultant with any and all materials containing policies of the police department that describe the purpose, mission or protocols of such division. The police commissioner shall ensure that all members of the police department and other persons acting on behalf of such department respond to inquiries by such external consultant in connection with such review.

4770945.action_summary: Make publicly available online and submit to the mayor and speaker of the council a written statement on actions taken or planned in response to the external consultant's report within 120 days of receiving it, including detailed explanation if deviating from recommendations.
4770945.citation: Section 5(d) of the Local Law
4770945.quote: Within 120 days after receiving such report from such external consultant, the police commissioner shall make publicly available online and submit to the mayor and speaker of the council a written statement on the actions that the police department has taken or plans to take in response to the findings and recommendations in such report. In any instance where the action taken or planned to be taken in response to such report differs from that recommended in such report, the police commissioner shall provide in such statement a detailed explanation of the reasons for deviating from such recommendation.
4770945.deadline_text: Within 120 days after receiving such report from such external consultant

4770945.action_summary: Provide an updated written statement to the mayor and speaker of the council within 10 days after taking any action in response to the external consultant's report after the initial 120-day period that was not described in a prior statement.
4770945.citation: Section 5(d) of the Local Law
4770945.quote: If the police commissioner takes any action in response to such report after such 120-day period, and such action was not described in a prior statement prepared by the police commissioner pursuant to this subdivision, the police commissioner shall make publicly available online and provide to the mayor and speaker of the council an updated version of such statement within 10 days after taking such action.
4770945.deadline_text: within 10 days after taking such action

4770945.actor_raw: the police department or an external consultant engaged by such department
4770945.action_summary: Before making any report available to the public, remove any individual's name, all personal identifying information, and any information that in conjunction with publicly available information may result in disclosure of identity.
4770945.citation: Section 5(f) of the Local Law
4770945.quote: Before making any report available to the public pursuant to this section, the police department or an external consultant engaged by such department shall remove any individual's name, all personal identifying information as defined by subdivision a of section 10-501 of the administrative code of the city of New York and any information that, in conjunction with information available to the general public, may result in the disclosure of an individual's identity.

4897750.agency_full: Mayor's Office of Climate and Environmental Justice
4897750.action_summary: Complete and post on its website an inventory and analysis of city government emissions measured in carbon dioxide equivalent for the fiscal year ending in the previous calendar year, and calculate the percentage change in city government emissions.
