4897750.agency_full: Mayor's Office of Climate and Environmental Justice
4897750.action_summary: Complete and post on its website a list of current and future capital projects intended to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from city government operations, with estimated emission reductions, project timeline, total projected budget, and schedule of planned commitments.
4897750.quote: No later than 30 days after the publication of the report that, pursuant to paragraph 1 of subdivision d of section 219 of the charter, is required to be published no later than 90 days after the adoption of the capital budget, the office shall complete and post on its website a list of current and future capital projects intended to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from city government operations, and, for each such project, an estimate of the expected reductions of greenhouse gas emissions, a project timeline, the total projected budget, and the schedule of planned commitments
4897750.deadline_text: No later than 30 days after the publication of the report that, pursuant to paragraph 1 of subdivision d of section 219 of the charter, is required to be published no later than 90 days after the adoption of the capital budget

4897750.agency_full: Mayor's Office of Climate and Environmental Justice
4897750.action_summary: Ensure the report required by charter section 224.1 includes the amount and percentage change of greenhouse gas emissions from capital projects involving buildings owned or operated by the New York city housing authority.
4897750.quote: The report required by subdivision m of section 224.1 of the charter shall include the amount of greenhouse gas emissions from capital projects involving buildings that are owned or operated by the New York city housing authority measured in carbon dioxide equivalent for the fiscal year ending in the previous calendar year, and the percentage change in such emissions measured in carbon dioxide equivalent for such calendar year, relative to such emissions for calendar year 2005.

4897750.agency_full: Mayor's Office of Climate and Environmental Justice
4897750.action_summary: Submit to the mayor, speaker of the council, public advocate and comptroller, and post on its website, an annual report regarding actions taken pursuant to the greenhouse gas emissions chapter, including changes in citywide and city government emissions, programs developed and implemented, and education and outreach activities.
4897750.quote: No later than November 15 of every year after 2021, the office shall submit to the mayor, the speaker of the council, the public advocate and the comptroller and post on its website a report regarding actions taken by the office pursuant to the provisions of this chapter.
4897750.deadline_text: No later than November 15 of every year after 2021

4918988.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
4918988.action_summary: Submit to the City Council a biennial report listing changes made to pesticide classification lists and efforts undertaken by city agencies to reduce or eliminate pesticide use.
4918988.quote: On June 1, 2022, and every June 1 thereafter, the department shall submit to the City Council a report listing changes made to the lists of pesticides named in subdivisions b and c since the date of the last report submitted pursuant to this section.
4918988.deadline_text: On June 1, 2022, and every June 1 thereafter

4918988.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
4918988.action_summary: Post waiver applications in their entirety to the department's website within thirty days of granting a waiver.
4918988.quote: Within thirty days of granting a waiver, the department shall post the waiver application in its entirety to the department's website
4918988.deadline_text: Within thirty days of granting a waiver

4918988.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
4918988.action_summary: Promulgate regulations designating additional pesticides that pose risks to public health similar to those regulated, and providing limitations on their use by city agencies and contractors.
4918988.quote: The commissioner may promulgate regulations designating additional pesticides that pose risks to the public health similar to those posed by the pesticides regulated under this section, and providing that the use of such additional pesticides by city agencies and their contractors shall be subject to limitations set forth in such regulations.

4920296.action_summary: Establish a later effective date for the reduction of primary construction superintendent workload limits, provided such date is not later than January 1, 2025.
4920296.quote: beginning on January 1, 2024 or a later date established by the department, provided that such date is not later than January 1, 2025, no individual may be designated as the primary construction superintendent for more than three jobs
4920296.deadline_text: a later date established by the department, provided that such date is not later than January 1, 2025

4920296.action_summary: Establish a later effective date for requiring construction superintendents to be dedicated to one job only, provided such date is not later than January 1, 2027.
4920296.quote: beginning on January 1, 2026 or a later date established by the department, provided that such date is not later than January 1, 2027, no individual may be designated as the primary construction superintendent for more than one job
4920296.deadline_text: a later date established by the department, provided that such date is not later than January 1, 2027

4920296.action_summary: Promulgate rules or take other actions for the implementation of this local law prior to the effective date.
4920296.quote: the commissioner of buildings may promulgate rules or take other actions for the implementation of this local law prior to such effective date

5185972.action_summary: Develop and implement by September 30, 2022, a victim-centered, trauma-informed questioning training program designed to develop skills for the response to and investigation of incidents involving domestic violence, sexual crimes, or human trafficking.
5185972.quote: The department shall develop, and implement by September 30, 2022, a victim-centered, trauma-informed questioning training program designed to develop skills for the response to and investigation of incidents involving domestic violence, sexual crimes, or human trafficking.

5185972.actor_raw: the director of the mayor's office to end domestic and gender-based violence
5185972.agency_full: Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence
5185972.action_summary: Ensure an interdisciplinary and interagency committee meets no later than May 1, 2022, and twice a year thereafter to make recommendations to the department regarding the training program.
5185972.quote: There shall be an interdisciplinary and interagency committee that shall meet no later than May 1, 2022, and twice a year thereafter.

5185972.action_summary: Ensure all new department recruits receive at least three hours of training related to domestic violence, sexual crimes, and human trafficking.
5185972.quote: All new department recruits shall receive at least three hours of training related to domestic violence, sexual crimes, and human trafficking.

5185972.action_summary: Ensure all uniformed members whose responsibilities include routinely interacting with victims of crime receive training on incidents involving domestic violence, sexual crimes, or human trafficking on a biennial basis.
5185972.quote: All uniformed members of the department whose responsibilities include routinely interacting with victims of crime, shall receive training on incidents involving domestic violence, sexual crimes, or human trafficking, on a biennial basis.

5185972.action_summary: Report annually beginning February 1, 2023, information concerning domestic violence, sexual crimes, or human trafficking training for the previous calendar year, disaggregated by recruit and ongoing training, and post the report on the department's website and submit to the mayor and speaker of the council.
5185972.quote: Beginning February 1, 2023, and no later than each February 1 thereafter, the department shall report the following information concerning domestic violence, sexual crimes, or human trafficking training for the previous calendar year: the number of police officers trained and the curriculum used for each training session.
5185972.deadline_text: Beginning February 1, 2023, and no later than each February 1 thereafter

5185972.actor_raw: the director of the office to end domestic and gender-based violence
5185972.agency_full: Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence
5185972.action_summary: Serve as chairperson of the domestic violence fatality review committee and ensure the committee meets at least four times a year.
5185972.quote: The director of the office to end domestic and gender-based violence, or their designee, shall serve as chairperson of the committee.
affected_groups: agencies providing services to domestic violence victims

5185972.actor_raw: the director of the office to end domestic and gender-based violence
5185972.agency_full: Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence
5185972.action_summary: Submit to the mayor and speaker of the city council on an annual basis a report on domestic violence fatalities, including number of cases, non-identifying data on victims and perpetrators, risk factors, and recommendations for service coordination and improvement.
5185972.quote: The committee shall submit to the mayor and to the speaker of the city council, on an annual basis, a report including, but not limited to, the number of domestic violence fatality cases which occurred in the city of New York during the previous year

5185972.actor_raw: the director of the office to end domestic and gender-based violence
5185972.agency_full: Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence
5185972.action_summary: Establish a mechanism to review individual case-level data on gender-based and domestic violence fatalities and establish and chair a fatality advisory committee to conduct or assist in such review.
5185972.quote: The director of the office to end domestic and gender-based violence, or the director's designee, shall establish a mechanism to review certain individual case-level data on gender-based and domestic violence fatalities, identified after due consideration of the goals of the fatality review committee and to the extent such data is available.

5256132.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
5256132.action_summary: Amend the official map of the city of New York to reflect the renaming of St. Albans Park to Archie Spigner Park in Queens.
5256132.quote: The official map of the city of new york shall be amended in accordance with the provisions of section one of this local law.

5451335.action_summary: Submit an annual report to the speaker of the council and the mayor on training for school safety personnel to identify students in emotional crisis and training on trauma impacts, including outside experts consulted, training formats, number of personnel trained, and number who demonstrated proficiency.
5451335.quote: the department shall submit to the speaker of the council and the mayor and post on the department's website a report on any training for school safety personnel to identify a student in emotional crisis, or any training on the impacts of trauma on child development
5451335.deadline_text: No later than October 1, 2024, and no later than October 1 of each year thereafter

5451335.action_summary: Post the annual report on training for school safety personnel on the department's website.
5451335.quote: the department shall submit to the speaker of the council and the mayor and post on the department's website a report on any training for school safety personnel to identify a student in emotional crisis
5451335.deadline_text: No later than October 1, 2024, and no later than October 1 of each year thereafter

5521073.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
5521073.action_summary: Engage in ongoing public education efforts to inform employers, employment agencies, employees and job applicants about their rights and responsibilities under the earned safe and sick time act.
5521073.quote: The commissioner shall engage in ongoing public education efforts to inform employers, employment agencies, employees and job applicants about their rights and responsibilities under this chapter

5521073.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
5521073.action_summary: In coordination with the department of health and mental hygiene, distribute posters, flyers, and other written materials concerning employees' rights under the earned safe and sick time act to pharmacies, doctors' offices, hospitals and other appropriate sites.
5521073.quote: In coordination with the department of health and mental hygiene, distribute posters, flyers, and other written materials concerning employees' rights pursuant to this chapter to pharmacies, doctors' offices, and hospitals and such other sites as may be appropriate

5521073.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
5521073.action_summary: Invite the New York city health and hospitals corporation to participate in the posting and dissemination of posters, flyers and written materials concerning employees' rights under the earned safe and sick time act.
5521073.quote: Invite the New York city health and hospitals corporation to participate in the posting and dissemination of posters, flyers and written materials concerning employees' rights pursuant to this chapter

5534183.action_summary: Identify and study common issues relating to concerns and needs of shelter clients with disabilities, reasonable accommodation requests and complaints, and physical conditions of shelters, and make policy recommendations to the mayor, council, and department.
5534183.quote: identify and study common issues relating to the concerns and needs of shelter clients with disabilities; reasonable accommodation requests and complaints; and the physical conditions of shelters, and that shall make policy recommendations

5534183.action_summary: Hold its first meeting no later than 30 days after the appointment of the final public member and elect a chairperson at that meeting.
5534183.quote: The advisory board shall hold its first meeting no later than 30 days after the appointment of the final public member required by subdivision c of this local law, and at such meeting shall elect a chairperson.
5534183.deadline_text: no later than 30 days after the appointment of the final public member required by subdivision c of this local law

5534183.action_summary: Meet at least quarterly and keep a record of its proceedings including meeting agenda, minutes, follow-up items, list of participants, and date of next scheduled meeting.
5534183.quote: The advisory board shall meet at least quarterly and keep a record of its proceedings including, but not limited to, the meeting agenda, meeting minutes, any follow up items, a list of participants, and the date for the next scheduled meeting.

5534183.action_summary: Post records of each advisory board meeting on the department's website no later than 14 calendar days after each meeting is held.
5534183.quote: Records of each meeting of the advisory board shall be posted on the department's website no later than 14 calendar days after each such meeting is held.
5534183.deadline_text: no later than 14 calendar days after each such meeting is held

5534183.action_summary: Submit a report to the mayor, the speaker of the council, and the department including results of its study and any recommendations, no later than January 31, 2024, and annually on January 31 thereafter.
5534183.quote: No later than January 31, 2024, and annually on January 31 thereafter, the advisory board shall submit a report to the mayor, the speaker of the council, and the department including the results of its study and any recommendations required by this section.
5534183.deadline_text: No later than January 31, 2024, and annually on January 31 thereafter

5534183.action_summary: Post the advisory board's annual report on the department's website.
5534183.quote: Such report shall also be posted on the department's website.

5534183.action_summary: Appoint 4 of the 7 public members of the shelter accessibility advisory board.
5534183.quote: 4 of whom shall be appointed by the mayor and 3 of whom shall be appointed by the speaker of the council

5534211.action_summary: File the amended district plan of 2022 for the Sutphin Boulevard business improvement district extension with the city clerk.
5534211.quote: Immediately upon adoption of this local law by the council, the council shall file with the city clerk the amended district plan of 2022 upon which the Sutphin Boulevard business improvement district, and the extension thereof, is based.
5534211.deadline_text: Immediately upon adoption of this local law by the council

5534211.action_summary: File the amended district plan of 2022 containing the change in assessment method and increase in maximum expenditure for the Sutphin Boulevard business improvement district with the city clerk.
5534211.quote: Immediately upon adoption of this local law, the council shall file with the city clerk the amended district plan of 2022 containing the change in the method of assessment authorized by subdivision a of this section and the increase in the maximum total amount to be expended for improvements authorized by subdivision b of this section.
5534211.deadline_text: Immediately upon adoption of this local law
affected_groups: property owners in the Sutphin Boulevard business improvement district

5534289.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
5534289.action_summary: Provide educational materials and conduct outreach relating to the safe operation of electric space heaters in residential settings.
5534289.quote: providing educational materials and conducting outreach relating to the safe operation of electric space heaters in residential settings

5534289.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
5534289.action_summary: Make written fire safety educational materials available in the top ten languages most commonly spoken within the city.
5534289.quote: Any written materials disseminated by the department pertaining to fire safety education shall be made available in the top ten languages most commonly spoken within the city

5555546.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
5555546.action_summary: Submit to the mayor and speaker of the council, and make publicly available on the department's website, a biannual report on objections to department orders for lead abatement or remediation.
5555546.quote: The department shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and make publicly available on the department's website, a report on the number of objections to department orders for lead abatement or remediation
5555546.deadline_text: no later than August 30 for the period covering January through June of the same year, and no later than February 28 for the period covering July through December of the prior year
affected_groups: residents of housing developments operated by the New York city housing authority

5555546.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
5555546.action_summary: Include in the biannual report the number of orders withdrawn in full, disaggregated by reasons for withdrawal including faulty paint sampling, inconclusive test results, or exemptions based on dwelling construction date.
5555546.quote: The report required pursuant to subdivision a of this section shall include the number of orders withdrawn in full by the department, disaggregated by the reasons such orders were withdrawn
5555546.deadline_text: no later than August 30 for the period covering January through June of the same year, and no later than February 28 for the period covering July through December of the prior year
affected_groups: residents of housing developments operated by the New York city housing authority

5570408.action_summary: Post monthly, calendar year, and fiscal year citywide data regarding utilization of city-administered facilities on its website and the single web portal established pursuant to section 23-502.
5570408.quote: the mayor's office of operations shall for each month, calendar year and fiscal year post the following information, if known, on its website and the single web portal established pursuant to section 23-502
5570408.deadline_text: Commencing on November 1, 2011, and no later than the first day of each month thereafter

5570408.action_summary: Post monthly, calendar year, and fiscal year data on applications and entrance to DHS-administered shelter facilities on the same website location as subdivision (b) data.
5570408.quote: the mayor's office of operations shall for each month, calendar year and fiscal year post on the same location on its website as the data posted pursuant to subdivision b of this section, the following data for those seeking admission and entrance to DHS-administered shelter facilities
5570408.deadline_text: Commencing on November 1, 2011, and no later than the first day of each month thereafter

5570408.action_summary: Post all required data electronically in a commonly available non-proprietary database format suitable for analysis.
5570408.quote: The data required pursuant to subdivisions b and c of this section shall be posted electronically on the portal specified in subdivision b in a commonly available non-proprietary database format that is suitable for analysis

5570408.action_summary: Report monthly to the speaker of the council and post on the mayor's office of operations website disaggregated information on exits from city-administered residential facilities into various types of housing.
5570408.quote: the mayor's office of operations, for each month, calendar year and fiscal year, shall report to the speaker of the council and post on the mayor's office of operations website, disaggregated information, if known, regarding the number of families with children, adult families, single adults who have not returned within two monthly reporting cycles, and runaway and homeless youth from city-administered residential facilities that exited
5570408.deadline_text: Commencing on July 1, 2023, and no later than the first day of each month thereafter

5570408.action_summary: Report monthly to the speaker of the council and post on the mayor's office of operations website unduplicated information regarding financings, starts and completions of permanent housing set aside for individuals and families experiencing homelessness.
5570408.quote: the mayor's office of operations for each month, calendar year and fiscal year, shall report to the speaker of the council and post on the mayor's office of operations website, unduplicated information regarding the financings, starts and completions of the following permanent housing or subsequent iterations of such housing, set aside for individuals or families experiencing homelessness
5570408.deadline_text: Commencing on July 1, 2023, and no later than each month thereafter

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Set fees for disposal of yard waste and organic waste at department compost facilities by rule.
5570477.quote: Such fees shall be set by rule promulgated by the commissioner.

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Adopt and implement rules designating at least six recyclable materials including plastics and yard waste and organic waste, and requiring households to source separate such materials.
5570477.quote: The commissioner shall adopt and implement rules designating at least six recyclable materials, including plastics to the extent required in subdivision c of this section and yard waste to the extent required in section 16-308 of this chapter and organic waste to the extent required in section 16-308.1 of this chapter, contained in department-managed solid waste and requiring households to source separate such designated materials.

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Provide for source separation, collection and composting of yard waste from department-managed waste, and collection and composting of yard waste from residential properties owned or operated by the New York City Housing Authority.
5570477.quote: The commissioner shall provide for the source separation, collection and composting of department-managed yard waste, unless the generator otherwise provides for recycling or storage for composting or mulching. In addition, the commissioner shall provide for the collection and composting of yard waste generated and source separated at residential properties owned or operated by the New York city housing authority.

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Operate one or more yard waste composting facilities for composting yard waste collected by or delivered to the department.
5570477.quote: There shall be operated by or on behalf of the department one or more yard waste composting facilities through which the department shall compost yard waste collected by or delivered to the department pursuant to this section.

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Work in consultation with the composting facility siting task force to identify additional locations to site yard waste composting facilities with the goal of establishing at least one such facility in each borough where the department conducts yard waste composting collection.
5570477.quote: The department shall also work in consultation with the composting facility siting task force established by the two thousand and six solid waste management plan to identify additional locations to site yard waste composting facilities with the goal of establishing at least one such composting facility in each borough where the department conducts yard waste composting collection.

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Ensure that no landfill, waste transfer station, intermodal facility, incinerator or resource recovery facility owned, operated or used by the department accepts truckloads of department-managed waste primarily composed of yard waste for final disposal.
5570477.quote: No landfill, waste transfer station, intermodal facility, incinerator or resource recovery facility owned, operated or used by the department shall accept truckloads of department-managed waste primarily composed of yard waste for final disposal, except that composted yard waste may be used as part of the final vegetative cover for a department landfill.

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Notify all residents in districts that receive yard waste collection by the department of pre-collection procedures and undertake actions necessary to effectuate purposes of yard waste separation requirements.
5570477.quote: The commissioner shall notify all residents in districts that receive yard waste collection by the department of such pre-collection procedures, and undertake any other action necessary to effectuate the purposes of this subdivision.

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Establish a mandatory citywide curbside organics collection program for the diversion of organic waste by October 2, 2023 for at least 30 sanitation districts and by October 7, 2024 for all remaining sanitation districts.
5570477.quote: The department shall establish a mandatory citywide curbside organics collection program for the diversion of organic waste in accordance with this section. Such program shall be implemented by no later than: 1. October 2, 2023, for residential properties in no less than 30 sanitation districts, as determined by the commissioner by rule. 2. October 7, 2024, for residential properties in all remaining sanitation districts.
5570477.deadline_text: October 7, 2024, for residential properties in all remaining sanitation districts

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Develop, submit to the mayor and speaker of the council, and post on the department's website a curbside organics collection implementation plan by July 1, 2023.
5570477.quote: No later than July 1, 2023, the department shall develop, submit to the mayor and speaker of the council, and post on the department's website a curbside organics collection implementation plan.

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Include in the next solid waste management plan a plan to maximize usable composting of organic waste collected and describe the amount of organic waste collected and sent to composting facilities.
5570477.quote: In the next solid waste management plan prepared pursuant to section 27-0107 of the environmental conservation law and presented to the council pursuant to section 16-140 following the effective date of the local law that added this subdivision, the department shall include a plan to maximize the usable composting of organic waste collected pursuant to this section.

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Report by weight the total amount of organic waste diverted during the previous year disaggregated by sanitation district as part of the department's annual zero waste report.
5570477.quote: The department shall report by weight the total amount of organic waste diverted pursuant to this section during the previous year, disaggregated by sanitation district. Such report shall be included as part of the department's annual zero waste report required pursuant to section 16-316.5 of this chapter.

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Develop an outreach and education program to educate residents, building owners, and staff on the curbside organics collection program in all designated citywide languages and distribute materials two months prior to implementation in each district.
5570477.quote: The department shall develop an outreach and education program to educate residents, building owners, and staff of residential buildings on the curbside organics collection program established pursuant to this section. Materials used for such outreach and education program shall be available in all designated citywide languages, as defined in section 23-1101, and any additional languages as determined by the department in consultation with local community organizations. No later than two months prior to the implementation of the curbside organics collection program for residential properties in a sanitation district pursuant to subdivision a of this section, the department shall distribute such materials to residents, building owners, and community based organizations in such district.
5570477.deadline_text: No later than two months prior to the implementation of the curbside organics collection program for residential properties in a sanitation district

5570477.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570477.action_summary: Adopt and implement rules as necessary to effectuate the curbside organics collection section, including designation of organic waste as a recyclable material, procedures for placement of organic waste, and implementation and enforcement provisions.
5570477.quote: The commissioner shall adopt and implement rules as necessary to effectuate this section. Such rules may include, but need not be limited to, the designation of organic waste as a recyclable material pursuant to subdivision b of section 16-305 of this chapter, procedures requiring the placement of organic waste at the curbside, in specialized containers or in another manner determined by the commissioner pursuant to subdivision d of such section, and the implementation and enforcement of this section and such rules in buildings containing four or more dwelling units pursuant to subdivisions e, f, and g of section 16-305.

5570512.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570512.action_summary: Report annually to the council evaluations and determinations regarding the cost-reasonableness of designating rigid plastic containers as recyclable materials as part of the department's annual zero waste report.
5570512.quote: shall report such evaluations to the council as part of the department's annual zero waste report required pursuant to subdivision b of section 16-316.5

5570512.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570512.action_summary: Consolidate information from lead recycling or sustainability coordinator reports and include such information as part of the department's annual zero waste report.
5570512.quote: The department shall consolidate the information contained in all reports prepared pursuant to this subdivision and include such information as part of the department's annual zero waste report required pursuant to subdivision b of section 16-316.5

5570512.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570512.action_summary: Include the chancellor's annual compliance report as part of the department's annual zero waste report.
5570512.quote: The department shall include the chancellor's report as part of the department's annual zero waste report required pursuant to subdivision b of section 16-316.5

5570512.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570512.action_summary: Report annually the total number of public space recycling receptacles added during the relevant reporting year and the locations in which they were placed as part of the department's annual zero waste report.
5570512.quote: The department shall report the total number of public space recycling receptacles added during the relevant reporting year, and the locations in which they were placed. Such report shall be included as part of the department's annual zero waste report required pursuant to subdivision b of section 16-316.5

5570512.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570512.action_summary: Report annually by weight the amount of textiles collected in publicly accessible textile drop-off bins and through public textile reuse and recycling sites as part of the department's annual zero waste report.
5570512.quote: The department shall report by weight the amount of textiles collected in publicly accessible textile drop-off bins located on city property or property maintained by the city, through public textile reuse and recycling sites pursuant to subdivision a of this section and in publicly accessible textile drop-off bins maintained on private property. Such report shall be included as part of the department's annual zero waste report required pursuant to subdivision b of section 16-316.5

5570512.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570512.action_summary: Report annually the total amount of household hazardous waste diverted by the program, specifying each category of material and the amount collected at each collection event or site as part of the department's annual zero waste report.
5570512.quote: The department shall report annually the total amount of household hazardous waste diverted by the program established pursuant to subdivision a of this section. Such report shall specify each category of material and the amount of such material collected at each collection event or site established pursuant to subdivision a of this section. Such report shall be included as part of the department's annual zero waste report required pursuant to subdivision b of section 16-316.5

5570512.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570512.action_summary: Report on opportunities to establish additional household hazardous waste collection events and sites to the mayor and council within two years of the effective date, and annually thereafter, as part of the department's annual zero waste report.
5570512.quote: The commissioner shall report on such opportunities to the mayor and the council within two years of the effective date of this section, and annually thereafter, and such report shall be included as part of the department's annual zero waste report required pursuant to subdivision b of section 16-316.5
5570512.deadline_text: within two years of the effective date of this section

5570512.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570512.action_summary: Submit to the mayor, speaker of the council, district manager of each community board, and each citizens' solid waste advisory board, and make publicly available online, a plan to achieve zero waste and increase waste diversion from landfill and incineration.
5570512.quote: On or before January 1, 2024, the commissioner shall submit to the mayor, the speaker of the council, the district manager of each community board, and each citizens' solid waste advisory board as defined in section 16-317, and make publicly available online, a plan to achieve the goal of zero waste

5570512.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570512.action_summary: Submit to the mayor, speaker of the council, district manager of each community board, and each citizens' solid waste advisory board, and make publicly available online, an annual report on the city's progress toward achieving zero waste and increasing waste diversion from landfill and incineration.
5570512.quote: On or before October 1, 2024, and annually thereafter, the commissioner shall submit to the mayor, the speaker of the council, the district manager of each community board, and each citizens' solid waste advisory board as defined in section 16-317, and make publicly available online, a report on the city's progress toward the goal of achieving zero waste
5570512.deadline_text: On or before October 1, 2024, and annually thereafter

5570515.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
5570515.action_summary: Establish a goal of diverting citywide-generated recyclable waste by 100 percent by calendar year 2030 from landfills or incinerators.

6506662.action_summary: Establish by rule what constitutes significant alterations to parking garages that trigger the requirement to support EVSE.
6506662.quote: A new parking garage and a parking garage in an existing structure undergoing such significant alterations as established by the department by rule shall be capable of supporting EVSE in accordance with this section.

6506662.quote: A new open parking lot and an existing open parking lot on the same tax lot or appurtenant to a building owned by the same owner of such open parking lot undergoing such significant alterations as established by the department by rule shall be capable of supporting and be equipped with EVSE in accordance with this section.

6509351.agency_full: Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence
6509351.action_summary: Develop a training program on traumatic brain injury for first responders responding to domestic violence incidents, covering prevalence, causes, identification, response, and long-term health effects.
6509351.quote: the director, in consultation with the fire commissioner and the police commissioner, shall develop a training on the topic of traumatic brain injury to be provided to first responders likely to respond to incidents involving domestic violence.

6509351.agency_full: Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence
6509351.action_summary: Provide the traumatic brain injury training to the fire department and police department for inclusion in their e-learning courses and training series.
6509351.quote: The office shall provide the training created pursuant to subdivision a of this section to the fire department and police department to be included in such department's respective e-learning courses and training series

6509351.agency_full: Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence
6509351.action_summary: Conduct a public awareness campaign to destigmatize and increase understanding of the connection between domestic violence and traumatic brain injury, creating physical and digital materials.
6509351.quote: the office shall conduct a public awareness campaign to destigmatize and increase understanding of the connection between domestic violence and traumatic brain injury. Such campaign shall be limited to creating physical and digital materials.

6509351.agency_full: Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence
6509351.action_summary: Make public awareness campaign materials available in designated citywide languages and post on the office website, police department website, 311 citizen center website, and distribute at family justice centers.
6509351.quote: Such materials shall be made available in the designated citywide languages as defined in section 23-1101, posted on the office's website, the police department website, the 311 citizen center website, and distributed at family justice centers.

6509351.agency_full: Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence
6509351.action_summary: Create and maintain an advisory panel on traumatic brain injury to review training and campaign materials and make recommendations on accuracy and currency.
6509351.quote: The director shall create and maintain an advisory panel on traumatic brain injury. Such panel shall convene at least once every 2 years to review the training developed pursuant to subdivision a of this section and the materials developed pursuant to subdivision c

6509351.action_summary: Provide a victim-centered, trauma-informed questioning training program that includes the long-term health implications of physical violence including traumatic brain injury.
6509351.quote: The department shall provide a victim-centered, trauma-informed questioning training program designed to develop skills for the response to and investigation of incidents involving domestic violence, sexual crimes, or human trafficking. The training program shall include but not be limited to the following components: the dynamics of domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking, including abuser tactics of power and control; danger and lethality factors in domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking cases; the criminal law provisions of the family protection domestic violence intervention act of 1994, chapter 222 of the laws of 1994; how to determine the primary aggressor in a domestic violence incident; the family offenses; the offense of endangering the welfare of a child; the offenses of assault in the first degree, manslaughter in the first and second degrees, criminally negligent homicide, and murder in the second degree, together with the defense of justification and the role of trauma in victims' acts of self-defense; the importance of avoiding expressions of skepticism, victim-blaming, and minimizing of the offense in early communications with victims; how to recognize signs of drug-facilitated sexual assault and preserve crucial evidence thereof; the overlap among domestic violence, sexual assault and human trafficking; victim-centered, trauma-informed questioning in domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, and related cases; the effects of trauma on victims; the long-term health implications of physical violence including, but not limited to, traumatic brain injury; techniques of trauma-informed policing; the resources available to victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking, including shelter and nonresidential services, locating hospital-based sexual assault forensic exams, and domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking emergency resources; and any other training deemed relevant by the commissioner, except that the commissioner may eliminate a training component or replace a training component with an alternative component in order to provide a comprehensive victim-centered, trauma-informed questioning training program.

6509351.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
6509351.action_summary: Deliver the traumatic brain injury training to all new recruits in the academy and, at least once every 2 years, in-service to uniformed members who routinely interact with victims of crime.
6509351.quote: All fire department and police department new recruits shall receive such training in the academy. 2. Ongoing training. All uniformed members of the fire department and police department whose responsibilities include routinely interacting with victims of crime shall receive such training in-service at least once every 2 years.

6555130.action_summary: Review all city-controlled parking lots and identify those where solar canopy installation would be cost-effective.
