6566072.quote: The official map of the city of New York shall be amended in accordance with the provisions of section one of this local law.

6566073.action_summary: Issue a report to the mayor and speaker of the council on the implementation of next generation 911 within the 911 emergency assistance system, and make it publicly available online.
6566073.quote: By no later than 6 months after the end of each fiscal year, the commissioner, in consultation with the police commissioner and fire commissioner, shall issue to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and make publicly available online, a report on the implementation of next generation 911 within the 911 emergency assistance system.
6566073.deadline_text: By no later than 6 months after the end of each fiscal year
affected_groups: deaf and hard of hearing community

6584182.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
6584182.action_summary: Complete a detailed, comprehensive citywide multi-season study of the city's residential and institutional waste streams to determine waste composition by type of material.
6584182.quote: the commissioner shall conduct a detailed, comprehensive citywide multi-season study of the department-managed residential and institutional waste streams for the purpose of determining the composition of such waste streams characterized by type of material

6584182.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
6584182.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council and the mayor and post on the department's website the results of the waste characterization study and an analysis of those results.
6584182.quote: Within 60 days of the completion of each study conducted pursuant to subdivision c of this section, the commissioner shall submit to the speaker of the council and the mayor and post on the department's website the results of such study and an analysis of those results
6584182.deadline_text: Within 60 days of the completion of each study

6584182.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
6584182.action_summary: Conduct a study of the composition of the commercial waste stream in the city, including construction and demolition debris, to the extent that information about such composition is readily available to the department.
6584182.quote: the commissioner shall conduct a study of the composition of the commercial waste stream in the city, including construction and demolition debris, to the extent that information about such composition is readily available to the department

6584226.action_summary: Submit to the mayor, speaker of the council, and board of correction a biannual report on alleged incidents of sexual assault and sexual harassment of correctional staff, including detailed data on each incident in machine-readable format.
6584226.quote: No later than February 15, 2026, and every 6 months thereafter, the department shall submit to the mayor, the speaker of the council, and the board of correction a report on alleged incidents of sexual assault of staff and sexual harassment of staff that occurred, or for which an investigation was pending, during the preceding reporting period.
6584226.deadline_text: No later than February 15, 2026, and every 6 months thereafter

6584226.action_summary: Assist the department of correction in collecting the information required to be reported on sexual assault and sexual harassment incidents of staff.
6584226.quote: In accordance with applicable law, correctional health services shall assist the department in collecting the information required to be reported under this section.

6584226.action_summary: Provide staff access to mental health resources relating to reducing stress and other adverse mental health impacts for persons working in correctional facilities, including confidential mental health counseling to address impacts of sexual assault and sexual harassment of staff.
6584226.quote: The department shall provide to staff access to mental health resources relating to reducing stress and other adverse mental health impacts for persons working in correctional facilities. In providing such access, the department shall consider guidance and any best practices established by the national institute of corrections. Such resources shall include, but need not be limited to, confidential mental health counseling to address the impacts of sexual assault of staff and sexual harassment of staff.

6584226.action_summary: Provide information about the availability of mental health resources on the department's website, electronically communicate such information to staff, and post such information in conspicuous locations in department facilities.
6584226.quote: The commissioner shall provide information about the availability of such resources on the department's website. The commissioner shall electronically communicate such information to staff, and shall post such information in conspicuous locations in facilities of the department.

6632652.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
6632652.action_summary: Notify a contractor of the process for requesting a written explanation when denying a request for final approval of a subcontractor.
6632652.quote: At the time of denial, such agency shall notify such contractor of the process for requesting a written explanation.

6632652.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
6632652.action_summary: Provide a written explanation of the reasons for denying a contractor's request for final approval of a subcontractor within thirty days of receipt of the request.
6632652.quote: Such agency shall provide such contractor a written explanation of the reasons for denial within thirty days of receipt of such request from such contractor.
6632652.deadline_text: within thirty days of receipt of such request from such contractor

6695222.actor_raw: the office, or another agency designated by the mayor
6695222.action_summary: Conduct outreach and education activities to raise awareness about city resources for addressing mental health challenges faced by parents, including perinatal mood and anxiety disorders, with materials reflecting current resource availability and including state and federal resources.
6695222.quote: The office, or another agency designated by the mayor, shall conduct outreach and education activities to raise awareness about city resources for addressing mental health challenges faced by parents
affected_groups: individuals with perinatal mood and anxiety disorders

6702334.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
6702334.action_summary: Make available written materials identifying resources for parents and guardians of newborn children, including essential care items, child safety, breastfeeding, nutrition, social services programs, postpartum care, support services, vaccine schedules, employment protections, and college savings plans.
6702334.quote: The department shall make available written materials that identify resources available to parents and guardians of newborn children, and shall update such materials periodically and as necessary to ensure accuracy.

6702334.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
6702334.action_summary: Distribute resource materials to parents or guardians of newborn children at the address designated for receipt of the child's certificate of registration of birth within 30 days following registration.
6702334.quote: Within 30 days following the registration of any birth, the department shall provide the resource materials described in subdivision a of this section to the parents or guardians of a newborn child
6702334.deadline_text: Within 30 days following the registration of any birth

6702334.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
6702334.action_summary: Make resource materials available on its website in English and each of the designated citywide languages as defined in section 23-1101 of the administrative code.
6702334.quote: The department shall make such resource materials available on its website in English and each of the designated citywide languages as defined in section 23-1101 of the administrative code.

6702334.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
6702334.action_summary: Create and maintain on its website a publicly accessible, searchable directory of community-based organizations contracted to provide services supporting maternal health, searchable by location, service provided, and including service types, languages offered, and contact information.
6702334.quote: The department shall create and maintain on its website a publicly accessible, searchable directory of (i) community-based organizations that maintain contracts with the department to provide services supporting maternal health and (ii) organizations contracted with agencies and entities consulted pursuant to subdivision b of this section to support maternal health.

6727936.action_summary: Send a notification to each owner of real property with assessed value of $250,000 or less where tax liens from nonpayment exceed $100, no later than 45 days after each tax installment is due.
6727936.quote: No later than 45 days after the date on which each installment of real property tax is due pursuant to paragraph (b) of subdivision 2 of section 1519-a of the charter, the department of finance shall send a notification to each owner of real property with an assessed value of two hundred fifty thousand dollars or less where the amount of tax liens arising as a result of the nonpayment of taxes on such property exceeds $100.
6727936.deadline_text: No later than 45 days after the date on which each installment of real property tax is due
affected_groups: property owners with assessed value of $250,000 or less

6727936.action_summary: Send a notification to each owner of real property with assessed value exceeding $250,000 where tax liens from nonpayment exceed $100, no later than 45 days after each tax installment is due.
6727936.quote: No later than 45 days after the date on which each installment of real property tax is due pursuant to paragraph (b) of subdivision 3 of section 1519-a of the charter, the department of finance shall send a notification to each owner of real property with an assessed value of more than two hundred fifty thousand dollars where the amount of tax liens arising as a result of the nonpayment of taxes on such property exceeds $100.
6727936.deadline_text: No later than 45 days after the date on which each installment of real property tax is due
affected_groups: property owners with assessed value exceeding $250,000

6727936.action_summary: Compile a list of properties included in notice of sale at least two times in preceding four notices, classified as class two multiple dwellings with cumulative lien-to-value ratio of at least 15%, no less than ninety days preceding tax lien sale.
6727936.quote: Not less than ninety days preceding the date of sale of a tax lien or tax liens, the commissioner of finance shall compile a list that includes any property that: (i) has been included in the notice of sale required pursuant to subdivision a of this section at least two times in the preceding four notices of sale published pursuant to such subdivision a; and (ii) is a multiple dwelling classified as class two
6727936.deadline_text: Not less than ninety days preceding the date of sale of a tax lien or tax liens
affected_groups: property owners of multiple dwellings classified as class two

6727936.action_summary: Transmit the compiled list of properties to the department of housing preservation and development for housing inspections.
6727936.quote: Upon compilation of such list, the commissioner of finance shall transmit such list to the department of housing preservation and development
affected_groups: property owners of multiple dwellings classified as class two

6727936.actor_raw: the department of housing preservation and development
6727936.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
6727936.action_summary: Inspect each property on the list provided by the department of finance for violations of the housing maintenance code, making best efforts to conduct inspections prior to the tax lien sale date.
6727936.quote: the department of housing preservation and development shall inspect each property on such list for violations of the housing maintenance code, as appropriate, provided that such property has not been inspected by such department within the past year pursuant to: (i) paragraph (2) of subdivision (b) of section 27-2033.1; (ii) section 27-2041.2; (iii) subdivision (c) of section 27-2091; (iv) section 27-2153; (v) article seven-A of the real property actions and proceedings law; or (vi) any other enhanced enforcement program established to secure compliance with the requirements of the housing maintenance code or other state or local laws imposing maintenance requirements on dwellings. The department of housing preservation and development shall make best efforts to conduct such inspections prior to the date of sale of a tax lien on a list compiled pursuant to this subdivision.
affected_groups: property owners of multiple dwellings classified as class two

6727936.actor_raw: the department of housing preservation and development
6727936.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
6727936.action_summary: Distribute a notice regarding the department's housing information guide to all dwelling units within each inspected property.
6727936.quote: During the course of any such inspection, such department shall distribute a notice regarding such department's housing information guide to all dwelling units within such property. Any notice required by this subdivision shall also be available in any of the designated citywide languages as defined in section 23-1101.

6727936.actor_raw: the department of housing preservation and development
6727936.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
6727936.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council a rental watchlist report no later than 120 days after the date of sale, providing property details and housing maintenance code violations for each inspected property.
6727936.quote: No later than one hundred twenty days after the date of sale, the department of housing preservation and development shall submit to the speaker of the council a rental watchlist report that provides, for each property inspected pursuant to paragraph three of this subdivision: (i) the borough, block, lot number, and address for such property, (ii) the number of apartment units and the owner of record for such property, and (iii) a description of all housing maintenance code violations issued for such property, if any.
6727936.deadline_text: No later than one hundred twenty days after the date of sale

6727936.action_summary: Submit a report to the speaker of the council no less than ninety days preceding the tax lien sale listing any property designated as vacant land on the final assessment roll.
6727936.quote: Not less than ninety days preceding the date of sale, the commissioner of finance shall submit a report to the speaker of the council including any property that has been included in the notice of sale required pursuant to subdivision a of this section and that is designated as vacant land on the final assessment roll delivered most recently to the council pursuant to section 11-218 of this title
6727936.deadline_text: Not less than ninety days preceding the date of sale

6727936.action_summary: Submit to the council lists disaggregated by council district of all properties noticed for sale no later than 90, 60, 30, and 10 days prior to the date of sale, containing detailed property information and lien amounts.
6727936.quote: Not later than ninety days, sixty days, thirty days and ten days prior to the date of sale of a tax lien or tax liens, the department of finance shall submit to the council a list, disaggregated by council district, of all properties noticed for sale pursuant to paragraph 1 of subdivision b of this section containing the following information for each property on such list: (a) the street address and the borough, block, and lot of such property; (b) the property owners of record; (c) the community board and community board district within which such property is located; (d) the amount that, if paid, would render the tax lien or tax liens on such property ineligible to be sold in accordance with section 11-319 of this chapter; and (e) the sum of the tax lien or tax liens on such property, disaggregated by the amount of the lien arising from the nonpayment of property taxes, the amount of any lien arising from the nonpayment of water and sewer charges, provided that the department of environmental protection has provided such information to the department of finance, the amount of any lien arising from emergency repair program charges, and the amount of any other lien that contributes to the sum of the tax lien or tax liens on the property.
6727936.deadline_text: Not later than ninety days, sixty days, thirty days and ten days prior to the date of sale

6727936.action_summary: Submit to the council no later than 120 days after the tax lien sale a list of all properties noticed for sale with a description of their disposition, including reasons for removal from sale.
6727936.quote: No later than one hundred twenty days after the [tax lien] date of sale, the commissioner of finance shall submit to the council a list of all properties, identified by block and lot, noticed for sale pursuant to subdivision b of this section. Such list shall also include a description of the disposition of such properties that shall include, but not be limited to, [whether an owner entered into a payment plan with the city pursuant to section 11-322 or 11-322.1 of this chapter, whether an owner satisfied the tax lien or liens, whether ownership of the property was transferred, provided that such information is available to the city, or whether the property was distressed, as defined in subdivision four of section 11-401 of this title, or removed from the sale pursuant to the discretion of the commissioner of the department of housing preservation and development] the sum of the tax lien or tax liens noticed for sale, disaggregated by the groups of properties described in subparagraphs (i) and (ii) of paragraph 1 of subdivision h of this section; the reasons provided for removal of any tax lien from a tax lien sale, based on records maintained by the department of finance, including but not limited to, payment, entry into installment agreement, and removal pursuant to section 11-412.3 of this title.
6727936.deadline_text: No later than one hundred twenty days after the [tax lien] date of sale

6727936.action_summary: Conduct outreach sessions in the ten council districts with the greatest number of properties noticed for sale, with additional sessions in the five council districts with the greatest number of such properties, providing information about tax lien sale processes, exemptions, and installment agreements.
6727936.quote: the commissioner of finance, in consultation with the commissioner of housing preservation and development and the commissioner of environmental protection, may conduct outreach sessions in the district of such council member, provided, however, that, the commissioner of finance shall conduct such outreach sessions in the ten council districts with the greatest number of properties for which a notice of intention to sell a tax lien has been mailed ninety days prior to the date of sale pursuant to paragraph one of subdivision b of this section, and provided, further, however, that, such commissioner shall conduct additional outreach sessions in the five council districts with the greatest number of properties for which a notice of intention to sell a tax lien has been mailed ninety days prior to the date of sale pursuant to such paragraph.

6727936.actor_raw: the commissioner of housing preservation and development
6727936.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
6727936.action_summary: Beginning July 1, 2024, make good faith efforts to contact owners of class one and class two residential properties noticed for tax lien sale to inform them of homeownership counseling and support services and assist in submitting applications for exemptions or benefits.
6727936.quote: Beginning July first, two thousand twenty-four, the commissioner of housing preservation and development, in consultation with the commissioner of finance and the commissioner of environmental protection, shall make good faith efforts to establish a procedure to contact the owner of record of any class one property or class two property that is a residential condominium or residential cooperative that has been included in the notice of sale required pursuant to subdivision a of this section, and any other person who has registered pursuant to section 11-309 of this chapter or who has provided notice to the commissioner of finance pursuant to section 11-416 or section 11-417 of this title in relation to such property, to inform them of relevant homeownership counseling and support services that the city, or a not-for-profit organization identified by the commissioner of housing preservation and development, provides and to assist in submitting any application for any exemption, credit or other benefit that would operate to exclude the property from a tax lien sale.
6727936.deadline_text: Beginning July first, two thousand twenty-four
affected_groups: property owners of class one and class two residential properties

6727936.actor_raw: the commissioner of housing preservation and development
6727936.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
6727936.action_summary: Provide a report to the speaker of the council no later than one year after enactment and annually thereafter regarding outreach activities conducted to contact property owners about homeownership counseling and support services.
6727936.quote: No later than one year after the enactment of the local law that added this subdivision, and annually thereafter, the commissioner of housing preservation and development shall provide a report to the speaker of the council regarding the outreach described in this subdivision that was conducted during the prior year, including a summary of the outreach activities and the number of homeowners reached.
6727936.deadline_text: No later than one year after the enactment of the local law that added this subdivision, and annually thereafter

6727936.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing procedures for requesting removal of a tax lien from a tax lien sale and appealing denials of such requests.
6727936.quote: The department shall promulgate rules establishing procedures for requesting that a tax lien or tax liens on a property or a dwelling unit be removed from a sale of tax liens and appealing a denial of a request that a tax lien or tax liens on a property or a dwelling unit be removed from a sale of tax liens. Such rules may include a time period within which the department will respond to a request, by an owner of a property or a dwelling unit, that such tax lien or tax liens be removed, a time period within which an owner could appeal a denial of such request, and a time period within which such department will respond to such appeal.

6727936.actor_raw: the department of housing preservation and development
6727936.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
6727936.action_summary: Select a qualified preservation purchaser for properties subject to summary foreclosure actions, using methods the department determines will best meet the purposes of the selection process.
6727936.quote: The department of housing preservation and development shall select a qualified preservation purchaser by any method it determines will best meet the purposes of such selection process, including, without limitation, selection by a request for qualifications process, a request for proposals process, a pre-qualified list, a request for offer process, or by direct selection of an entity determined by such department to be qualified.

6727936.action_summary: Notify the owner of a property about the option to elect summary foreclosure action within 30 days after the date of sale of a tax lien.
6727936.quote: the department, in consultation with the department of housing preservation and development, shall notify the owner of a property about the option to elect to subject the tax lien or tax liens on such property to the summary foreclosure action set forth in section 11-412.5 within 30 days after the date of sale, as defined in subdivision e of section 11-320 of this title, of such tax lien or tax liens on such property.
6727936.deadline_text: within 30 days after the date of sale
affected_groups: property owners of class one properties

6727936.action_summary: Develop forms for property owners to certify their election of summary foreclosure action, and for qualified preservation purchasers to commit to lease terms, regulatory agreements, and note execution.
6727936.quote: The department shall develop forms in which: 1. the owner of a property shall certify: (i) their election to subject the tax lien or tax liens on such property to the summary foreclosure action set forth in section 11-412.5 of this chapter; (ii) that such election has been made after consultation with an attorney; (iii) their election to forego the option to interpose an answer to such action; and (iv) their decision to forego any further option to pay all unpaid tax lien or tax liens on such property together with interest thereon;
affected_groups: property owners of class one properties

6727936.actor_raw: the department of finance or another agency designated by the mayor
6727936.action_summary: Subject to appropriations, make available the services of an attorney to property owners electing summary foreclosure action at no cost to satisfy the attorney consultation requirement.
6727936.quote: Subject to appropriations, the department, or another agency designated by the mayor, shall make available the services of an attorney to an owner of property who elects to subject the tax lien or tax liens on such property to the summary foreclosure action for the purpose of satisfying the requirement described in paragraph 5 of subdivision b of this section and shall make available such services at no cost to such owner.
affected_groups: property owners of class one properties

6727936.action_summary: Prepare a notice of summary foreclosure action upon receipt of signed and notarized forms and completion of reasonable efforts to confirm no other mortgages, liens, or encumbrances exist on the property.
6727936.quote: Upon receipt by the commissioner of finance of signed and notarized copies of the forms described in subdivision e of section 11-412.4 of this chapter, and upon the completion of reasonable efforts by the commissioner of finance to confirm that there are no mortgages, liens or encumbrances on the property that is the subject of the summary foreclosure action, the commissioner of finance shall prepare a notice of the summary foreclosure action.

6727936.action_summary: File two duplicate originals of the notice of summary foreclosure action, verified by the commissioner or designee, in the office of the county clerk in the county where the property is situated.
6727936.quote: Two duplicate originals of the notice of the summary foreclosure action, prepared pursuant to subdivision a of this section, verified by the commissioner of finance or a subordinate designated by the commissioner, shall be filed in the office of the clerk of the county in which the property is situated.

6727936.action_summary: File a copy of each notice of summary foreclosure action, certified as a copy by the commissioner or designee, in the borough office of the department of finance and in the office of the corporation counsel.
6727936.quote: The commissioner of finance shall file a copy of each notice of the summary foreclosure action, certified as such copy by him or her or a subordinate designated by the commissioner, in the borough office of the department of finance in the borough in which the property listed therein is situated and in the office of the corporation counsel.

6727936.action_summary: Cause a notice of foreclosure to be posted on the department's website and published in the City Record and designated newspaper for 6 successive weeks.
6727936.quote: Upon the filing of a notice of the summary foreclosure action in the office of the county clerk, the commissioner of finance forthwith shall cause a notice of foreclosure to be posted on the department's website for 6 successive weeks and published at least once a week for 6 successive weeks in the City Record and, subject to section 91 of the judiciary law, in 1 newspaper, which may be a law journal, to be designated by the commissioner of finance, which is published in and is circulated throughout the county in which the affected property is located.

6727936.action_summary: Cause a copy of the notice of foreclosure to be posted in the office of the commissioner of finance, the county courthouse, and 3 other conspicuous places in the borough where the property is located.
6727936.quote: The commissioner of finance shall cause a copy of such notice of foreclosure to be posted in the office of the commissioner of finance, in the county courthouse of the county in which the property subject to the summary foreclosure action is situated and at 3 other conspicuous places in the borough in which the affected property is located.

6727936.action_summary: Publish on its website the declaration and agreement of trust, purchase agreements, servicing agreements, paying agent and custody agreement, indentures, bonds, bond purchase agreements, and certificate of trust for any trust created for tax lien sale purposes no later than August 1, 2024.
6727936.quote: For each trust created by the city or in which the city has an ownership or residual interest for the purposes of a negotiated sale pursuant to paragraph 2 of subdivision b of section 11-319 of the administrative code of the city of New York that was established on or before July 1, 2024, the department of finance shall, no later than August 1, 2024, publish on its website the following documents: 1. The declaration and agreement of trust, as such declaration and agreement may have been amended or restated; 2. Any purchase agreements, servicing agreements, paying agent and custody agreement, copies of any indenture or bonds, and bond purchase agreements, as each of such documents may have been amended or restated; and 3. The certificate of trust filed with the secretary of state of New York.

6727936.action_summary: Publish on its website the documents described in Section 27 for any trust created after July 1, 2024 no later than 30 days after the effective date of each document.
6727936.quote: For any such trust created by the city or in which the city has an ownership or residual interest for the purposes of a negotiated sale pursuant to paragraph 2 of subdivision b of section 11-319 of the administrative code of the city of New York that is established after July 1, 2024, the department of finance shall publish on its website the documents described in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of subdivision b of this section no later than 30 days after the effective date of each such document.
6727936.deadline_text: no later than 30 days after the effective date of each such document

6727936.action_summary: Establish a temporary task force to review effects of tax lien sale trusts and recommend reforms to ensure efficient and fair collection, reduce repeated sales, preserve affordable housing, and improve transparency.
6727936.quote: The mayor and council shall establish a temporary task force to review the task force subjects of inquiry.

6727936.action_summary: Hold an initial meeting no later than September 15, 2024 and thereafter meet at least monthly to review, evaluate, and make recommendations regarding tax lien sale trusts and related legislative amendments.
6727936.quote: No later than September 15, 2024, the task force shall hold its initial meeting and thereafter shall meet at least monthly, except as otherwise determined by such task force, to review, evaluate and make recommendations for legislative amendments and changes in administrative policy in relation to the task force subjects of inquiry and such other matters as the task force deems appropriate.

6727936.action_summary: Hold a public hearing no later than May 1, 2025 to receive written and in-person comments and testimony, making preliminary recommendations publicly available at least 20 days prior.
6727936.quote: No later than May 1, 2025, the task force shall hold a public hearing to receive written and in-person comments and testimony. The task force's preliminary recommendations shall be made publicly available at least twenty days prior to such public hearing.

6727936.action_summary: Submit written recommendations to the mayor and speaker of the council no later than September 15, 2025 regarding task force subjects of inquiry including effects of tax lien sale trusts and potential reforms.
6727936.quote: No later than September 15, 2025, the temporary task force shall submit written recommendations to the mayor and the speaker of the council regarding task force subjects of inquiry.

6727936.action_summary: Mail bills for taxes, charges and assessments to all owners who have notified the department in writing or electronically of their mailing address, or to the owner of record at the property address if no mailing address is provided.
6727936.quote: The commissioner of finance shall mail bills for taxes, charges and assessments to all owners who have notified the commissioner of finance in writing or electronically of the owner's mailing address for communications from the commissioner, at the address so provided, or, if no mailing address has been so provided, to the owner of record at the property address, if any, appearing in the latest assessment roll, but the failure of the commissioner of finance so to mail such bill shall not invalidate or otherwise affect the tax, charge or assessment represented thereby nor prevent the accruing of any interest or penalty imposed for the non-payment thereof, nor prevent or stay proceedings under this chapter, nor affect the title of the plaintiff or any purchaser under such proceedings.

6727936.action_summary: Mail notice of foreclosure and any other process to all owners who have notified the department in writing or electronically of their mailing address whenever a property is included in a list of delinquent taxes.
6727936.quote: The commissioner of finance shall also mail notice of foreclosure and any other process required by this chapter to all owners who have notified the commissioner of finance in writing or electronically of the owner's mailing address for communications from the commissioner, at the address so provided, whenever a property is included in a list of delinquent taxes filed pursuant to this chapter. The failure to receive such notice or process as herein provided shall not affect the validity of any action or proceeding brought pursuant to this chapter.

6727936.action_summary: Mail notice of foreclosure and any other process to each person who has notified the department in writing or electronically of an interest in real property and requested notice at a designated address, whenever a property with that person's interest is included in a list of delinquent taxes.
6727936.quote: The commissioner of finance shall mail a notice of foreclosure and any other process required by this chapter to each person who is not entitled to have tax bills mailed to such person by the commissioner of finance, but who has notified the commissioner of finance in writing or electronically that he or she has an interest in real property, including the interest of a mortgagee, lienor or encumbrancer, and who has requested the commissioner of finance to mail a notice to him or her at a designated mailing address, at the address so provided, whenever the property in which the person has an interest is included in a list of delinquent taxes filed pursuant to this chapter.

6727936.actor_raw: the commissioners of finance and environmental protection
6727936.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing procedures for property owners to enter into installment agreements for the payment of delinquent real property taxes, assessments, sewer rents, sewer surcharges, water rents, and other charges made a lien.
6727936.quote: In accordance with rules promulgated by the commissioners of finance and environmental protection, a property owner, or other eligible person, as defined by rule, acting on behalf of an owner, may enter into agreements with the departments of finance and environmental protection for the payment in installments of any delinquent real property taxes, assessments, sewer rents, sewer surcharges, water rents, or any other charges that are made a lien subject to the provisions of this chapter, provided that any agreement with the department of environmental protection shall be subject to title 2-A of article 5 of the public authorities law and the rules of the New York city water board.

6727936.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing a process for an applicant to make the demonstration required for renewal of a fixed length income-based installment agreement by self-certification.
6727936.quote: The department may promulgate rules that establish a process for an applicant to make the demonstration required by paragraph 2 of this subdivision by self-certification.
affected_groups: property owners with low to moderate income

6727936.actor_raw: an agency designated by the mayor
6727936.action_summary: Determine which properties designated as vacant land have development that is economically impracticable or infeasible due to size, shape, zoning, configuration, or topography.
6727936.quote: real property that is designated as vacant land on the final assessment roll delivered most recently to the council pursuant to section 11-218 of this title and that an agency designated by the mayor determines the development of which is economically impracticable or infeasible, due to the size, shape, applicable zoning, configuration or topography of such property

6729133.action_summary: Provide to the council and publish on its website a report regarding recidivism and probation violations, including specified data on probationers' arrests, convictions, compliance, and outcomes, disaggregated by age, case type, and risk level.
6729133.quote: By January 30, 2026, and no later than June 30 and January 30 thereafter, the department shall provide to the council and publish on its website a report regarding recidivism and probation violations.
6729133.deadline_text: By January 30, 2026, and no later than June 30 and January 30 thereafter

7126859.action_summary: Provide access to benefits and services to every person with HIV who requests assistance.
7126859.quote: There shall be a division [of AIDS services] within the New York city department of social services[. Such division shall] to provide access to benefits and services, as defined in section 21-128(a)(1) [of this chapter], to every person [with clinical/symptomatic HIV illness, as determined by the New York state department of health AIDS institute, or with AIDS, as defined by the federal centers for disease control and prevention,] with HIV who requests assistance

7126859.action_summary: Direct staff of the division to provide intensive case management with specified caseworker-to-client ratios and transportation and nutrition allowances to persons with HIV satisfying medicaid income eligibility requirements.
7126859.quote: The commissioner shall direct staff of the division established pursuant to section 21-126 to provide to persons with HIV who satisfy the income eligibility requirements for medicaid as set forth in section 1396 et. seq. of title 42 of the United States code: (i) intensive case management with an average ratio which shall not exceed 1 caseworker or supervisor to 25 family cases, and with an overall average ratio for all cases which shall not exceed 1 caseworker or supervisor to 34 cases; and (ii) transportation and nutrition allowances.

7126859.action_summary: Establish criteria within 30 days of effective date pursuant to which an applicant shall be entitled to a home or hospital visit for the purpose of establishing eligibility and applying for benefits and services.
7126859.quote: Within 30 days of the effective date of the local law that added this section, the commissioner shall establish criteria pursuant to which an applicant shall be entitled to a home or hospital visit for the purpose of establishing eligibility and applying for benefits and services.
7126859.deadline_text: Within [thirty] 30 days of the effective date of the local law that added this section

7126859.action_summary: Provide every person with HIV who applies for benefits and services with a receipt on the day of application or submission of documents, including date, description of information received, and statement of completeness.
7126859.quote: Upon written or oral application to the division for benefits and services or submission of documents required to establish eligibility for benefits and services by a person with HIV, such person shall immediately be provided with a receipt which shall include, but not be limited to, the date, a description of the information received, and a statement as to whether any application for such benefits and services is complete or incomplete, and if incomplete, such receipt shall identify any information or documents needed in order for the application to be deemed complete.

7126859.action_summary: Provide every homeless client determined eligible for services with an application for medically appropriate non-emergency housing and information regarding financial assistance and housing options on the day eligibility is determined.
7126859.quote: Unless the client shall decline, the division shall provide the following to every homeless client of the division on the day the client is determined to be eligible for services as a client of the division: [(i)] (1) an application for medically appropriate non-emergency housing; and [(ii)] (2) information regarding financial assistance available to assist eligible clients in obtaining housing and regarding available housing options.

7126859.action_summary: Ensure every client receives assistance needed to complete the application for medically appropriate non-emergency housing within 10 business days of the day the client is determined eligible for division services.
7126859.quote: The division shall ensure that every client receives any assistance needed to complete the application for medically appropriate non-emergency housing within 10 business days of the day on which the client is determined to be eligible for services as a client of the division.
7126859.deadline_text: within 10 business days of the day on which the client is determined to be eligible for services as a client of the division

7126859.action_summary: Provide every client eligible for non-emergency housing with a referral to an available medically appropriate non-emergency housing option within 90 days of initial placement in emergency housing or completion of physical documentation, whichever is sooner.
7126859.quote: Within 90 days of initial placement in emergency housing or of completion of the physical documentation required from the client for the application for non-emergency housing, whichever is sooner, the division must provide every client who is eligible for non-emergency housing a referral to an available medically appropriate non-emergency housing option, which takes into consideration the medical, educational and familial needs and social circumstances of the client, to the extent such option is available.
7126859.deadline_text: Within 90 days of initial placement in emergency housing or of completion of the physical documentation required from the client for the application for non-emergency housing, whichever is sooner

7126859.action_summary: Provide a referral to another medically appropriate non-emergency housing option for any client who remains homeless or in emergency housing for over 45 days after housing referral requirements have been met.
7126859.quote: For any client who remains homeless or in emergency housing for over 45 days after the requirements of subparagraph (c) of this paragraph or the requirements of this subparagraph have been met, the division shall provide a referral to another medically appropriate non-emergency housing option, to the extent such option is available.

7126859.action_summary: Prepare a draft policy and procedures manual for division staff within 60 days of effective date, including guidelines on confidentiality, medical/psychological needs, application procedures, eligibility standards, mandated time periods for benefits and services, and advocacy resources.
7126859.quote: [Not] No later than [sixty] 60 days from the effective date of the local law that added this section, the commissioner shall prepare a draft policy and procedures manual for division staff. Such policy and procedures manual shall include, but not be limited to, strict guidelines on maintaining the confidentiality of the identity of and information relating to all applicants and recipients, instructional materials relating to the medical and psychological needs of persons with [clinical/symptomatic HIV illness or with AIDS] HIV, application procedures, eligibility standards, mandated time periods for the provision of each benefit and service available to applicants and recipients and advocacy resources available to persons with [clinical/symptomatic HIV illness or with AIDS] HIV.
7126859.deadline_text: No later than [sixty] 60 days from the effective date of the local law that added this section

7126859.action_summary: Update the list of advocacy resources in the policy and procedures manual on a semi-annual basis.
7126859.quote: Such list of advocacy resources shall be updated semi-annually.

7126859.action_summary: Distribute the draft policy and procedures manual to contracted social service agencies and other appropriate entities within 30 days of preparation and hold at least one noticed public hearing at an accessible site before preparing the final manual.
7126859.quote: Within [thirty] 30 days following the preparation of such draft policy and procedure manual and prior to the preparation of a final policy and procedures manual, the commissioner shall distribute such draft policy and procedure manual to all social service agencies and organizations that contract with the department to provide HIV-related services and to all others whom the commissioner deems appropriate, and hold no fewer than [one] 1 noticed public hearing at a site accessible to [the disabled] individuals with disabilities, at which advocates, service providers, persons who have tested positive for HIV, and any other member of the public shall be given an opportunity to comment on such draft policy and procedures manual.
7126859.deadline_text: Within [thirty] 30 days following the preparation of such draft policy and procedure manual

7126859.action_summary: Prepare a final policy and procedures manual within 30 days after conclusion of the public hearing and thereafter review and revise on an annual basis.
7126859.quote: The commissioner shall prepare a final policy and procedures manual within 30 days after the conclusion of such hearing and shall thereafter review and where appropriate, revise such policy and procedures manual on an annual basis.
7126859.deadline_text: within [thirty] 30 days after the conclusion of such hearing

7126859.action_summary: Provide semi-annual training to all division staff using the policy and procedures manual.
7126859.quote: The commissioner shall provide for semi-annual training, using such policy and procedures manual, for all division staff.

7126859.action_summary: Publish a proposed rule establishing a bill of rights for persons with HIV within 60 days of effective date, including benefits and services, timetables, file examination rights, home/hospital visit rights, hearing process, and anti-discrimination remedies.
7126859.quote: [Not] No later than [sixty] 60 days from the effective date of the local law that added this section, the commissioner shall publish a proposed rule establishing a bill of rights for persons with [clinical/symptomatic HIV illness or with AIDS] HIV. Such draft bill of rights shall include, but not be limited to, an explanation of the benefits and services for which persons with [clinical/symptomatic HIV illness or with AIDS] HIV may be eligible; timetables within which such benefits and services shall be provided to eligible persons; an explanation of an applicant's and recipient's right to examine [his or her] such applicant's and recipient's file and the procedure for disputing any information contained therein; an explanation of an applicant's and recipient's right to a home or hospital visit for the purpose of applying for or maintaining benefits or services; an explanation of the process for requesting a division conference or New York state fair hearing; and a summary of the rights and remedies for the redress of discrimination as provided for in title [eight of this code] 8.
7126859.deadline_text: No later than [sixty] 60 days from the effective date of the local law that added this section

7126859.action_summary: Hold at least one noticed public hearing at an accessible site within 60 days following publication of the proposed bill of rights rule, allowing advocates, service providers, persons with HIV, and the public to comment.
7126859.quote: Within 60 days following the publication of such proposed rule, and prior to the publication of a final rule, the commissioner shall hold no fewer than 1 noticed public hearing at a site accessible to individuals with disabilities at which advocates, service providers, persons who have tested positive for HIV, and any other member of the public shall be given an opportunity to comment on such draft bill of rights.
7126859.deadline_text: Within [sixty] 60 days following the publication of such proposed rule

7126859.action_summary: Publish a final bill of rights rule within 30 days after conclusion of the public hearing and thereafter review and revise on an annual basis.
7126859.quote: The commissioner shall publish a final rule within 30 days after the conclusion of such hearing and shall thereafter review, and where appropriate, revise such bill of rights on an annual basis.
7126859.deadline_text: within [thirty] 30 days after the conclusion of such hearing

7126859.action_summary: Post the bill of rights conspicuously in all division offices open to the public and make available for distribution in English, Spanish, and any other languages deemed appropriate.
7126859.quote: Such bill of rights shall be conspicuously posted in all division offices that are open to the public and shall be available for distribution to the public in English, Spanish and any other languages that the commissioner deems appropriate.

7126859.action_summary: Establish a policy or procedure for overseeing and monitoring the delivery of services to persons with HIV within 90 days of effective date, including quality assurance measurements.
7126859.quote: [Not] No later than [ninety] 90 days from the effective date of the local law that added this section, the commissioner shall establish a policy or procedure for overseeing and monitoring the delivery of services required pursuant to this section to persons with [clinical/symptomatic HIV illness or with AIDS] HIV which shall include, but not be limited to, quality assurance measurements.
7126859.deadline_text: No later than [ninety] 90 days from the effective date of the local law that added this section

7126859.quote: The commissioner shall submit such policy or procedure to the mayor and the council in writing within 10 days from the date such policy or procedure is established.

7126859.quote: The commissioner shall submit written, quarterly reports to the mayor and the speaker of the council no later than 60 days after the last day of the time period covered by the report and shall, at a minimum, provide the following information:

7258693.quote: Within 14 days of receipt of a covered complaint, the department shall make its best effort to inspect the building to which such complaint pertains for signs of rat activity or conditions that attract rats
7258693.deadline_text: Within 14 days of receipt of a covered complaint

7258693.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
7258693.action_summary: Record inspection information including date, address, pass/fail determination, violations or abatement orders issued, and inspector observations during rat and rat-attractant inspections.
7258693.quote: During an inspection, the department shall record the following information: 1. The date of the inspection; 2. The street address of the building so inspected; 3. Whether such building passed or failed such inspection, as determined by the department; 4. If any notice of violation relating to the presence of rats or order to abate a condition related to the presence of rats is issued to the person in charge of such building in response to such inspection, the number of such notices of violation or orders to abate so issued; and 5. The inspector's observations of signs of rats or conditions that attract rats during such inspection or any subsequent inspection.

7258693.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
7258693.action_summary: Make publicly available on a website inspection information collected during rat and rat-attractant inspections, viewable by address or through an interactive map.
7258693.quote: Within 30 days of completing an inspection pursuant to subdivision b of this section, or pursuant to any other lawful rat mitigation program inspection conducted by the department related to rats or conditions that attract rats, the department shall make publicly available on a website the information collected during such inspection
7258693.deadline_text: Within 30 days of completing an inspection

7292040.action_summary: Make available holistic clinical assessments for covered persons upon their request, their attorney's request, or when required for acceptance to a court-based alternative to incarceration program.

7292040.deadline_text: within 3 weeks of the referral, except that if such assessment requires complex analysis including but not limited to psychological testing for intellectual disabilities, an assessment of the risk of violence of such covered person, documentation of domestic violence and abuse history or other complex history and needs, such assessment shall be provided within 6 weeks of such referral

7292040.action_summary: Provide all material information collected during the jail population review to covered persons' attorneys as early as practicable.

7315779.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

7861459.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation

7861459.actor_raw: the commissioner or the commissioner's designee
7861459.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation

7861459.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation

7861459.actor_raw: the commissioner or the commissioner's designee

7861459.actor_raw: the commissioner or the commissioner's designee
