3458226.deadline_text: no later than 180 days from the date of the application

3458226.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
3458226.action_summary: Specify conditions for authorizing on-street bus stops for sight-seeing buses and revoke authorizations for violations of such conditions.
3458226.quote: When authorizing one or more on-street bus stops for sight-seeing buses, the commissioner shall specify the conditions on which such authorization is based.

3458226.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
3458226.action_summary: Notify the commissioner of consumer affairs of any revocations of sight-seeing bus stop authorizations as soon as practicable.
3458226.quote: The commissioner shall notify the commissioner of consumer affairs of any such revocations as soon as practicable.

3458226.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
3458226.action_summary: Establish criteria by rule under which sight-seeing bus companies that possess on-street bus stop authorizations prior to the effective date may be issued an authorization to use such bus stops for a period of up to three years from the effective date.
3458226.quote: The commissioner shall by rule establish criteria under which sight-seeing bus companies that possess on-street bus stop authorizations prior to the effective date of this section may be issued an authorization

3458226.actor_raw: the commissioner of transportation and the commissioner of consumer affairs
3458226.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
3458226.action_summary: Promulgate rules and take measures as necessary for the implementation of this local law.
3458226.quote: the commissioner of transportation and the commissioner of consumer affairs shall take such measures as are necessary for the implementation of this local law, including the promulgation of rules, before such date

3458226.actor_raw: the commissioner of transportation and the commissioner of consumer affairs
3458226.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
3458226.action_summary: Promulgate rules and take measures as necessary for the implementation of this local law.
3458226.quote: the commissioner of transportation and the commissioner of consumer affairs shall take such measures as are necessary for the implementation of this local law, including the promulgation of rules, before such date

3458226.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
3458226.action_summary: Notify the commissioner of transportation of each sight-seeing bus license that is suspended or revoked.
3458226.quote: The commissioner shall, as soon as practicable, notify the commissioner of transportation of each sight-seeing bus license that is suspended or revoked.

7824705.action_summary: Ensure that one or more searchable and publicly accessible online interfaces provide information about each procurement exceeding small purchase limits, including contracting process identifiers, agency names, procurement summaries, solicitation details, contract awards, and expenditure summaries.
7824705.quote: The city chief procurement officer shall ensure that one or more searchable and publicly accessible online interfaces provide information about each procurement that exceeds the small purchase limits as set pursuant to the authority and procedure set forth in subdivision a of section 314 of the charter
7824705.deadline_text: within 30 days of the occurrence of the relevant procurement event, except that information required by paragraph 3 of subdivision b shall be published no later than 15 days prior to the release of a solicitation document

7717530.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
7717530.action_summary: Execute agreements regarding covered projects for income bands so that at least 50 percent of aggregate dwelling units created are affordable for extremely low-income and very low-income households, with at least 30 percent affordable for extremely low-income households.
7717530.quote: the department shall execute agreements regarding covered projects for income bands so that at least 50 percent of the aggregate number of dwelling units so created shall be affordable for extremely low-income households and very low-income households, provided that at least 30 percent of such aggregate dwelling unit count shall be affordable for extremely low-income households.

7717530.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
7717530.action_summary: Demonstrate compliance with the requirements of sections 26-3802 and 26-3803 as part of the long-term housing needs assessment required by the charter.
7717530.quote: As part of the long-term housing needs assessment required by subdivision c of section 16-a of the charter, the department shall demonstrate compliance with the requirements of sections 26-3802 and 26-3803.

7717530.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
7717530.action_summary: Notify in writing the speaker of the council and each borough president of adjustments to percentages that the department intends to make, at least 90 days prior to issuing such determination.
7717530.quote: Ninety days prior to issuing such determination, the department shall notify in writing the speaker of the council and each borough president of the adjustments that the department intends to make pursuant to this section.
7717530.deadline_text: Ninety days prior to issuing such determination

6509477.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6509477.action_summary: Establish a program to implement curbside overnight parking areas for commercial vehicles within each industrial business zone where feasible.
6509477.quote: The department shall establish a program to implement a curbside overnight parking area for the exclusive use of commercial vehicles within each industrial business zone where the department determines such a program is feasible.

6509477.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6509477.action_summary: Allow commercial vehicles to park for at least 10 continuous hours in overnight parking areas, with hours of operation between 6:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m.
6509477.quote: allow commercial vehicles to park for at least 10 continuous hours, except that these overnight parking areas shall not be active between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.

6509477.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6509477.action_summary: Prohibit non-commercial vehicles from parking in overnight parking areas during hours when commercial vehicles are allowed to park.
6509477.quote: prohibit vehicles that are not commercial vehicles from parking in such area during such hours when commercial vehicles are allowed to park

6509477.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6509477.action_summary: Post signage in overnight parking areas indicating the allowance for commercial vehicles and prohibition of non-commercial vehicles.
6509477.quote: post signage indicating such allowance and prohibition.

6509477.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6509477.action_summary: Provide written notice to community boards and council members at least 30 days prior to implementing an overnight parking area.
6509477.quote: At least 30 days prior to the implementation of such an area, the department shall provide written notice to any community board representing the community district in which such industrial business zone is located, and to any council member in whose district such industrial business zone is located.
6509477.deadline_text: At least 30 days prior to the implementation of such an area

6509477.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6509477.action_summary: Upon request, discuss the implementation of overnight parking areas with community boards or council members prior to implementation.
6509477.quote: Upon a request, the department shall discuss such implementation with such community board or council member prior to such implementation.

6509477.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6509477.action_summary: Conduct outreach to commercial establishments and truck drivers to inform them of overnight parking area implementations.
6509477.quote: The department shall conduct outreach to commercial establishments within each industrial business zone and to commercial truck drivers who operate commercial vehicles within the city to inform them of the implementation of overnight parking areas

6509477.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6509477.action_summary: Submit an annual report to the mayor and speaker of the council and publish on its website regarding the use of overnight parking areas, including their locations, usage data, and assessment of effects.
6509477.quote: By June 1 of each year, the department shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and publish on its website, a report on the use of the overnight parking areas in industrial business zones implemented pursuant to subdivision b of this section.

6632641.action_summary: Designate an agency or an office within the executive office of the mayor to establish guidelines relating to the amount of insurance or type of insurance a food procurement vendor must carry.
6632641.quote: The mayor shall designate an agency or an office within the executive office of the mayor to establish guidelines relating to the amount of insurance or type of insurance a food procurement vendor must carry.

6632641.action_summary: Establish guidelines relating to the amount of insurance or type of insurance a food procurement vendor must carry, in consultation with the office of food policy, and provide a draft of any such guidelines or changes to the council at least 30 days prior to finalizing them.
6632641.quote: Such agency or office shall establish such guidelines in consultation with the office of food policy, and shall provide a draft of any such guidelines or changes to such guidelines to the council at least 30 days prior to finalizing them.
6632641.deadline_text: at least 30 days prior to finalizing them
6632641.agency_unit: Food Procurement Vendor Insurance Guidelines Office

6632641.actor_raw: The agency or office designated by the mayor
6632641.action_summary: Review the guidelines established pursuant to subdivision b every two years and revise such guidelines in accordance with such review.
6632641.quote: The agency or office designated by the mayor pursuant to subdivision b of this section shall review the guidelines established pursuant to such subdivision every two years and revise such guidelines in accordance with such review.

6695195.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
6695195.action_summary: Determine whether a proposed contract for standard or professional services valued over one million dollars would result in displacement of any city employee within the agency.
6695195.quote: Prior to issuing an invitation for bids, request for proposals, or other solicitation, or renewing or amending an existing contract, the agency shall determine whether such contract is the result of or would result in the displacement of any city employee within the agency.

6695195.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
6695195.action_summary: Include in any solicitation or contract renewal/amendment a signed certification by the agency head detailing the basis for determining that displacement would not occur, including information on civil service titles performing similar services, capacity analysis, and confirmation of no triggering events.
6695195.quote: If the agency determines that displacement would not occur, it shall include a certification to that effect, signed by the agency head, in any invitation for bids, request for proposals, or other solicitation, or with any contract renewal or amendment.

6695195.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
6695195.action_summary: Conduct a cost and benefits analysis comparing the costs and benefits of performing the service with city employees versus contracting it out, and submit this analysis with supporting documentation to the comptroller prior to issuance of any solicitation or contract renewal/amendment.
6695195.quote: If the agency determines that displacement would occur, the agency shall determine the costs incurred and the benefits derived in performing the service, consistent with the scope and specifications within the solicitation, renewal, or amendment, with city employees, and shall submit such analysis, with all supporting documentation, prior to issuance of any solicitation or entry into any contract renewal or amendment, to the comptroller.

6695195.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
6695195.action_summary: Submit the displacement determination, analysis, and supporting documentation to the city council and to appropriate collective bargaining representatives immediately upon receipt of bids or proposals, or prior to renewal or amendment of an existing contract.
6695195.quote: Immediately upon receipt of bids, proposals, and other solicitation responses, or prior to the renewal or amendment of an existing contract, the agency shall submit such determination, analysis, and supporting documentation to the council and to the appropriate collective bargaining representatives representing employees who would be affected pursuant to paragraph 1 of subdivision a of this section.

6695195.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
6695195.action_summary: Perform a comparative cost analysis comparing costs and benefits of contracting with a proposed vendor versus providing the service with city employees, and if the agency head intends to award the contract, submit the reasons, analysis, and supporting documentation to the comptroller, city council, and affected collective bargaining representatives.
6695195.quote: Prior to award of a contract, a renewal, or an amendment, the agency shall perform a comparative analysis of the costs expected to be incurred and the benefits expected to be derived from entering into, renewing, or amending a contract with the proposed vendor, based on such vendor's best and final offer, and such agency's analysis of the costs incurred and the benefits derived from providing the service with city employees. If the agency head intends to award, renew, or amend the contract, he or she shall submit the reasons therefor, together with such analysis, and all supporting documentation, to the comptroller, the council, and the appropriate collective bargaining representatives representing employees who would be affected pursuant to paragraph 1 of subdivision a of this section.

6695195.action_summary: Produce and publish on the mayor's office of contract services website by July 31st of each year a plan and schedule detailing each agency's anticipated contracting actions for the upcoming fiscal year, including information on solicitations and contract renewals or amendments.
6695195.quote: The mayor shall, no later than July 31st of each year, produce and publish on the mayor's office of contract services website a plan and schedule for each agency detailing the anticipated contracting actions of each such agency for the upcoming fiscal year.
6695195.deadline_text: no later than July 31st of each year

6695195.action_summary: Provide public notice ten days before an agency issues a solicitation or enters into a contract renewal or amendment that was not included in the annual plan or differs materially from it, posting the notice on the mayor's office of contract services website and in the city record.
6695195.quote: the mayor shall provide public notice ten days before such agency issues such invitation, request, or solicitation, or enters into such renewal or amendment. Such notice, which shall be posted on the website of the mayor's office of contract services and in the city record,
6695195.deadline_text: ten days before such agency issues such invitation, request, or solicitation, or enters into such renewal or amendment

6702301.action_summary: Submit the name of a nominee for a head of department subject to council advice and consent within 60 days following the occurrence of a vacancy.
6702301.quote: Within 60 days following the occurrence of a vacancy in the office of any head of department subject to the provisions of subdivision a, the mayor shall submit to the council the name of the mayor's nominee for such office.
6702301.deadline_text: Within 60 days following the occurrence of a vacancy

6702301.action_summary: Submit a new person for nomination to the council within 60 days of council disapproval of a mayoral nomination for a head of department subject to council advice and consent.
6702301.quote: If the council disapproves a nomination while the office is vacant, the mayor shall submit a new person for nomination to the council within 60 days of council disapproval.

6702301.action_summary: Make all reasonable efforts to ensure that a vacancy in a head of department subject to council advice and consent is filled through the nomination and council approval process within 120 days of the occurrence of the vacancy.
6702301.quote: The mayor shall make all reasonable efforts to ensure that the vacancy is filled through the process described in this subdivision within 120 days of the occurrence of the vacancy.
6702301.deadline_text: within 120 days of the occurrence of the vacancy

6702301.action_summary: Hold a hearing and act upon a nomination for a head of department or other position subject to council advice and consent within 30 days after the first stated meeting of the council after receipt of the nomination.
6702301.quote: Within 30 days after the first stated meeting of the council after receipt of a nomination, the council shall hold a hearing and act upon such nomination and in the event it does not act within such period, the nomination shall be deemed to be confirmed.
6702301.deadline_text: Within 30 days after the first stated meeting of the council after receipt of a nomination

6702301.action_summary: Take all necessary steps to effectuate the provisions of section 6 regarding submission of the local law for voter approval in accordance with law.
6702301.quote: The New York city clerk shall take all necessary steps to effectuate the provisions of this section in accordance with law.

6202971.action_summary: Submit a fair housing plan to the mayor and speaker of the council and post it on its website, including analysis of citywide fair housing data and policy goals and strategies to affirmatively further fair housing.
6202971.quote: the administrating agency shall submit a fair housing plan to the mayor and the speaker of the council and post such plan on its website. Such plan shall include, but need not be limited to:
6202971.deadline_text: no later than October 1, 2025 and every 5 years thereafter

6202971.action_summary: Conduct a citywide assessment of the total number of housing units, affordable housing units, deeply affordable housing units, and housing serving formerly homeless households needed to provide housing opportunity for all socio-economic levels.
6202971.quote: the administrating agency shall conduct a citywide assessment of the total number of housing units, affordable housing units, deeply affordable housing units, and housing serving formerly homeless households that such agency determines is needed
6202971.deadline_text: No later than 1 year after the date required for the submission of a fair housing plan

6202971.action_summary: Submit citywide 5-year housing production targets for total housing units, affordable housing units, deeply affordable housing units, housing serving formerly homeless households, and preservation of housing units to the mayor and speaker of the council and post on its website.
6202971.quote: the administrating agency shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council and post on its website: 1. A 5-year citywide housing production target for each of the following housing types
6202971.deadline_text: No later than 1 year after the submission of a fair housing plan

6202971.action_summary: Submit community district-level 5-year housing production targets for total housing units, affordable housing units, deeply affordable housing units, and housing serving formerly homeless households to the mayor and speaker of the council and post on its website.
6202971.quote: For each community district, 5-year housing production targets for the following housing types identified in paragraph 1 of this subdivision: total housing units; affordable housing units; deeply affordable housing units; and housing serving formerly homeless households.
6202971.deadline_text: No later than 1 year after the submission of a fair housing plan

6202971.action_summary: Submit a strategic equity framework assessing obstacles to and identifying goals and strategies for furthering fair housing citywide and across community districts to the mayor and speaker of the council and post on its website.
6202971.quote: the administrating agency shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council and post on its website a strategic equity framework that assesses obstacles to and identifies goals and strategies for furthering fair housing citywide and across community districts.
6202971.deadline_text: No later than 1 year after the submission of a fair housing plan

6202971.action_summary: Release a preliminary version of the fair housing plan at least 30 days before submission of the final plan.
6202971.quote: The administrating agency shall release a preliminary version of the plan required by subdivision b available at least 30 days before the submission of such final plan.
6202971.deadline_text: at least 30 days before the submission of such final plan

6202971.action_summary: Meet with the public to address borough-specific considerations in developing the fair housing plan, with at least one meeting after the release of the preliminary plan.
6202971.quote: the administrating agency shall meet with the public prior to the submission of such final plan to address borough-specific considerations, provided that at least one such meeting shall occur after the release of the preliminary plan.
6202971.deadline_text: prior to the submission of such final plan

6202971.action_summary: Release preliminary versions of the long-term housing needs assessment, housing production targets, and strategic equity framework at least 30 days before submission and meet with the public after release and before final submission.
6202971.quote: the administrating agency shall release preliminary versions at least 30 days before the submission of such final assessment, targets, and framework and meet with the public after the release of the preliminary versions and before the submission of the final assessment, targets, and framework.
6202971.deadline_text: at least 30 days before the submission of such final assessment, targets, and framework

6202971.action_summary: Submit an annual update on the city's progress relating to the goals and strategies identified in the fair housing plan to the mayor and speaker of the council and post on its website, except in years when a plan or other required report is due.
6202971.quote: the administrating agency shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council and post on its website an annual update on the city's progress relating to the goals and strategies identified pursuant to subdivision b of this section, except that no such annual update shall be due in any year for which a plan pursuant to subdivision b or a report pursuant to subdivisions c, d, or e of this section is due.
6202971.deadline_text: No later than October 1, 2026, and annually thereafter

5958277.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5958277.action_summary: Notify a business using a bicycle for commercial purposes of a first-time violation of section 10-157.1(a) or (b) and request that action be taken to correct such violation within 30 days, and afford such business an opportunity to contest the commissioner's finding in a manner set forth in the rules of the department of transportation.
5958277.quote: With respect to first time violations of such subdivisions or rules, the commissioner of transportation shall notify a business using a bicycle for commercial purposes of such violation and request that action be taken to correct such violation in such a manner within 30 days and shall afford such business an opportunity to contest the commissioner's finding in a manner set forth in the rules of the department of transportation.
affected_groups: businesses using bicycles for commercial purposes

5958277.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5958277.action_summary: Notify a business of a first-time violation of section 10-157(d) and request that action be taken to correct such violation within 30 days, and afford such business an opportunity to contest the commissioner's finding in a manner set forth in the rules of the department of transportation.
5958277.quote: the commissioner of transportation shall notify such business of such violation and request that action be taken to correct such violation in such a manner within 30 days and shall afford such business an opportunity to contest the commissioner's finding in a manner set forth in the rules of the department of transportation.
affected_groups: businesses using bicycles for commercial purposes

5958277.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
5958277.action_summary: Make signs available at no cost to food service establishments.
5958277.quote: The department shall make signs available[, and may charge a fee to cover printing, postage and handling expenses] at no cost to such an establishment.

5958277.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
5958277.action_summary: Permit persons to submit proof of cure of violations of section 20-910(f) electronically or in person.
5958277.quote: The department shall permit such proof to be submitted electronically or in person.

5958277.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
5958277.action_summary: Offer as part of any settlement offer made to a person who has received a first-time notice of violation of section 20-910(f) the option of presenting proof that the violation has been cured.
5958277.quote: The option of presenting proof that the violation has been cured shall be offered as part of any settlement offer made by the department to a person who has received, for the first time, a notice of violation of this subdivision or any rule promulgated thereunder.

5958277.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
5958277.action_summary: Offer as part of any settlement offer made to a person who has received a first-time notice of violation of section 20-544 the option of presenting proof that the violation has been cured.
5958277.quote: The option of presenting proof that the violation has been cured shall be offered as part of any settlement offer made by the department to a person who has received, for the first time, a notice of violation of section 20-544 of this subchapter or any rule promulgated thereunder.

5400747.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5400747.action_summary: Promulgate rules relating to the granting of licenses and revocable consents for sidewalk and roadway cafes, the administration of such licenses and consents, the design of sidewalk and roadway cafes, priorities among applicants, and operation and maintenance standards.
5400747.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160(b))
5400747.quote: the department, consistent with chapter 14 of the charter and the provisions of this subchapter, shall promulgate rules relating to (i) the granting of such licenses and revocable consents, and the administration of such licenses and revocable consents; (ii) the design of a sidewalk cafe or roadway cafe; (iii) priorities among applicants

5400747.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5400747.action_summary: Provide notice of petitions for revocable consents for roadway cafes to affected community boards and council members and provide opportunity for comment.
5400747.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.1(e))
5400747.quote: The department shall provide notice of a petition for a revocable consent for a roadway cafe to the affected community board and council member, and, to the extent practicable, provide an opportunity for both the community board and council member to submit comments to the department

5400747.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5400747.action_summary: Forward complete petitions for sidewalk cafes to the borough president, council speaker, council member, and community board within 5 days of receipt.
5400747.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.2(a))
5400747.quote: the department shall, within 5 days of the filing of such complete and accurate petition, forward such petition by electronic mail to the president of the borough in which the cafe is proposed to be located, the speaker of the council and the council member in whose district the cafe is proposed to be located, for information purposes, and to the community board for the community district in which the cafe is proposed to be located, for review
5400747.deadline_text: within 5 days of the filing of such complete and accurate petition

5400747.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5400747.action_summary: Approve, disapprove, or approve with modifications petitions for sidewalk cafes within 20 days after the expiration of the community board review period.
5400747.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.2(c)(1))
5400747.quote: within 20 days after the expiration of the period allowed for the filing of a recommendation or waiver by the community board pursuant to subdivision b of this section, the department shall (i) approve the petition for a sidewalk cafe, disapprove it or approve it with modifications; and (ii) file with the council any such decision to approve or approve with modifications
5400747.deadline_text: within 20 days after the expiration of the period allowed for the filing of a recommendation or waiver by the community board

5400747.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5400747.action_summary: Hold a public hearing on petitions for sidewalk cafes when required by law and render approval, disapproval, or approval with modifications decisions within 30 or 45 days.
5400747.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.2(c)(2))
5400747.quote: If the department holds such a public hearing, within 30 days after the expiration of the period allowed for the filing of a recommendation or waiver by the community board pursuant to subdivision b of the section, or within 45 days after the expiration of such period when the department plans to combine the public hearing on the petition with the public hearing required on 1 or more additional petitions pursuant to paragraph 3 of this subdivision, the department shall (i) hold a public hearing on the petition
5400747.deadline_text: within 30 days after the expiration of the period allowed for the filing of a recommendation or waiver by the community board pursuant to subdivision b of the section, or within 45 days after the expiration of such period when the department plans to combine the public hearing on the petition

5400747.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5400747.action_summary: Give notice at least 15 days prior to holding a public hearing on sidewalk cafe petitions to the community board, borough president, and council member.
5400747.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.2(d))
5400747.quote: At least 15 days prior to the date of a hearing held pursuant to paragraph 2 of subdivision c of this section, the department will give notice to the community board for the district in which the cafe is proposed to be located, to the president of the borough in which the cafe is proposed to be located and to the council member in whose district the cafe is proposed to be located.
5400747.deadline_text: At least 15 days prior to the date of a hearing

5400747.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5400747.action_summary: Publish notice of sidewalk cafe petition hearings in the City Record and in print or online editions of local newspapers at least 5 calendar days prior to the hearing.
5400747.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.2(d))
5400747.quote: Not less than 5 calendar days prior to the date of any such hearing, notice of the hearing shall be published in the City Record and in the print or online edition of 1 newspaper of local circulation in the community where the cafe is proposed to be located.
5400747.deadline_text: Not less than 5 calendar days prior to the date of any such hearing

5400747.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5400747.action_summary: Notify license holders of first-time violations and request corrective action within 30 days, and afford opportunity to contest the finding.
5400747.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.5(e))
5400747.quote: if the department finds that any holder of a license to operate a sidewalk cafe or roadway cafe has violated for the first time (i) any provision of section 19-160 through 19-160.6 or any rule promulgated thereunder, or (ii) the terms or conditions of such license, the department shall notify such license holder of such violation and request that action be taken to correct such violation within 30 days and shall afford such licensee an opportunity to contest the department's finding
affected_groups: sidewalk cafe and roadway cafe license holders

5400747.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5400747.action_summary: Submit a report on compensation for revocable consents for sidewalk and roadway cafes by May 1, 2027 and every 4 years thereafter.
5400747.citation: Section 6 of the local law (NYC Admin. Code § 19-160.7)
5400747.quote: No later than May 1, 2027, and every 4 years thereafter, the commissioner shall submit a report to the speaker of the council and the mayor on the changes to the median annual rent charged for a ground floor commercial premises for each sector, the corresponding percent land area for each sector, the number of restaurants operating sidewalk and/or roadway cafes in each sector, and the square footage of each sidewalk and roadway cafe in operation.
5400747.deadline_text: No later than May 1, 2027, and every 4 years thereafter

5400747.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5400747.action_summary: Establish a permanent open restaurants program including the use of roadway seating for outdoor dining and accessibility for people with disabilities.
5400747.citation: Section 8, amending Local Law 114 of 2020 (subdivision b of section 2)
5400747.quote: The department of transportation [and any other agency designated by the mayor] shall establish a permanent open restaurants program to succeed the temporary program established by local law number 77 for the year 2020[, provided that any additional legislation necessary to authorize such program has been enacted]. Such program shall include but not be limited to the following elements: 1. The use of roadway seating for outdoor dining; and 2. [The use of a pedestrian plaza, or other public outdoor location for outdoor dining; and 3.] Accessibility for people with disabilities in compliance with applicable federal, state and local law.

5400747.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5400747.action_summary: Develop a map on the department's website showing the location and name of each restaurant with a license and revocable consent for sidewalk or roadway cafes, required drawings, and inspection history.
5400747.quote: Within 12 months of the effective date of section 19-160 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by section six of this local law, the department of transportation shall develop a map on its website that shows the location and name of each restaurant that has obtained a license and revocable consent to operate a sidewalk cafe or a roadway cafe; a copy of the drawing required to be submitted with the petition for a revocable consent for a roadway cafe pursuant to the rules of the department; a copy of the drawing required to be submitted with the petition for a revocable consent for a sidewalk cafe pursuant to subdivision a of section 19-160.2 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by section six of this local law, and a history of any inspections of such sidewalk cafe or roadway cafe by such department.
5400747.deadline_text: Within 12 months of the effective date of section 19-160 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by section six of this local law

5400747.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
5400747.action_summary: Submit an annual report to the mayor and speaker of the council for 4 years specifying the total number of sidewalk and roadway cafes licensed, disaggregated by borough, and the total number of inspections and summonses issued.
5400747.quote: Within 12 months of the effective date of section 19-160 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by section six of this local law, and annually thereafter for 4 years, the department of transportation shall submit to the mayor and to the speaker of the council a report. Such report shall specify the total number of sidewalk cafes and roadway cafes licensed by such department, disaggregated by borough, and the total number of inspections performed and summonses issued by such department in the preceding 12-month period.
5400747.deadline_text: Within 12 months of the effective date of section 19-160 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by section six of this local law, and annually thereafter for 4 years

Such report shall also include recommendations for the creation of designated community spaces where street vendors can congregate to vend, including specific recommendations concerning appropriate locations for food trucks and the availability of commissary space throughout the city.

3686667.agency_full: the street vendor advisory board
3686667.action_summary: Issue to the speaker of the council a recommendation on whether the department of health and mental hygiene's authority to issue supervisory licenses should be restricted, expanded, or otherwise altered based on analysis of results from the increased permits issued.
3686667.quote: In addition to its other duties, the street vendor advisory board shall, prior to June 1 of each year from 2023 through 2030, issue to the speaker of the council a recommendation on whether the department of health and mental hygiene's authority to issue any or all of the supervisory licenses authorized to be issued by such department should be restricted, expanded, or otherwise altered based on an analysis of the results of the increased number of food vendor permits issued pursuant to the local law that added this section.
3686667.deadline_text: prior to June 1 of each year from 2023 through 2030

3686667.actor_raw: the commissioner of health and mental hygiene
3686667.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3686667.action_summary: Open the waiting list for full-term permits for persons who have held a food vendor license continuously since on or before March 1, 2017, no later than six months prior to the first issuance of supervisory licenses.
3686667.quote: The commissioner of health and mental hygiene shall open the waiting list for full-term permits operated pursuant to subparagraph (e) of paragraph 2 of subdivision b of section 17-307 of the administrative code of the city of New York as soon as practicable, but no later than six months prior to the first issuance of supervisory licenses pursuant to subparagraph (b) of paragraph 5 of subdivision b of section 17-307 of the administrative code of the city of New York. At such time, only persons who have held a food vendor license continuously since on or before March 1, 2017 may be added to the waiting list.
3686667.deadline_text: no later than six months prior to the first issuance of supervisory licenses

3686667.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3686667.action_summary: Establish by rule separate waiting lists for each relevant borough for fresh fruits and vegetables permits to be administered in accordance with procedures established by rules.
3686667.quote: After the initial issuance of such permits, the commissioner shall establish a separate waiting list for each of the relevant boroughs to be administered in accordance with procedures to be established by rules of the commissioner.

3686667.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3686667.action_summary: Limit the number of places on waiting lists for supervisory licenses by rule.
3686667.quote: The commissioner may by rule limit the number of places on such waiting list, but shall ensure that such waiting list is operative prior to supervisory licenses becoming available to new individuals.

3686667.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3686667.action_summary: Ensure that the waiting list for supervisory licenses is operative prior to supervisory licenses becoming available to new individuals.
3686667.quote: The commissioner may by rule limit the number of places on such waiting list, but shall ensure that such waiting list is operative prior to supervisory licenses becoming available to new individuals.
3686667.deadline_text: prior to supervisory licenses becoming available to new individuals

3686667.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3686667.action_summary: Promulgate rules regarding exceptions to the requirement that a supervisory licensee be physically present and vending at a vehicle or pushcart.
3686667.quote: A permittee issued a supervisory license shall not allow the operation of such permittee's vehicle or pushcart unless such permittee or another holder of a supervisory licensee is physically present and vending at such vehicle or pushcart, subject to any exceptions provided in rules of the commissioner.

3686667.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3686667.action_summary: Promulgate rules regarding renewal procedures and requirements for food vendor training certificates.
3686667.quote: Renewal shall be contingent on passing an examination regarding the vending restrictions contained in this section and any other information the department deems necessary to the safe operation of such vending unit pursuant to rules promulgated by the department.

3686667.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3686667.action_summary: Designate by rule a list of healthful foods in addition to fresh fruits and vegetables, water, and raw single ingredient nuts, aligned with evidence-based dietary recommendations.
3686667.quote: The commissioner may designate by rule a list of healthful foods in addition to fresh fruits and vegetables, water, and raw single ingredient nuts, provided that any food designated as healthful is in alignment with evidence-based dietary recommendations.

3686667.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3686667.action_summary: Establish procedures by rules to designate supervisory licenses for use in any borough and boroughs outside of Manhattan according to specified distribution.
3686667.quote: In accordance with procedures to be established by rules of the commissioner, in each twelve month period, 100 of the supervisory licenses made available for application under this paragraph shall be designated for use in any borough, and the remaining 300 such supervisory licenses shall be designated for use in boroughs outside of Manhattan.

3686667.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3686667.action_summary: Designate fresh fruits and vegetables permits for use exclusively within specified police precincts or in any other police precinct determined to have substantially lower fresh fruit and vegetable consumption or elevated nutrition-related health problems.
3686667.quote: In addition to the police precincts listed in subparagraph (b) of this paragraph, a fresh fruits and vegetable permits that is designated for use exclusively in a borough as specified in subparagraph (a) of this paragraph may also be designated for use in any other police precinct in such borough that the commissioner has specified in rules of the department, after determining that the rate of consumption of fresh fruits and vegetables in such precinct is substantially lower than the citywide average and that the precinct has an elevated rate of nutrition-related health problems compared to the rest of the city.

3686667.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3686667.action_summary: Limit the number of places on waiting lists for fresh fruits and vegetables permits by rule.
3686667.quote: The commissioner may by rule limit the number of places on each such waiting list.

3343878.action_summary: Propose a surveillance technology impact and use policy and post it on the department's website at least 90 days prior to the use of any new surveillance technology.
3343878.quote: The department shall propose a surveillance technology impact and use policy and post such proposal on the department's website, at least 90 days prior to the use of any new surveillance technology.
3343878.deadline_text: at least 90 days prior to the use of any new surveillance technology

3343878.action_summary: Propose a surveillance technology impact and use policy for existing surveillance technology and post it on the department's website.
3343878.quote: For existing surveillance technology as of the effective date of the local law that added this section, the department shall propose a surveillance technology impact and use policy and post such proposal on the department's website within 180 days of such effective date.
3343878.deadline_text: within 180 days of such effective date

3343878.action_summary: Provide an addendum to the existing surveillance technology impact and use policy when acquiring enhancements or using surveillance technology for purposes not previously disclosed.
3343878.quote: When the department seeks to acquire or acquires enhancements to surveillance technology or uses such surveillance technology for a purpose or in a manner not previously disclosed through the surveillance technology impact and use policy, the department shall provide an addendum to the existing surveillance technology impact and use policy describing such enhancement or additional use.

3343878.action_summary: Consider public comments and provide the final surveillance technology impact and use policy to the speaker and mayor, and post it on the department's website.
3343878.quote: The commissioner shall consider public comments and provide the final surveillance technology impact and use policy to the speaker and the mayor, and shall post it on the department's website no more than 45 days after the close of the public comment period established by subdivision e of this section.
3343878.deadline_text: no more than 45 days after the close of the public comment period established by subdivision e of this section

3343878.action_summary: Prepare annual audits of surveillance technology impact and use policies assessing compliance, describing violations, and publishing recommendations for revisions.
3343878.quote: The commissioner shall prepare annual audits of surveillance technology impact and use policies as defined in section 14-188 of the administrative code that shall: 1. assess whether the New York city police department's use of surveillance technology, as defined in section 14-188 of the administrative code, complies with the terms of the applicable surveillance technology impact and use policy; 2. describe any known or reasonably suspected violations of the surveillance technology impact and use policy, including but not limited to complaints alleging such violations made by individuals pursuant to paragraph (6) of subdivision c of this section; and 3. publish recommendations, if any, relating to revisions of any surveillance technology impact and use policies.

3977012.action_summary: Seek voluntary consent from incarcerated individuals diagnosed with serious mental illness to share medical information with their attorney of record within 48 hours of diagnosis.
3977012.quote: For each incarcerated individual who is not sentenced and who is diagnosed with a serious mental illness, correctional health services shall seek voluntary consent from such individual to share medical information with the attorney of record
affected_groups: incarcerated individuals with serious mental illness

3977012.action_summary: Provide medical information to the attorney of record for incarcerated individuals diagnosed with serious mental illness within five calendar days of obtaining consent.
3977012.quote: provide such information created or obtained pursuant to sections 17-1802 and 17-1804 to the attorney of record for any such individual within five calendar days of obtaining consent from the individual
3977012.deadline_text: within five calendar days of obtaining consent from the individual
affected_groups: incarcerated individuals with serious mental illness

3977012.action_summary: Make good faith efforts to ascertain each incarcerated individual's attorney of record through reasonable means including consulting court websites, speaking with the individual, contacting court clerks, or other necessary methods.
3977012.quote: Correctional health services shall make a good faith effort to ascertain such individual's attorney of record, including but not limited to consulting the website maintained by the New York state unified court system, speaking with the individual, contacting the clerk of the court, or any other reasonable means necessary to identify such individual's attorney
affected_groups: incarcerated individuals with serious mental illness

3977012.action_summary: Provide a confidential medical condition letter to the attorney of record for qualifying incarcerated individuals within five business days prior to any court date.
3977012.quote: Within five business days prior to any court date indicated by the New York city department of correction's inmate information system, correctional health services shall provide a confidential medical condition letter to the attorney of record for any incarcerated individual to whom subdivision a of this section applies
3977012.deadline_text: Within five business days prior to any court date
affected_groups: incarcerated individuals with serious mental illness

3458224.action_summary: Determine the percentage difference in consumer price index and adjust maximum contribution limits accordingly, publishing the adjusted amounts in the City Record.
3458224.quote: the campaign finance board shall (i) determine the percentage difference between the average over a calendar year of the consumer price index for the metropolitan New York-New Jersey region published by the United States bureau of labor statistics for the twelve months preceding the beginning of such calendar year and the average over the calendar year two thousand nineteen of such consumer price index; (ii) adjust each maximum contribution applicable pursuant to paragraph (f) of subdivision one of this section by the amount of such percentage difference to the nearest fifty dollars; and (iii) publish such adjusted maximum contribution in the City Record.
3458224.deadline_text: Not later than the first day of March in the year two thousand twenty-two and every fourth year thereafter

3458224.action_summary: Review each timely disclosure report submitted by candidates prior to the filing deadline and issue a written review within 30 days, informing candidates of compliance questions and public funding eligibility concerns.
3458224.quote: The board shall review each disclosure report timely submitted by a candidate prior to the last date upon which such candidate may file a certification pursuant to paragraph (c) of subdivision one of this section, or subdivision one of section 3-717, and issue to the candidate a review within 30 days of the date upon which such disclosure report was due
3458224.deadline_text: within 30 days of the date upon which such disclosure report was due

3458224.action_summary: Check each contribution against the doing business database and notify the principal or authorized committee within prescribed timeframes if a contribution exceeds doing business contribution limitations or is not matchable.
3458224.quote: The board shall check each contribution against the doing business database and shall notify the principal committee within twenty days of the reporting of such contribution if a contribution exceeding the doing business contribution limitation set forth in subdivision 1-a of section 3-703 is subject to such limitations of this subchapter or if a contribution is not matchable pursuant to such subdivision. Notwithstanding any provision in this subdivision, in the six weeks preceding the covered election the board shall provide such notification to the principal or authorized committee within four business days of the reporting of such contribution to the board

3458224.action_summary: Make public funds payments to participating candidates within four business days after receipt of matchable contribution reports, withhold up to five percent pending final pre-election payment, and schedule payment dates on December 15, January 15, February 15, March 15, April 15, July 15, and minimum three to four additional dates before primary and general elections.
3458224.quote: the campaign finance board shall make possible payment within four business days after receipt of reports of matchable contributions, or as soon thereafter as is practicable; provided, however, that the board shall withhold up to five percent of all public funds payments to participating candidates until the final pre-election payment for any given election. The board shall schedule payment dates on December 15 of the year preceding the year of election, as well as January 15, February 15, March 15, April 15 and a minimum of three payment dates within the forty-five days prior to a covered primary election, a payment date of July 15 and a minimum of four payment dates within the ninety days prior to a covered general election, and a minimum of three payment dates within the thirty days prior to any other covered election.
3458224.deadline_text: within four business days after receipt of reports of matchable contributions, or as soon thereafter as is practicable

3458224.action_summary: Require filing of reports of contributions and expenditures in accordance with the schedule specified by the state board of elections for campaign receipt and expenditure statements.
3458224.quote: The board shall require the filing of reports of contributions and expenditures for purposes of determining compliance with paragraph (f) of subdivision one of section 3-703, section 3-706, subdivision 1-a of section 3-703, section 3-717, and section 3-718, in accordance with the schedule specified by the state board of elections for the filing of campaign receipt and expenditure statements.

3458224.action_summary: Inform participating candidates who cease actively campaigning that they have ceased such activity and determine that expenditures after such cessation are not qualified expenditures.
3458224.quote: the board shall inform such participating candidate of the board's determination that such candidate has ceased actively campaigning for a covered office. Expenditures incurred prior to the date by which such candidate has ceased actively campaigning for a covered office may be considered qualified expenditures, but no expenditures incurred after the date of such a determination of the board shall be considered qualified expenditures.

3458224.action_summary: Administer and enforce the contribution limitations and public matching funds provisions for covered elections held prior to 2022 in accordance with whether participating candidates have chosen Option A or Option B.
3458224.quote: the campaign finance board shall administer and enforce the contribution limitations and public matching funds provisions, including those pertaining to the matching formula, qualifying threshold, and public funds cap in accordance with whether the participating candidate has chosen Option A or Option B
affected_groups: candidates for covered elections held prior to 2022

2884636.action_summary: Consider the feasibility of designing and constructing each capital project subject to low energy intensity building requirements as an onsite energy generating building.
2884636.quote: For each capital project subject to subparagraph (i) of this paragraph the design agency shall consider the feasibility of designing and constructing such project as an onsite energy generating building.

2884636.action_summary: Consider the feasibility of designing and constructing capital projects of no more than three stories above grade as net zero energy buildings.
2884636.quote: For each capital project subject to subparagraph (i) of this paragraph with an estimated height of no more than three stories above grade, the design agency shall consider the feasibility of designing and constructing such project as a net zero energy building.

2884636.action_summary: Consider the feasibility of designing and constructing capital projects to incorporate green infrastructure.
2884636.quote: For each capital project subject to subparagraph (i) of this paragraph the design agency shall consider the feasibility of designing and constructing such project to incorporate green infrastructure.

2884636.action_summary: Examine sources of water supply of private water companies, establish rules and regulations, and exercise superintendence, regulation and control over water supply.
2884636.quote: The commissioner shall examine into the sources of water supply of any private companies supplying the city or any portion thereof or its inhabitants with water to see that the same is wholesome and the supply is adequate, to establish such rules and regulations in respect thereof as are reasonable and necessary for the convenience of the public and to exercise superintendence, regulation and control in respect to the supply of water by such water companies

2884636.action_summary: Promulgate rules defining volatile flammable liquids and the specifications for the temperature at which such liquids will emit flammable vapor.
2884636.quote: A volatile, flammable liquid is any liquid that will emit a flammable vapor at a temperature specified in rules of the department.

2884636.actor_raw: the commissioner of environmental protection, and the environmental control board within the office of administrative trials and hearings
2884636.agency_full: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings
2884636.action_summary: Enforce provisions of subdivisions b and b-1 of section 1403 of the charter and sections 24-504 through 24-523 and related rules, and issue orders as necessary for enforcement.
2884636.quote: the commissioner of environmental protection, and the environmental control board within the office of administrative trials and hearings, shall enforce the provisions of subdivisions b and b-1 of section 1403 of the charter and sections 24-504 through 24-523 of this chapter and the rules promulgated pursuant thereto. Such commissioner and board shall have the power to issue such orders as may be provided for therein and such additional orders as may be necessary for the enforcement of such provisions.

2884636.action_summary: Promulgate rules governing the appeal of orders issued by the commissioner.
2884636.quote: The department of environmental protection shall promulgate rules governing the appeal of orders issued by the commissioner.

2884636.actor_raw: the environmental control board within the office of administrative trials and hearings
2884636.agency_full: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings
2884636.action_summary: Provide hearings for persons affected by cease and desist orders within two business days of receipt of application, and may suspend, modify or terminate such orders.
2884636.quote: Any person affected by such an order may make written application to the environmental control board within the office of administrative trials and hearings for a hearing. Such hearing shall be provided, pursuant to the rules of such board within such office, and shall be held within two business days after the receipt of such application. The board may suspend, modify or terminate such order.
2884636.deadline_text: within two business days after the receipt of such application
affected_groups: all persons affected by cease and desist orders

2884636.action_summary: Promulgate rules to carry out provisions of stormwater construction and post-construction control subchapter, including rules regarding SWPPP content, design standards, exemptions, development thresholds, procedures and fees, training requirements, recordkeeping, compliance certifications, and maintenance standards.
2884636.quote: The department shall promulgate rules to carry out the provisions of this subchapter in accordance with the NYC MS4 permit and the NYSDEC construction general permit, including but not limited to rules that: a. Set forth the content of SWPPPs, consistent with the NYSDEC construction general permit, including identifying those development projects requiring only erosion and sediment controls during construction and those development projects requiring erosion and sediment controls and post-construction stormwater management facilities. b. Establish design standards for erosion and sediment controls and post-construction stormwater management facilities which shall not be less stringent than the standards set forth or incorporated by reference in the NYSDEC construction general permit. c. Establish exemptions from permit requirements, consistent with the NYC MS4 permit and the NYSDEC construction general permit. d. After completion of the lot size soil disturbance study required by the NYC MS4 permit, provide for the regulation of development activity of less than one acre, based either on total disturbance of soil or on amount of impervious surface created or replaced, where an appropriate reduction in the threshold is necessary in accordance with the NYC MS4 permit. e. Establish procedures and fees for the review of SWPPPs and the issuance and renewal of permits required by this subchapter. f. Establish training, experience and/or education requirements for qualified professionals and qualified inspectors, which shall not be less stringent than those required by the NYSDEC construction general permit. g. Establish record keeping, inspection and reporting requirements for applicants and permittees to monitor compliance with this subchapter and approved SWPPPs. h. Establish requirements for compliance certifications by contractors to be included with SWPPPs. i. Establish standards for the maintenance, inspection, repair and replacement of required erosion and sediment controls and post-construction stormwater management facilities.
2884636.deadline_text: to be determined by the department as practicable within 45 days after NYSDEC SWMP approval and no later than 6 months after such approval

2884636.action_summary: Review stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPPs) submitted by developers, issue stormwater construction permits upon acceptance of SWPPP, issue MS4 SWPPP acceptance forms, and send notice of rejection with specific deficiencies when SWPPP is rejected.
2884636.quote: The department or a qualified professional designated by the department shall review the SWPPP within time periods to be specified in the rules of the department. If the department accepts the SWPPP the department shall issue a stormwater construction permit to the developer and, for projects subject to the NYSDEC construction general permit, shall issue an MS4 SWPPP acceptance form for filing with NYSDEC. If the department rejects the SWPPP the department shall send notice of such rejection to the developer indicating the specific deficiencies that caused the department to reject the SWPPP.
2884636.deadline_text: within time periods to be specified in the rules of the department

2884636.action_summary: Maintain a record of all post-construction stormwater management facilities and the property served by each such facility.
2884636.quote: The department shall maintain a record of all such post-construction stormwater management facilities and the property served by each such facility.

2884636.action_summary: Issue or renew stormwater maintenance permits upon receipt of satisfactory inspection reports certifying that post-construction stormwater management facilities have been installed and are operated and maintained in good working condition.
2884636.quote: The department shall issue or renew such permit upon receipt of a satisfactory inspection report certified by a qualified professional retained by the owner indicating that the facility has been installed and/or is operated and maintained in good working condition to meet applicable design standards and the rules of the department.

2884636.action_summary: Enter on property and inspect industrial stormwater sources for evidence of unauthorized discharges, illic connections, and compliance with MSGP requirements and local stormwater requirements, at a minimum in accordance with the schedule and requirements set forth in the NYC MS4 Permit.
2884636.quote: The department shall have the authority to enter and inspect industrial stormwater sources including, but not limited to, their equipment, practices, operations and records, consistent with applicable law and in accordance with rules of the department related to such entry and inspection, and shall, at a minimum, conduct inspections of such sources in accordance with the schedule and requirements for such inspections set forth in the NYC MS4 Permit.

2884636.actor_raw: the commissioner, and the environmental control board within the office of administrative trials and hearings
2884636.agency_full: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings
2884636.action_summary: Enforce provisions of chapter 5-A of title 24 (water pollution control) and the rules promulgated pursuant thereto, and issue orders as necessary for enforcement.
2884636.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the commissioner, and the environmental control board within the office of administrative trials and hearings, shall enforce the provisions of this chapter and the rules promulgated pursuant thereto.

2884636.action_summary: Promulgate rules governing the appeal of orders issued by department employees or authorized inspection agents.
2884636.quote: The department shall promulgate rules governing the appeal of such orders where they are issued by department employees or authorized inspection agents.

2884636.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing categories of violations for which authorized inspection agents may issue notices, categories of orders such agents may issue, circumstances requiring department approval, and eligibility criteria and training requirements for such agents.
2884636.quote: Authorized inspection agents shall perform their duties in accordance with this chapter and rules of the department promulgated pursuant thereto, which rules shall set forth the categories of violations for which such notices may be issued by such agents, the categories of orders that may be issued by such agents and the circumstances in which such agents shall obtain department approval or refer matters to the department for further action. In addition, the department shall, through standards imposed by means of procurement or rulemaking, ensure that such agents are subject to appropriate eligibility criteria, training requirements and grounds for revoking inspection and enforcement authority.

2884636.action_summary: Not issue a certificate of occupancy or letter of completion for a building that is part of a covered development project unless the applicant submits proof that the department of environmental protection has issued a stormwater maintenance permit for any post-construction stormwater management facilities serving such building.
2884636.quote: The department shall not issue a certificate of occupancy or letter of completion with respect to a building or premises that is part of a covered development project unless the applicant submits proof that the department of environmental protection has issued a stormwater maintenance permit for any post-construction stormwater management facilities serving such building or premises.

2884636.action_summary: Not issue a certificate of occupancy for a building that is part of a covered development project unless the applicant submits proof that the department of environmental protection has issued a stormwater maintenance permit for any post-construction stormwater management facilities serving such building.
2884636.quote: The department shall not issue a certificate of occupancy with respect to a building or premises that is part of a covered development project unless the applicant submits proof that the department of environmental protection has issued a stormwater maintenance permit for any post-construction stormwater management facilities serving such building or premises.

2884636.action_summary: Determine the effective date or dates for implementation of stormwater management program provisions and set forth such dates in rules, subject to NYSDEC approval of the stormwater management program and the timing constraints specified.
2884636.quote: Such date or dates shall be determined by the department of environmental protection and set forth in rules implementing the provisions of such sections, provided that such date or dates shall be no earlier than forty-five days after the date of the final approval by the New York state department of environmental conservation of the storm water management program (SWMP) submitted by the department of environmental protection under such permit and no later than six months after the date of such SWMP approval
2884636.deadline_text: no later than six months after the date of SWMP approval

2884636.action_summary: Notify the New York state legislative bill drafting commission and the corporation counsel upon determination of the effective dates for implementation of stormwater management program provisions.
2884636.quote: upon the determination of the effective date or dates pursuant to this subdivision, the commissioner of environmental protection shall notify the New York state legislative bill drafting commission, in order that the commission may maintain an accurate and timely effective database of the official text of the New York city charter and administrative code in furtherance of effectuating the provisions of section 70-b of the public officers law, and the corporation counsel, who shall notify relevant publishers in furtherance of effectuating the provisions of section 7-111 of the administrative code
2884636.deadline_text: upon the determination of the effective date or dates

2884636.action_summary: Administer and enforce provisions relating to management and control of discharges and runoff from public and private property, including stormwater discharges, and regulate discharges into waters of harmful substances that may adversely impact waters of the state.
2884636.quote: the commissioner shall have the power to administer and enforce provisions of law, rules and regulations relating to the management and control of discharges and runoff from public and private property, including but not limited to stormwater discharges; regulate and control discharges into water within and about the city of New York of harmful or objectionable substances, contaminants and pollutants that may have an adverse impact on waters of the state; enforce all laws, rules and regulations with respect to discharges described in this paragraph; make such investigations and studies as may be desirable for the purpose of such enforcement and of controlling and eliminating pollution of waters within and about the city of New York; and, for the purposes set forth in this paragraph, compel the attendance of witnesses and take such witnesses' testimony under oath.

2884636.action_summary: Coordinate the actions of city agencies with respect to compliance with the SPDES permit for municipal separate storm sewer systems.
2884636.quote: The commissioner shall have the power to coordinate the actions of city agencies with respect to compliance with the state pollutant discharge elimination system (SPDES) permit for municipal separate storm sewer systems of New York city, SPDES No. NY-0287890 or its successor.

2884636.action_summary: Issue cease and desist orders requiring persons to halt or prevent unlawful discharges that create imminent danger to the sewer system or public health, and seal, block, or inactivate equipment or facilities as necessary.
2884636.quote: such commissioner may issue a cease and desist order requiring any person who owns, leases, operates, controls or supervises any building, structure, facility or installation from which the unlawful discharge is emitted to take such action as may be necessary to halt or prevent such discharge.

2884636.actor_raw: the office of administrative trials and hearings
2884636.agency_full: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings
2884636.action_summary: Impose civil penalties for violations of water pollution control provisions, and maintain power to enforce final decisions imposing such penalties as money judgments.
2884636.quote: The office of administrative trials and hearings, pursuant to section 1049-a of the charter, shall have the power to impose such civil penalties.

2884636.actor_raw: the environmental control board within the office of administrative trials and hearings
2884636.agency_full: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings
2884636.action_summary: Establish a schedule of civil penalties indicating minimum and maximum penalties for each offense, or use a schedule adopted by the department of environmental protection.
2884636.quote: The environmental control board within the office of administrative trials and hearings, in its discretion, may, within the limits set forth in this subdivision, establish a schedule of civil penalties indicating the minimum and maximum penalty for each separate offense or may use a schedule adopted by the department of environmental protection.

2884636.actor_raw: Officers and employees of the department of environmental protection and of other city agencies designated by the commissioner of environmental protection
2884636.action_summary: Issue summonses, appearance tickets, orders and notices of violation based upon violations of water pollution control provisions or rules.
2884636.quote: Officers and employees of the department of environmental protection and of other city agencies designated by the commissioner of environmental protection shall have the power to issue summonses, appearance tickets, orders and notices of violation based upon violations of this chapter or rules of the department promulgated hereunder.

2884636.actor_raw: An authorized representative of the department of environmental protection
2884636.action_summary: Enter on property and conduct inspections for compliance with water pollution control provisions and departmental rules.
2884636.quote: An authorized representative of the department of environmental protection may enter on any property, consistent with applicable law and in accordance with rules of the department related to such entry and inspection, to inspect for compliance with this chapter and rules of the department promulgated hereunder.

2884636.actor_raw: The commissioner, and the environmental control board within the office of administrative trials and hearings
2884636.agency_full: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings
2884636.action_summary: Issue orders requiring inspection by qualified inspectors or professionals, maintenance or replacement of post-construction stormwater management facilities, compliance with MSGP through monitoring and reporting, and installation or maintenance of stormwater management practices.
2884636.quote: The commissioner, and the environmental control board within the office of administrative trials and hearings, shall have the power to issue such orders as may be provided for in this chapter and the rules promulgated pursuant thereto and such additional orders as may be necessary for the enforcement of such provisions. Such orders may include, but are not limited to, orders requiring (i) inspection by a qualified inspector or qualified professional, (ii) maintenance, repair or replacement of post-construction stormwater management facilities, (iii) compliance with the MSGP through actions including, but not limited to, monitoring, analysis, and reporting or (iv) the installation, implementation and maintenance of SMPs.

2884636.action_summary: Issue cease and desist orders requiring persons to halt or prevent conditions in violation of stormwater management provisions that create imminent danger to the sewer system or public health.
2884636.quote: Whenever the commissioner has reasonable cause to believe that (i) a condition exists in violation of any of the provisions of sections 24-559, 24-560 or 24-572 or in violation of any order or rule issued by the board or commissioner pursuant to such provisions or to section 24-581 in furtherance of such provisions and (ii) that such condition creates or may create an imminent danger to the sewer system or to the public health or to the life or safety of persons, the commissioner may issue a cease and desist order requiring any person who owns, leases, operates, controls or supervises any building, structure, facility or installation in which the condition is located to take such action as may be necessary to halt or prevent such condition.

2884636.actor_raw: the environmental control board within the office of administrative trials and hearings
2884636.agency_full: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings
2884636.action_summary: Issue cease and desist orders in cases of continued or knowing violations of stormwater management provisions that present danger to the environment or threaten to interfere with sewer system operation, after notice and opportunity for hearing.
