3713964.quote: The department shall retain an organization to make at least two doulas at any given time available to provide doula services twice a week, for four hours, at all department facilities that house incarcerated persons who identify as female, as well as to provide doula services during labor and delivery, upon request.
affected_groups: incarcerated persons who identify as female

3713964.action_summary: Ensure that doula services are available at a frequency determined by available department resources and exigent circumstances, permit doulas to access the nursery and programming areas, allow doulas to accompany incarcerated individuals to medical appointments upon request, and subject doulas to the department's service provider processing security clearance protocol.
3713964.quote: The department shall ensure that doula services are available at a frequency to be determined by factors including available department resources and exigent circumstances. The department shall permit doulas to access the nursery, as defined in section 9-142, to access areas where programming is typically provided and to accompany incarcerated individuals to medical appointments, upon request.
affected_groups: incarcerated persons who identify as female

3713964.action_summary: Provide to the speaker of the council and publish on its website in a machine readable format a report on the number of doula service hours provided, types of services provided, and number of incarcerated individuals served in the previous six month period.
3713964.quote: the department shall provide to the speaker of the council and publish on its website, in a machine readable format, a report on the number of doula service hours provided, the types of services provided, and the number of incarcerated individuals served in the previous six month period.
3713964.deadline_text: No later than January 15, 2023 and every six months thereafter
affected_groups: incarcerated persons who identify as female

3713964.action_summary: Convene a working group composed of the speaker of the city council or designee, commissioner of correction or designee, representatives from the department of health and mental hygiene, representatives from the organization providing doula services, and department staff who work on programming for incarcerated persons who identify as female.
3713964.quote: the commissioner of correction shall convene a working group composed of the speaker of the city council or the speaker's designee; commissioner of correction or the commissioner's designee; representatives from the department of health and mental hygiene; representatives from the organization providing doula services pursuant to subdivision b of this section; and department staff who regularly work on programming for incarcerated persons who identify as female.
affected_groups: incarcerated persons who identify as female

3713964.action_summary: Meet every six months until August 31, 2029, and at least once a year thereafter, to review reports on doula services, reports from the providing organization, reports from city agencies on maternal health, and discuss improving communication and collaboration related to pregnant individuals in custody.
3713964.quote: Until August 31, 2029, the working group shall meet every six months to review the reports required by subdivision d of this section, review relevant reports issued by the organization providing doula services, consider any reports issued by city agencies regarding maternal health and discuss improving communication, collaboration and efficiency related to pregnant individuals in custody. After September 1, 2029, the working group shall meet at least once a year
affected_groups: incarcerated persons who identify as female

3844848.actor_raw: the department of health and mental hygiene
3844848.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3844848.action_summary: Complete a study of diabetes-related health problems in the city and submit a report to the mayor and speaker of the council, and post the report on the department's website, disclosing specified diabetes data for the previous 6 months.
3844848.quote: the department of health and mental hygiene shall complete a study of diabetes-related health problems in the city and shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and post on such department's website, a report disclosing the following information
3844848.deadline_text: No later than December 1, 2020, and every 6 months thereafter

3844848.actor_raw: the commissioner of health and mental hygiene
3844848.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3844848.action_summary: Develop and submit to the mayor and speaker of the council a comprehensive report of cumulative diabetes studies that includes recommendations to reduce diabetes-related health problems and a plan to implement the department's recommendations.
3844848.quote: the commissioner of health and mental hygiene shall develop and submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a comprehensive report of the results of the cumulative studies required by section one of this local law. Such comprehensive report shall include recommendations to reduce diabetes-related health problems and a plan to implement the department's recommendations.

3521904.action_summary: Compile a list of multiple dwellings with excessive housing maintenance or construction code violations at least once every six months.
3521904.quote: The commissioner shall, no less than once every six months, compile a list of multiple dwellings that includes: (i) all multiple dwellings containing fewer than 35 units that have a ratio of open hazardous or immediately hazardous housing maintenance code violations or immediately hazardous or major construction code violations that equal in the aggregate three or more such violations for every dwelling unit in such multiple dwelling; and (ii) all multiple dwellings containing 35 units or more that have a ratio of open hazardous or immediately hazardous housing maintenance code violations or immediately hazardous or major construction code violations that equal in the aggregate two or more such violations for every dwelling unit in such multiple dwelling.
3521904.deadline_text: no less than once every six months

3521904.action_summary: Deny permits for multiple dwellings on the excessive violations list unless an exception applies.
3521904.quote: The commissioner shall not issue permits for multiple dwellings on such list.

3521904.action_summary: Remove a multiple dwelling from the excessive violations list once the owner corrects violations so that the violation ratio falls below the threshold.
3521904.quote: If the owner of a multiple dwelling on such list corrects open hazardous or immediately hazardous housing maintenance code violations or immediately hazardous or major construction code violations in such multiple dwelling so that the ratio of such violations to the number of dwelling units in such multiple dwelling falls below those outlined in this section, the commissioner shall remove such multiple dwelling from such list.

3521904.action_summary: Promulgate rules necessary for implementation of the permit denial requirements prior to the effective date.
3521904.quote: the commissioner of buildings may take such measures as are necessary for its implementation, including the promulgation of rules, prior to such effective date.

3147852.actor_raw: the department of homeless services and the department
3147852.agency: the department of homeless services and the department
3147852.agency_full: the department of homeless services and the department
3147852.action_summary: Create and maintain an intake and assessment process for runaway youth and homeless youth transitioning from runaway and homeless youth shelter services to department of homeless services shelters, permitting eligible youth to bypass intake centers or assessment shelters when demographic and social services information is provided in advance.
3147852.quote: The department of homeless services and the department shall create and maintain an intake and assessment process for runaway youth and homeless youth who have reached the age and/or time limitations applicable to department-funded shelter services or, as designated by the department, other runaway or homeless youth receiving shelter services, and who seek to transition from runaway and homeless youth shelter services to a department of homeless services shelter.

3147852.agency_full: Department of Youth and Community Development
3147852.action_summary: Submit a report to the mayor and speaker of the council describing the intake and assessment process, the number of runaway and homeless youth referred through such process, referral sources, service access outcomes, and recommendations for process changes.
3147852.quote: On or before July 31, 2018, and every six months thereafter, the department shall submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council which includes, but need not be limited to, the following information: a description of the intake and assessment process required by subdivision b of this section; the number of runaway and homeless youth referred through such process; where such youth were referred from; whether such youth accessed services through the process; and any recommendations for changes to the process.
3147852.deadline_text: On or before July 31, 2018, and every six months thereafter

2264229.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
2264229.action_summary: Make available signs in English and the top six limited English proficiency languages spoken by the population of New York City based on United States census data.
2264229.quote: Such signs shall be made available by the department in English and in the top six limited English proficiency languages spoken by the population of New York city as determined by the department of the city planning and the office of the language services coordinator, based on United States census data.

2264229.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
2264229.action_summary: In conjunction with the mayor's office of immigrant affairs, prepare and submit a report to the mayor and speaker of the city council on complaints, investigations, violations, and trends related to providers of immigration assistance services.
2264229.quote: In conjunction with the mayor's office of immigrant affairs, the department shall prepare and submit to the mayor and the speaker of the city council a report that includes the following information related to providers of immigration assistance services
2264229.deadline_text: on or before October 1, 2017 and every six months thereafter until the year 2020

2264229.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
2264229.action_summary: In conjunction with the mayor's office of immigrant affairs, engage in community outreach and education efforts to raise awareness about fraudulent schemes and complaint mechanisms.
2264229.quote: In conjunction with the mayor's office of immigrant affairs, the department shall engage in community outreach and education efforts to raise awareness about topics including but not limited to common fraudulent schemes committed by providers of immigration assistance services and the department's complaint mechanisms and services.

2264229.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
2264229.action_summary: In conjunction with the mayor's office of immigrant affairs, create a Consumer Bill of Rights for customers seeking assistance from providers of immigration assistance services and post it on the department's website in English and the top six limited English proficiency languages.
2264229.quote: In conjunction with the mayor's office of immigrant affairs, the department shall create a "Consumer Bill of Rights" for customers seeking assistance from providers of immigration assistance services. Such bill of rights shall be posted on the department's website in English, as well as in the top six limited English proficiency languages spoken by the population of New York city as determined by the department of the city planning and the office of the language services coordinator, based on United States census data.

2264229.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
2264229.action_summary: Promulgate rules and regulations necessary for implementing and carrying out the provisions of this subchapter.
2264229.quote: The commissioner may promulgate such rules and regulations as are necessary for the purposes of implementing and carrying out the provisions of this subchapter.

3698822.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3698822.action_summary: Submit an annual report to the mayor and speaker of the city council on cooling tower registrations, certifications, microbe test results, inspections, violations, cleanings, and legionnaires' disease diagnoses.
3698822.quote: The commissioner, in consultation with the department of buildings, shall submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the city council on or before May 15 each year until May 15, 2025, reporting on the following information for the prior year
3698822.deadline_text: on or before May 15 each year until May 15, 2025

3698822.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3698822.action_summary: Post the results of each cooling tower inspection in a searchable format on the department's website and maintain such results for no less than three years.
3698822.quote: the results of each inspection of a cooling tower by the department conducted after the effective date of this section pursuant to paragraph 1 of subdivision i of this section shall be posted in a searchable format on the website of the department and maintained on such website for no less than three years

6635504.action_summary: Promulgate a rule to adopt an interim flood risk area map showing the 10-year rainfall risk area and the coastal flood risk area, and post the map on the city's website.
6635504.quote: The department, in consultation with the department of buildings, the office of long-term planning and sustainability, and other relevant agencies shall promulgate a rule to adopt an interim flood risk area map, showing the 10-year rainfall risk area and the coastal flood risk area, and post a map

6635504.action_summary: Adopt by rule and post on the city's website an updated flood risk area map showing an updated 10-year rainfall risk area no later than January 1, 2028.
6635504.quote: No later than January 1, 2028, the department, in consultation with the department of buildings, the office of long-term planning and sustainability, and other relevant agencies shall adopt by rule and post on the city's website, an updated flood risk area map, showing an updated 10-year rainfall risk area

6635504.action_summary: Within 1 year of new federal emergency management agency flood insurance rate maps issuance, consider whether the coastal flood risk area should be updated and adopt any such updated coastal flood risk area by rule and post the updated map.
6635504.quote: Within 1 year of the issuance of new effective flood insurance rate maps for the city of New York by the federal emergency management agency, the department, in consultation with the department of buildings, the office of long-term planning and sustainability, and other relevant agencies, may consider whether the coastal flood risk area should be updated to replace the interim coastal flood risk area established pursuant to paragraph 1 of this section, based on projections of the New York city panel on climate change and any other data such agencies determine to be reasonable. The department shall adopt any such updated coastal flood risk area by rule and post such updated map
6635504.deadline_text: Within 1 year of the issuance of new effective flood insurance rate maps

6635504.action_summary: Within 1 year of new projections by the New York city panel on climate change, consider whether the 10-year rainfall risk area should be updated and adopt any such updated 10-year rainfall risk area by rule and post the updated flood risk area map.
6635504.quote: Within 1 year of the issuance of new projections by the New York city panel on climate change, pursuant to subdivision 2 of section 3-122, the department may, in consultation with the department of buildings, the office of long-term planning and sustainability, and other relevant agencies, consider whether the 10-year rainfall risk area adopted pursuant to subparagraph (a) of this paragraph should be updated based on such projections, and any other data such agencies determine to be reasonable. The department shall adopt any such updated 10-year rainfall risk area by rule and post on the city's website an updated flood risk area map
6635504.deadline_text: Within 1 year of the issuance of new projections by the New York city panel on climate change

1681064.action_summary: Promulgate rules as necessary for timely implementation of the independent expenditure disclosure requirements.
1681064.quote: the campaign finance board shall take such actions, including the promulgation of rules, as are necessary for timely implementation of this local law.

7406709.action_summary: Establish or adopt by rule a standard for listing natural gas alarms and rules governing their provision and installation.
7406709.quote: Natural gas alarms listed in accordance with a standard established or adopted by department rule shall be provided and installed in accordance with department rules.
affected_groups: owners of dwellings required to install natural gas alarms

7406709.action_summary: Submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a determination of the market availability of battery-powered natural gas alarms, indicating whether at least 4 distinct manufacturers of compliant battery-powered natural gas alarms have been identified.
7406709.quote: No later than July 1, 2026, the commissioner shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a determination of the market availability of battery-powered natural gas alarms.

7406709.action_summary: If market availability determination indicates fewer than 4 distinct manufacturers of battery-powered natural gas alarms, extend by rule the installation deadline to January 1, 2029.
7406709.quote: If such determination indicates less than 4 such manufacturers, the commissioner shall by rule extend the date by which such alarms must be installed in accordance with section 28-315.2.4 to January 1, 2029.

5983599.action_summary: Promulgate rules governing the calculation of greenhouse gas emissions for campus-style electric systems and buildings not connected to the utility distribution system.
5983599.quote: The department, in consultation with the office of long term planning and sustainability, shall promulgate rules governing the calculation of greenhouse gas emissions for campus-style electric systems that share on-site generation but make use of the utility distribution system and for buildings that are not connected to the utility distribution system.

5983599.action_summary: Determine the electricity grid marginal emissions factor for natural gas powered fuel cells and promulgate rules regarding such factor and emissions attributable to other energy sources.
5983599.quote: The amount of greenhouse gas emissions attributable to natural gas powered fuel cells shall be credited compared to the electricity grid marginal emissions factor that will be determined by the commissioner and promulgated into rules of the department.
affected_groups: covered building owners with fuel cell systems

5983599.action_summary: Audit no less than 25 percent of construction documents for multiple dwellings with specified affordability and regulatory status on a monthly basis.
5983599.quote: On a monthly basis, the commissioner shall audit no less than 25 percent of construction documents which are for multiple dwellings where 25 percent or more of the dwelling units are occupied and such multiple dwelling, in whole or in part, either (i) are subject to rent regulation, (ii) are being rehabilitated or maintained as affordable housing through a department of housing preservation and development program, (iii) are subject to a city regulatory agreement mandating the creation or preservation of a certain number of affordable units, (iv) contain affordable housing units created, sponsored or preserved through other city programs or initiatives, or (v) where the department knows or has reason to know, are the subject of a rent overcharge application which is in the process of being investigated by the New York State division of housing and community renewal.

5983599.action_summary: Perform final inspection for permitted work in R-2 occupancies listed on the Department of Housing Preservation and Development's website and charge a fee for such inspection.
5983599.quote: Final inspection shall be performed by the department for permitted work in R-2 occupancies if the building is listed on the department of housing preservation and development's website pursuant to paragraph 6 of subdivision m of section 27-2115 of the administrative code. The department shall charge a fee for such inspection.
5983599.deadline_text: within one year after the expiration of the last permit

5983599.action_summary: Not approve construction documents for construction or alteration in special flood hazard areas unless the application complies with the requirements of appendix G of the New York City Building Code.
5983599.quote: Within coastal special flood hazard areas and special flood hazard areas, the commissioner shall not approve construction documents for construction or alteration of buildings or structures, including alterations pursuant to section 28-101.4.3 of this code, or for any other activity regulated by section G201 of appendix G of the New York city building code, unless the application complies with the requirements of appendix G of the New York city building code.
affected_groups: property owners in flood hazard areas

5983599.action_summary: Limit by rule the amount of deduction authorized for renewable energy credits, considering availability, environmental justice impacts, and other relevant factors.
5983599.quote: The department shall by rule limit the amount of a deduction authorized pursuant to section 28-320.6.1. In determining such limit, the department shall consider items 1 through 3 of this section.

5983599.action_summary: Promulgate rules ensuring that greenhouse gas offsets exhibit environmental integrity principles including additionality, in consultation with the Office of Long-Term Planning and Sustainability.
5983599.quote: Such greenhouse gas offsets must exhibit environmental integrity principles, including additionality, in accordance with rules promulgated by the department in consultation with the office of long term planning and sustainability.

5983599.action_summary: Consult the advisory board on environmental justice before promulgating rules regarding greenhouse gas offset standards.
5983599.quote: Prior to the department promulgation of rules pursuant to this section, the department shall consult the advisory board on environmental justice as established by section 3-1006 of the administrative code.

5983599.action_summary: Establish by rule alternative pathways for individuals applying for limited hoisting machine operator licenses for articulating boom cranes, mini cranes, or other limited licenses within two years of the provision's effective date.
5983599.quote: The commissioner may, by rule, establish alternative pathways for individuals who, on or before the date that is two years after the effective date of this provision, apply for a limited license for articulating boom cranes, a limited license for mini cranes, or other limited license established by rule.
5983599.deadline_text: on or before the date that is two years after the effective date of this provision

7998285.actor_raw: an office or agency designated by the mayor
7998285.action_summary: Make biographical or background information about the person or entity for whom a street, park, playground, facility or structure was renamed or co-named available on its website within 90 days of the enactment of the local law which named the street, park, playground, facility or structure, or portion thereof.
7998285.quote: an office or agency designated by the mayor, shall make biographical or background information about the person or entity for whom the naming is on behalf of available on its website within 90 days of the enactment of the local law which named the street, park, playground, facility or structure, or portion thereof.
7998285.deadline_text: within 90 days of the enactment of the local law which named the street, park, playground, facility or structure, or portion thereof

7998285.actor_raw: an office or agency designated by the mayor
7998285.action_summary: Obtain biographical or background information about a person or entity for whom a street, park, playground, facility or structure, or portion thereof, was renamed or co-named from the legislative record or through its own research.
7998285.quote: An office or agency designated by the mayor pursuant to this section shall obtain biographical or background information about a person or entity for whom a street, park, playground, facility or structure, or portion thereof, was renamed or co-named from: (a) The legislative record for the local law that named such street, park, playground, facility or structure, or portion thereof; or (b) Where such legislative record does not include any such biographical or background information, any other source such office or agency identifies through its own research.

7998285.actor_raw: an office or agency designated by the mayor
7998285.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
7998285.action_summary: To the extent practicable, indicate on its website the source of any biographical or background information obtained through its own research.
7998285.quote: such office or agency shall, to the extent practicable, indicate on its website the source of any such information.

7998285.actor_raw: an office or agency designated by the mayor
7998285.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
7998285.action_summary: Indicate on its website that biographical or background information required to be made available is not available when such information cannot be obtained.
7998285.quote: such office or agency shall indicate on its website that such information is not available.

6565854.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6565854.action_summary: Coordinate with any other agency or public utility company affected by the department's resurfacing work.
6565854.quote: For any resurfacing work by the department that impacts the operations of any other agency or a public utility company, the department shall coordinate with such agency or company.

6565854.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6565854.action_summary: Complete resurfacing work within 15 business days after the completion of milling, where practicable.
6565854.quote: The department shall complete any resurfacing work within 15 business days after the completion of milling for such resurfacing, where practicable.
6565854.deadline_text: within 15 business days after the completion of milling

6565854.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6565854.action_summary: Post notice on the department's website and provide notice to affected community boards by electronic mail when resurfacing work requires additional time beyond 15 business days, including the reason for delay and new expected completion date.
6565854.quote: the department shall post a notice on the department's website and provide notice to the affected community board by electronic mail. Such notice shall include the reason the department requires additional time to complete such resurfacing and the new expected date of completion.

6695286.action_summary: Develop and make available a standardized food quality feedback survey to agencies that hold food service contracts, including questions assessing consumer satisfaction regarding food quality, taste, and cultural relevance.
6695286.quote: The office of food policy, in consultation with the department of health and mental hygiene, shall develop and make available a standardized food quality feedback survey to agencies that hold food service contracts.

6695286.action_summary: Beginning January 1, 2026, designate an agency or agencies holding a food service contract to participate in a six-month pilot program to evaluate the implementation of food quality feedback surveys.
6695286.quote: Beginning January 1, 2026, the mayor shall designate an agency or agencies holding a food service contract to participate in a six-month pilot program

6695286.actor_raw: each agency participating in the pilot program
6695286.action_summary: Post on its website a summary of the aggregate food quality feedback survey findings collected during the pilot period.
6695286.quote: Each agency participating in the pilot program established pursuant to subdivision b of this section shall, no later than 30 days after the conclusion of the pilot period, post on its website a summary of the aggregate food quality feedback survey findings
6695286.deadline_text: no later than 30 days after the conclusion of the pilot period

6695286.action_summary: Submit a summary to the mayor and the speaker of the council evaluating the effectiveness and feasibility of the pilot program and making recommendations for improving the methodology, implementation, and analysis of future food quality feedback surveys.
6695286.quote: No later than 120 days after the conclusion of the pilot period, the office of food policy shall submit a summary to the mayor and the speaker of the council evaluating the effectiveness and feasibility of the pilot program
6695286.deadline_text: no later than 120 days after the conclusion of the pilot period

6695286.action_summary: Provide the aggregate results of one or more food quality feedback surveys to the speaker of the council upon request.
6695286.quote: The aggregate results of one or more such surveys shall be provided to the speaker of the council upon request.

6695286.actor_raw: each agency designated to participate in the pilot program
6695286.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
6695286.action_summary: Require the food service contractor to administer food quality feedback surveys during the pilot period.
6695286.deadline_text: during the six-month pilot program beginning January 1, 2026

5669060.quote: No later than July 1, 2023, the administering agency shall establish, subject to appropriation, a three-year pilot program from which grants may be awarded to child care programs

5669060.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
5669060.action_summary: Promulgate rules to carry out the pilot program, including determining eligibility criteria for grants and establishing an equitable allocation method.

5669060.agency_full: Not specified in the law text

1194780.action_summary: Designate an agency to implement the animal abuse registry provisions and report the designation to the speaker of the council.
1194780.quote: The mayor or his designee shall designate an agency to implement the provisions of this chapter and shall report such designation to the speaker of the council.
affected_groups: persons convicted of animal abuse crimes

1194780.action_summary: Take all actions necessary for implementation of the animal abuse registry, including promulgation of rules.
1194780.quote: the commissioner of such agency shall take all actions necessary for its implementation, including the promulgation of rules, prior to such effective date.
affected_groups: persons convicted of animal abuse crimes

1194780.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1194780.action_summary: Create, manage and maintain an electronic registry of individuals living in the city who have been convicted of animal abuse crimes.
1194780.quote: The department shall create, manage and maintain an electronic registry of individuals living in the city of New York who have been convicted of an animal abuse crime and who have registered with the department pursuant to this chapter.

1194780.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1194780.action_summary: Grant authorized entities password-protected electronic access to query the registry using identifying information to determine if a person is prohibited from owning an animal.
1194780.quote: the department shall grant authorized entities the password-protected ability to electronically query the registry using a person's name, driver's license or non-driver photo ID card number, or other identifying information determined by the commissioner

1194780.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1194780.action_summary: Photograph registrants at the time of initial registration.
1194780.quote: The department shall photograph the registrant at the time of registration.
affected_groups: persons convicted of animal abuse crimes

1194780.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1194780.action_summary: Photograph registrants and verify the continuing accuracy of their registration information at annual appearances.
1194780.quote: At such appearance the department shall photograph the registrant and verify the continuing accuracy of the information provided by the registrant pursuant to subdivision c of this section.
affected_groups: persons convicted of animal abuse crimes

1194780.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
1194780.action_summary: Promulgate rules necessary for the implementation of the animal abuse registry chapter.
1194780.quote: The commissioner may promulgate rules necessary for the implementation of this chapter.
affected_groups: persons convicted of animal abuse crimes

2537041.action_summary: Issue notices of violations that state whether the violation is subject to the disaster exception and set forth the procedure and time period for correcting such violation without incurring a civil penalty.

2537041.quote: The notice of such violation shall state that such violation is subject to this exception and shall set forth the procedure and time period for correcting such violation without incurring a civil penalty.

2537041.agency_full: New York City Department of Sanitation
2537041.action_summary: Determine whether a natural or man-made disaster occurred within 30 days preceding issuance of a violation and whether a building or premises is within the affected area.

1739313.action_summary: Promulgate rules as necessary to effectuate the provisions of chapter 9 of title 20, including establishing civil penalties not exceeding two hundred fifty dollars for rule violations.
1739313.quote: The commissioner may promulgate such rules as he or she deems necessary to effectuate the provisions of this chapter, including, but not limited to, establishing civil penalties for the violation of such rules in amounts not exceeding two hundred fifty dollars for any such violation.

4286205.action_summary: Establish the position of public housing liaison to receive and process complaints regarding senior center facilities located on property owned by the New York City Housing Authority.
4286205.quote: There shall be in the department the position of public housing liaison whose duties shall include, but not be limited to the following: a. Establishing a system to receive and process complaints regarding senior center facilities located on property owned by the New York city housing authority, including assisting senior center participants with concerns about repairs at such facilities

4286205.action_summary: Conduct outreach to participants of senior centers located on New York City Housing Authority property about the existence of the public housing liaison, how to contact the liaison, and about existing systems for filing complaints or grievances.
4286205.quote: Conducting outreach to participants of senior centers located on property owned by the New York city housing authority about the existence of such liaison, how to contact such liaison, and about any existing system for filing complaints or grievances about senior centers with the department

4286205.action_summary: Make recommendations to the commissioner regarding how programs and facilities that receive department funding can better serve older adult public housing residents.
4286205.quote: Making recommendations to the commissioner with respect to how programs and facilities that receive funding from the department can better serve older adult public housing residents

4286205.action_summary: Coordinate with the New York City Housing Authority regarding facilities and other matters impacting older adults in public housing.
4286205.quote: Coordinating with the New York city housing authority, as necessary, about facilities and any other matters impacting older adults in public housing

2939942.action_summary: Establish registration process and set qualifications for construction superintendents in rules.
2939942.quote: Construction superintendents shall register with the department, in a form and manner acceptable to the department, and shall meet any qualifications set forth in rules by the department

2939942.action_summary: Upon request, receive and review site safety plans required to be kept on site for jobs requiring a primary construction superintendent.
2939942.quote: a site safety plan that meets the applicable requirements of Article 110 of Chapter 1 of Title 28 of the Administrative Code shall be kept on site and made available to the department upon request

2939942.action_summary: Accept immediate notification from construction superintendents of specified dangerous conditions including structural collapses, fires, explosions, and other listed hazardous conditions.
2939942.quote: The construction superintendent must immediately notify the department, in a form and manner acceptable to the department, when he or she discovers, at any job site for which the construction superintendent is responsible, any of the conditions listed in Section 3310.8.2.1

2939942.action_summary: Upon request, receive and review logs maintained by construction superintendents at each job site.
2939942.quote: Such log must be made available to the commissioner upon request

2939942.action_summary: Promulgate rules necessary for the implementation of construction superintendent requirements.
2939942.quote: the commissioner of buildings may take such measures as are necessary for its implementation, including the promulgation of rules, before such effective date

2324742.action_summary: Include a mandate in all new or renewed agreements with subcontractors having regular contact with the public to follow voter registration distribution guidelines.
2324742.citation: NYC Charter § 1057-a, as amended by Local Law 139 of 2016
2324742.quote: Participating agencies shall include a mandate in all new or renewed agreements with those subcontractors having regular contact with the public in the daily administration of their business to follow the guidelines of this section.

2324742.action_summary: Provide assistance in completing distributed voter registration forms, including the organ donor section, if requested.
2324742.citation: NYC Charter § 1057-a § 2, as amended by Local Law 139 of 2016
2324742.quote: Participating agency staff shall provide assistance in completing these distributed voter registration forms, including the section of the form allowing for registration to become an organ donor, and in cases in which such an agency would provide assistance with its own form, such agency shall provide the same degree of assistance with regard to the voter registration and organ donor forms as is provided with regard to the completion of its own form, if so requested.

2324742.action_summary: Include a voter registration form with any agency communication sent through the United States mail for the purpose of supplying clients with application, renewal, recertification, or change of address materials.
2324742.citation: NYC Charter § 1057-a § 2, as amended by Local Law 139 of 2016
2324742.quote: Participating agencies shall also include a voter registration form with any agency communication sent through the United States mail for the purpose of supplying clients with application, renewal or recertification for services and change of address relating to such services materials.

2324742.action_summary: Incorporate an opportunity to request a voter registration application into any application for services, renewal, recertification, or change of address provided on computer terminals, the World Wide Web, or the Internet.
2324742.citation: NYC Charter § 1057-a § 2, as amended by Local Law 139 of 2016
2324742.quote: Participating agencies shall also incorporate an opportunity to request a voter registration application into any application for services, renewal or recertification for services and change of address relating to such services provided on computer terminals, the World Wide Web or the Internet.

2324742.action_summary: Send a voter registration form to persons requesting it via computer terminals, the World Wide Web, or the Internet, or direct them to where such a form may be downloaded.
2324742.citation: NYC Charter § 1057-a § 2, as amended by Local Law 139 of 2016
2324742.quote: Any person indicating that they wish to be sent a voter registration form, via computer terminals, the World Wide Web or the Internet shall be sent such a form by the participating agency, or directed to a bank on that system where such a form may be downloaded.

7955161.action_summary: Hold the first meeting of the advisory board and at that meeting set a date for one or more public hearings to solicit testimony on the development of a citywide wildlife management plan.
7955161.quote: The advisory board shall hold its first meeting no later than 180 days after the effective date of this local law. At such meeting, the advisory board shall set a date for one or more public hearings to solicit testimony from the public and other stakeholders
7955161.deadline_text: no later than 180 days after the effective date of this local law

7955161.action_summary: Submit a citywide wildlife management plan to the mayor and the speaker of the council that includes an analysis of challenges to wildlife management, proposed strategies, policies, and recommendations.
7955161.quote: The advisory board shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a citywide wildlife management plan no later than 18 months after the effective date of this local law. Such plan shall include, but need not be limited to
7955161.deadline_text: no later than 18 months after the effective date of this local law

7955161.actor_raw: the mayor's office of animal welfare
7955161.action_summary: Submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council regarding programs relating to wildlife management in the city, beginning no later than one year after termination of the advisory board and every two years thereafter.
7955161.quote: the mayor's office of animal welfare, in consultation with the department of parks and recreation, shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a report regarding programs relating to wildlife management in the city
7955161.deadline_text: No later than 1 year after the termination of the wildlife management advisory board

7731697.action_summary: Adopt a written radio encryption policy governing department radio communications that meets specified requirements regarding critical incident broadcasts, encrypted channel access for professional journalists, and protection of sensitive information.
7731697.quote: The department shall adopt a written radio encryption policy governing department radio communications. Such policy shall meet the following requirements
7731697.deadline_text: no more than 12 months after the effective date of the local law that added this section

7731697.action_summary: Publish a proposal of the radio encryption policy on the department's website for public comment.
7731697.quote: The department shall publish a proposal of the policy required by subdivision b of this section on the department's website no more than 180 days after the effective date of the local law that added this section.
7731697.deadline_text: no more than 180 days after the effective date of the local law that added this section

7731697.action_summary: Consider public comments on the proposed policy and publish the final policy with an explanation of changes made in response to comments on the department's website, and provide copies to the speaker of the council and the mayor.
7731697.quote: The commissioner shall consider public comments and include in the publication of the final policy an explanation of any changes that were made in response to comments. Such final policy shall be provided to the speaker of the council and the mayor and shall be posted on the department's website no more than 45 days after the conclusion of the public comment period
7731697.deadline_text: no more than 45 days after the conclusion of the public comment period established pursuant to subdivision c of this section

7731697.action_summary: Implement the final radio encryption policy.
7731697.quote: The department shall implement the final policy required by subdivision d no more than 12 months after the effective date of the local law that added this section.
7731697.deadline_text: no more than 12 months after the effective date of the local law that added this section

6874682.action_summary: Conduct a study examining the impacts of algorithmic tools and automated employment decision tools on employees and the administration of their municipal duties.
6874682.quote: The department shall, in consultation with the department of citywide administrative services, the mayor's office of operations, and other stakeholders deemed relevant by the commissioner, examine the impacts of algorithmic tools and automated employment decision tools on employees and the administration of their municipal duties.

6874682.action_summary: Submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a report on the findings of the study and any recommendations related to the impacts of algorithmic tools and automated employment decision tools on employees.
6874682.quote: The department shall, within 3 months of the completion of the study required by subdivision b of section 1 of this local law, submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a report on the findings of such study and any recommendations
6874682.deadline_text: within 3 months of the completion of the study required by subdivision b of section 1 of this local law

6874682.action_summary: Notify the corporation counsel for the purpose of effectuating section 7-111 of the administrative code upon submission of the report.
6874682.quote: Upon such submission, the mayor shall notify the corporation counsel for the purpose of effectuating section 7-111 of the administrative code of the city of New York.

6831564.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6831564.action_summary: Establish a pilot program to allow for-hire vehicles to park in commercial parking meter areas subject to specified conditions including payment requirements and a maximum 3-hour parking duration.
6831564.quote: the department shall establish a pilot program to allow for-hire vehicles to park in commercial parking meter areas, provided that no person shall park a for-hire vehicle, whether attended or not, in a commercial parking meter area pursuant to such pilot program
6831564.deadline_text: no later than 180 days after the effective date of this local law

6831564.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
6831564.action_summary: Submit a report to the mayor and speaker of the council evaluating the effects of the pilot program on efficient delivery of goods, enforcement of parking rules, utilization of commercial parking meter areas, and driver health and safety, including feasibility recommendations for duration limits and area restrictions.
6831564.quote: the department shall submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council evaluating the effects of such pilot program on, and proposing any recommendations for future changes to law, rule, or policy related to: (i) the efficient and orderly delivery of goods in commercial parking meter areas; (ii) enforcement of rules relating to parking, stopping, and standing in commercial parking meter areas; (iii) the utilization of commercial parking meter areas by for-hire vehicles and commercial vehicles; and (iv) the health, safety, and well-being of for-hire vehicle drivers.
6831564.deadline_text: No later than 1 year after the commencement of the pilot program conducted pursuant to subdivision b of this local law

7681683.action_summary: Make quarterly payments of at least 25 percent of the fiscal year budget to contractors on covered contracts at the beginning of each quarter, with the first payment due upon comptroller registration.
7681683.quote: a contracting agency shall make a payment to a contractor of at least 25 percent of the fiscal year budget for such contract for the current fiscal year at the beginning of each quarter of such fiscal year
affected_groups: individuals served by criminal justice programs

7681683.actor_raw: the office of management and budget in the executive office of the mayor
7681683.agency_full: Mayor's Office of Management and Budget
7681683.action_summary: Provide written notice within 10 days to contracting agencies and the speaker of the council of any determination to defer quarterly payments due to fiscal constraints, including reason and expected duration.
7681683.quote: the office of management and budget shall provide, within 10 days of the determination of such deferral, written notice to contracting agencies and the speaker of the council of such deferral, the reason for the determination, and the expected duration of such deferral
7681683.deadline_text: within 10 days of the determination of such deferral

7681683.actor_raw: the office of management and budget in the executive office of the mayor
7681683.agency_full: Mayor's Office of Management and Budget
7681683.action_summary: Provide additional written notice to contracting agencies and the speaker of the council of any subsequent determination to cancel a payment deferral.
7681683.quote: The office of management and budget shall provide additional written notice to contracting agencies and the speaker of the council of any subsequent determination to cancel such deferral

7681683.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing a process for contracting agencies to recover monies paid pursuant to quarterly payment requirements where the amount paid exceeds the value of services received, including standard audit requirements.
7681683.quote: The office of contract services shall promulgate rules establishing a process for the contracting agency to recover from a contractor monies paid pursuant to paragraph 2 of this subdivision where the amount of monies paid exceeds the value of the services received and accepted by such contracting agency, including, but not limited to, rules to establish standard audit requirements

7681683.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a report on the implementation of quarterly payments for covered contracts, including number and value of contracts, instances of nonpayment or delayed payment, contractor feedback, and recommendations.
7681683.quote: No later than December 31, 2028, the office of contract services shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a report on the implementation of quarterly payments for covered contracts

7681683.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing criteria for eligibility of contracts for the pilot program, including eligibility requirements and rules for implementation and management of the pilot program.
7681683.quote: The office of contract services shall promulgate rules establishing criteria for the eligibility of contracts for the pilot program established pursuant to this section, including, but not limited to, that such contracts (a) are registered on or after July 1, 2029, (b) have a contract value of 1 million dollars or more, (c) have not been designated as federal subrecipient awards in accordance with 2 CFR 200.331, (d) are not subject, in whole or part, to payment requirements imposed by an agency of the state of New York that are inconsistent with the payment requirements of this subdivision, and (e) are not covered contracts

7681683.action_summary: Promulgate rules necessary for the implementation and management of the quarterly payment pilot program for other human services contracts.
7681683.quote: The office of contract services shall promulgate rules necessary for the implementation and management of the pilot program pursuant to this subdivision, provided that any such rule be superseded by any applicable rule of the procurement policy board

7681683.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website an annual report on the implementation of quarterly payments on pilot contracts, beginning December 31, 2030 and annually thereafter until expiration of the pilot program.
7681683.quote: Beginning on December 31, 2030 and annually thereafter until the expiration of the pilot program established pursuant to this subdivision, the office of contract services shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a report on the implementation of quarterly payments on pilot contracts
7681683.deadline_text: Beginning on December 31, 2030 and annually thereafter until the expiration of the pilot program

7681683.action_summary: Submit to the council an evaluation of the pilot program and, if appropriate, a plan to make such pilot program permanent.
7681683.quote: No later than December 31, 2030, the mayor shall submit to the council an evaluation of the pilot program established by this subdivision and, if appropriate, a plan to make such pilot program permanent

7681683.action_summary: Promulgate rules as necessary for implementation of the quarterly payment requirements for covered contracts.
7681683.quote: and may promulgate any rules necessary for the implementation of this subdivision, provided that any such rule shall be superseded by any applicable rule of the procurement policy board

7075832.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
7075832.action_summary: Test no fewer than 3 different types of high visibility pavement marking products not currently utilized by the department, evaluating their durability, visibility in poor driving conditions, and operational feasibility for widespread use.
7075832.quote: the department shall test no fewer than 3 different types of high visibility pavement marking products that are not currently utilized by the department, except that if fewer than 3 such products may be procured by the department then only those products that may be procured shall be tested

7075832.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
7075832.action_summary: If feasibility and safety improvement are determined, establish a pilot program to install high visibility pavement markings in at least 5 locations in each borough, prioritizing locations with histories of traffic-related injuries or fatalities.
7075832.quote: if the commissioner determines that a high visibility pavement marking would both be feasible to install throughout the city and likely to improve traffic safety during poor driving conditions, the commissioner shall establish a pilot program no later than January 1, 2028 to install such high visibility pavement markings in at least 5 locations in each borough

7075832.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
7075832.action_summary: Submit to the mayor and speaker of the council a report detailing the findings of the testing program, including challenges, issues, and a recommendation on whether to conduct a pilot program.
7075832.quote: the commissioner shall submit to the mayor and speaker of the council a report detailing the findings of such testing program, including any challenges and issues presented by such testing program, and a recommendation on whether to conduct a pilot program
7075832.deadline_text: No later than 2 months after the conclusion of the testing program

7075832.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
7075832.action_summary: If a pilot program is established, submit to the mayor and speaker of the council a report one year after its conclusion with a recommendation on whether to expand or make permanent the program and identifying any challenges and issues.
7075832.quote: if a pilot program is established pursuant to subdivision c of this local law, 1 year after the conclusion of such pilot program, the commissioner shall submit to the mayor and speaker of the council a report that includes a recommendation on whether to expand or make permanent such program, and shall also identify any challenges and issues presented by such pilot program
7075832.deadline_text: 1 year after the conclusion of such pilot program

7318902.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
7318902.action_summary: Make a payment of at least 50 percent of the fiscal year budget for each contract with an eligible non-profit organization for human services within 30 days of registration, and for contracts extending beyond one fiscal year, make such payment upon the start of each fiscal year succeeding registration.
7318902.quote: the city shall make a payment of at least 50 percent of the fiscal year budget for such contract within 30 days of registration of such contract, and for each contract with a duration that extends beyond one fiscal year, the city shall make such payment upon the start of each fiscal year succeeding such registration
7318902.deadline_text: within 30 days of registration of such contract

7318902.actor_raw: the office of management and budget in the executive office of the mayor
7318902.agency_full: Mayor's Office of Management and Budget
7318902.action_summary: Provide written notice to contracting agencies and the speaker of the council within 10 days of determining a deferral of payment, including the reason and expected duration.
7318902.quote: the office of management and budget shall provide, within 10 days of the determination of such deferral, written notice to contracting agencies and the speaker of the council of such deferral, the reason for the determination, and the expected duration of such deferral
7318902.deadline_text: within 10 days of the determination of such deferral

7318902.actor_raw: the office of management and budget
7318902.agency_full: Mayor's Office of Management and Budget
7318902.action_summary: Provide additional written notice to contracting agencies and the speaker of the council of any subsequent determination to cancel a deferral.
7318902.quote: The office of management and budget shall provide additional written notice to contracting agencies and the speaker of the council of any subsequent determination to cancel such deferral

7318902.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing a process for contracting agencies to recover monies paid to contractors where the amount paid exceeds the value of services received and accepted.
7318902.quote: The office of contract services shall promulgate rules establishing a process for the contracting agency to recover from a contractor monies paid pursuant to paragraph 1 of this subdivision where the amount of monies paid exceeds the value of the services received and accepted

7318902.action_summary: Enact any additional rules necessary for the implementation of this subdivision.
7318902.quote: may enact any additional rules necessary for the implementation of this subdivision, provided that any such rule shall be superseded by any applicable rule of the procurement policy board

6584173.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
6584173.action_summary: File a strategic planning report with the mayor, speaker, public advocate, borough presidents, and community boards establishing and maintaining a citywide public bathroom network that meets or exceeds a target metric of 2,120 public bathrooms, of which at least half shall be publicly owned.
6584173.quote: the relevant agency shall file with the mayor, the speaker of the council, the public advocate, each borough president, and each community board a strategic planning report to establish and maintain a citywide public bathroom network.
6584173.deadline_text: No later than September 1, 2026, and every fourth year thereafter

6584173.actor_raw: an agency or office designated by the mayor
6584173.action_summary: Post or update on its website and make compatible for access on a mobile device a map of existing and planned public bathrooms with specified information including hours of operation, repair status, accessibility, fees, maintenance responsibility, expected opening dates, and facility features.
6584173.quote: an agency or office designated by the mayor shall post or update on its website and make compatible for access on a mobile device a map of existing and planned public bathrooms.
6584173.deadline_text: Upon the submission of the report required by subdivision b of this section

7086114.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
7086114.action_summary: Ensure that pavement markings or temporary markings are installed within 5 business days after completion of any street resurfacing, where practicable.
7086114.quote: the department shall, where practicable, ensure that pavement markings or temporary markings are installed within 5 business days after the completion of such resurfacing.
7086114.deadline_text: within 5 business days after the completion of such resurfacing

7086114.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
7086114.action_summary: Submit an annual report to the mayor and speaker of the council and post it on the department's website detailing pavement marking installations following street resurfacing, disaggregated by borough, compliance with the 5 business day deadline, and reasons for non-compliance.
7086114.quote: the department shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council and post on the department's website a report that includes: (a) The number of streets where, during the preceding year, the department installed pavement markings following the resurfacing of such street, disaggregated by borough; (b) The percentage of such streets for which pavement markings or temporary markings were installed within 5 business days after the completion of such resurfacing; and (c) For any such resurfacing completed during the preceding year where pavement markings or temporary markings were not installed within 5 business days after the completion of such resurfacing, the reason they were not installed within such time.
7086114.deadline_text: No later than March 1 of each year

6555128.action_summary: Establish a truth and reconciliation process with objectives to establish historical facts about slavery and its legacies in New York City, protect and acknowledge affected persons and communities, and recommend policy and social changes.
6555128.quote: CORE shall establish a truth and reconciliation process with the following objectives: 1. Establishing historical facts about slavery and its legacies in or in connection with the city of New York

6555128.action_summary: Deliver to the mayor and speaker of the council, and post publicly on its website, a plan describing the scope and implementation for a truth and reconciliation process.
6555128.quote: Not later than June 19, 2027, CORE shall deliver to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and shall post publicly on its website, a plan describing the scope and implementation for a truth and reconciliation process

6555128.action_summary: Submit to the mayor and speaker of the council, and post publicly on its website, a written update on selection and terms of engagement with community stakeholders and persons with expertise in truth and reconciliation.
6555128.quote: No later than January 15, 2026, CORE shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and post publicly on its website, a written update on its selection, and terms of engagement with, community stakeholders and persons with expertise in truth and reconciliation

6555128.action_summary: Submit to the mayor and speaker of the council, and post publicly on its website, a progress report on research process and preliminary findings in preparing the plan required by subdivision b of section 34-201.
6555128.quote: No later than January 15, 2027, and in consultation with community stakeholders and persons with expertise in truth and reconciliation, CORE shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and post publicly on its website, a progress report on CORE's research process and preliminary findings in preparing the plan required by subdivision b of this section

6555128.action_summary: Select a minimum of 5 sites on which to establish public forums for truth and reconciliation proceedings, with a minimum of 1 site in each borough.
6555128.quote: CORE, in consultation with community stakeholders, shall select a minimum of 5 sites on which to establish public forums for truth and reconciliation proceedings, as follows: 1. CORE shall select a minimum of 1 site in each borough.

6555128.action_summary: List the location, schedule of meetings, and topic or topics to be addressed at each public forum on its website, and publish materials, video recordings, public testimony, and other research from each public forum on its website as they become available.
6555128.quote: CORE shall list the location, schedule of meetings, and topic or topics to be addressed at each public forum on its website, and to the extent feasible publish materials, video recordings, public testimony, and other research from each public forum on its website as they become available.

6555128.action_summary: Conduct a public outreach and information campaign designed to encourage awareness of, engagement with, and participation in the truth and reconciliation process and findings.
6555128.quote: Beginning no later than July 1, 2025, and ending no earlier than 365 days after the conclusion of the truth and reconciliation process required by this chapter, CORE, in consultation with the civic engagement commission, the commission on human rights, and the office of ethnic and community media, shall conduct a public outreach and information campaign designed to encourage awareness of, engagement with, and participation in the truth and reconciliation process and findings.

6555128.action_summary: Issue terms and guidelines for the creation and safeguarding of a physically and psychologically secure space and process for truth and reconciliation.
6555128.quote: CORE shall issue terms and guidelines for the creation and safeguarding of a physically and psychologically secure space and process for truth and reconciliation.

6555128.action_summary: Post public notice of the time and place of meetings, hearings, and other proceedings relating to truth and reconciliation, including notice to the news media, in designated public locations, and on its website.
6555128.quote: CORE shall post public notice of the time and place of meetings, hearings, and other proceedings of CORE in which it is planned to address matters relating to truth and reconciliation. Wherever practicable, such proceedings shall be scheduled and publicly noticed at least 30 days in advance

6555128.action_summary: Provide appropriate staff and resources to facilitate and support any reasonably defined inquiry authorized by the chair or CORE.
6555128.quote: Pursuant to request by the chair or CORE, city agencies shall provide appropriate staff and resources to facilitate and support any reasonably defined inquiry authorized by this section.

6555128.action_summary: Publish a report on the history and legacies of slavery in the city of New York, documenting findings and experiences from the truth and reconciliation process and recommending steps the city can take to address race-based discrimination and injustice.
6555128.quote: No later than 1 year following the conclusion of the truth and reconciliation process required by this chapter, CORE shall publish a report on the history and legacies of slavery in the city of New York, including but not limited to the legacies and badges of such slavery, if any, that continue to undermine racial equity in the city of New York in the present day.
6555128.deadline_text: No later than 1 year following the conclusion of the truth and reconciliation process

6555128.action_summary: Preserve working documents, videos, transcripts, and operational and administrative records and recommend means of memorializing and making available to the public its records and findings for the purpose of public education and engagement in perpetuity.
6555128.quote: CORE shall preserve its working documents, videos, transcripts, and operational and administrative records and shall recommend, as part of the report required by section 34-206, a means of memorializing and making available to the public its records and findings for the purpose of public education and engagement in perpetuity.

5668979.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
5668979.action_summary: Post on its website information and resources for potential abortion patients, including abortion methods, health risks, and recovery information, translated into designated citywide languages.
5668979.quote: the department shall post on its website, and update as appropriate, information and resources for a potential patient of an abortion provider, which shall include, but need not be limited to, information outlining methods used to provide an abortion, attendant health risks and recovery from an abortion. Such information and resources shall be translated into the designated citywide languages.

5668979.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
5668979.action_summary: Survey abortion providers in the city to assess the availability and demand for language access services in connection with providing abortions, including methods of delivery, funding sources, and implementation challenges.
5668979.quote: the department shall survey abortion providers in the city to assess the availability of language access services for abortion and the demand for such services. Such needs assessment shall include, but need not be limited to, a survey of: 1. Language access services used in connection with providing abortions; 2. Preferred methods for delivery of language access services used in connection with providing abortions; 3. Public and private funding for language access services used in connection with providing abortions; and 4. Implementation challenges with language access services used in connection with providing abortions.

5668979.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
5668979.action_summary: Submit a report to the mayor and speaker of the council with findings and recommendations from the needs assessment, including best practices for language access services and city actions to assist abortion providers, and post the report on its website.
5668979.quote: the department shall submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council with recommendations resulting from such needs assessment and shall post such report on its website. Such report shall include, but not be limited to, the following information: 1. A summary of the findings of such needs assessment; 2. Recommendations for language access services based on such findings; 3. In consultation with the mayor's office of immigrant affairs, recommended best practices for language access services and for identifying providers of language access services; and 4. An assessment of actions the city could take to assist abortion providers with access to language access services, including, but not limited to, the practicability of providing grants to abortion providers to assist in such access, and methods of connecting abortion providers with healthcare providers that have implemented language access services.
5668979.deadline_text: No later than 30 days after completion of the needs assessment required by subdivision c of this section

5190185.action_summary: Publish a non-partisan, impartial voter guide in at least two media formats (printed and online) and distribute one copy of the printed guide to each household with at least one registered voter eligible to vote in the election.
5190185.quote: the publication of a non-partisan, impartial voter guide in at least two media formats, including but not necessarily limited to a printed voter guide and a voter guide to be published online, providing information on candidates, ballot proposals and referenda, and the distribution of one copy of such printed guide to each household in which there is at least one registered voter

5190185.action_summary: Comply with voter requests to opt out of receiving a printed copy of the voter guide to the extent feasible.
5190185.quote: A voter may opt out of receiving a copy of such printed guide and the board shall comply with this request to the extent feasible.

5190185.action_summary: Coordinate with good government organizations, disability organizations, limited English proficiency organizations, the mayor's office for people with disabilities, and the 311 customer service center to improve public awareness of candidates, proposals, and referenda.
5190185.quote: The board shall coordinate with good government organizations, organizations representing or run by people with disabilities, organizations representing or run by people with limited English proficiency, and other agencies, including but not necessarily limited to the mayor's office for people with disabilities and the 311 customer service center, as necessary to improve public awareness of candidates, proposals, and referenda as provided by this chapter.

5190185.action_summary: Publish annually the names of organizations with which the board collaborates to improve public awareness of candidates, proposals, and referenda.
5190185.quote: The board shall publish on an annual basis the names of any organizations with which it collaborates pursuant to this paragraph.

5190185.action_summary: Prepare and publish each voter guide in English and in each designated citywide language and promulgate rules for preparation and publication of voter guides in any other languages determined necessary and appropriate.
5190185.quote: The board shall prepare and publish each voter guide, regardless of format, in English and in each of the designated citywide languages as defined in section 23-1101 of the administrative code and shall promulgate such rules as it deems necessary for the preparation and publication of voter guides in any other languages the board determines to be necessary and appropriate

5190185.action_summary: Include brief video statements from eligible candidates in the online voter guide and ensure videos have captioning in English and designated citywide languages and American Sign Language translation.
5190185.quote: The online voter guide published by the board pursuant to paragraph 1 of subdivision b of section 1052 of this charter shall include a brief video statement from each candidate who: (a) is on the ballot in a contested primary or general election for the office of mayor, public advocate, borough president, comptroller or city council; (b) has agreed to participate in such a candidate video statement; and (c) has met any further requirements established by the board by rule.
affected_groups: individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing

5190185.action_summary: Promulgate rules to ensure candidate video statements are accessible to individuals with vision disabilities and any additional rules necessary for implementation.
5190185.quote: The board shall promulgate rules to ensure that any candidate video statements included in the online voter guide are accessible to individuals with vision disabilities and may promulgate any additional rules that it determines to be necessary for the implementation of this subdivision.

5190185.action_summary: Make all candidate video statements available to any city-owned or operated television channels for broadcast.
5190185.quote: The board shall make all candidate video statements created pursuant to this subdivision available to any city-owned or operated television channels for broadcast on such channels.

5190185.action_summary: Collaborate with public libraries and other organizations to make printed voter guide information available in formats accessible to individuals with print or vision disabilities.
5190185.quote: For any election in which the board publishes a printed voter guide pursuant to subdivision b of section 1052 of this charter, the board shall collaborate with public libraries and other organizations, as necessary, to cause the information in such printed voter guide to be made available in a format that is accessible to individuals with print or vision disabilities.

5190185.action_summary: Withhold five percent of public funds payments to candidates until final pre-election payment and deny payment to candidates who fail to provide required submissions for video statements in the online voter guide.
5190185.quote: the board shall withhold five percent of all public funds payments to participating candidates until the final pre-election payment for any given election; and further provided that, in addition to any other reason for withholding or non-payment pursuant to applicable law or board rules, such withheld funds shall not be payable to any candidate who is on the ballot in a contested primary or general election for the office of mayor, public advocate, borough president, comptroller or city council and fails to provide, to the satisfaction of the board, such submissions as may be requested by the board for the purpose of publishing a video statement in the online voter guide. The board shall provide each candidate with a written determination specifying the basis for any non-payment.

5190185.action_summary: Provide candidates a process to petition for reconsideration of non-payment determinations within five business days of filing.
5190185.quote: The board shall provide candidates with a process by which they may immediately upon receipt of such determination petition the board for reconsideration of any such non-payment and such reconsideration shall occur within five business days of the filing of such petition.
5190185.deadline_text: such reconsideration shall occur within five business days of the filing of such petition

5190185.action_summary: Immediately notify candidates of their right to bring a special proceeding if the board denies a petition for reconsideration of non-payment.
5190185.quote: In the event that the board denies such petition then it shall immediately notify the candidate of such candidate's right to bring a special proceeding pursuant to article 78 of the civil practice law and rules.

4649786.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
