4649786.action_summary: Prescribe the form of petitions for revocable consents for sidewalk cafes and permit petitioners to develop required drawings without requiring professional third-party development, review, or approval.
4649786.quote: The petition shall be in such form as prescribed by the department[.] and shall include an accurate drawing of required clearances, space to be occupied, and the locations of tables and chairs; provided, however that the department shall permit such drawings to be developed by the petitioner and shall not require that such drawings be developed, reviewed, or approved by an architect, engineer, or other professional third party.
affected_groups: petitioners for sidewalk cafe revocable consents

4649786.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
4649786.action_summary: Forward copies of sidewalk cafe petitions to the Department of City Planning, Department of Environmental Protection, and Landmarks Preservation Commission within five days of filing.
4649786.quote: The petition shall be filed with the department which, within five days of the filing of such petition shall forward copies thereof to the department of city planning, the department of environmental protection and the landmarks preservation commission for review pursuant to subdivision b of this section.
4649786.deadline_text: within five days of the filing of such petition
affected_groups: petitioners for sidewalk cafe revocable consents

4649786.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
4649786.action_summary: Forward copies of sidewalk cafe petitions to the Speaker of the Council and the Council member in whose district the cafe is proposed for informational purposes within five days of filing.
4649786.quote: The department shall forward copies of the petition, within five days of the filing of such petition, to the speaker of the council and to the council member in whose district the cafe is proposed to be located, for informational purposes.
4649786.deadline_text: within five days of the filing of such petition
affected_groups: petitioners for sidewalk cafe revocable consents

4649786.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
4649786.action_summary: Forward copies of sidewalk cafe petitions to the borough president, Speaker of the Council, and Council member within five days of filing for informational purposes, and to the community board for review.
4649786.quote: The department shall forward copies of the petition, within five days of the filing of such petition, to the president of the borough in which the cafe is proposed to be located, the speaker of the council and the council member in whose district the cafe is proposed to be located, for information purposes, and to the community board for the community district in which the cafe is proposed to be located, for review pursuant to subdivision b of this section.
4649786.deadline_text: within five days of the filing of such petition
affected_groups: petitioners for sidewalk cafe revocable consents

4920277.action_summary: State in writing to the interagency green team what action will be taken with respect to each recommendation from the innovation review board and the reasons for the action taken.
4920277.quote: The commissioner shall state in writing to the interagency green team established pursuant to subdivision i of section twenty of the charter what action the commissioner shall take with respect to each such recommendation and the reasons for the action taken.

4920277.action_summary: Maintain a separate list of alteration permits issued for cellular antenna erection or placement and make it available to the public upon request and in electronic format on the department website.
4920277.quote: The commissioner shall maintain a separate list of alteration permits issued for the erection or placement of antennae used to provide cellular telephone or similar service or any structure related to such service which shall, at a minimum, set forth the name, business address and business telephone number of the applicant, the date of the application, the date the permit was issued, the location for which the permit was issued, including the premises address and the zoning district, whether residential, commercial, or manufacturing, and the number of permits issued for such purpose at the same location. Such list shall be made available to the public upon request between regular business hours and shall be available to the public in electronic format on a 24-hour basis on the department's website.

4920277.actor_raw: the commissioner, the fire commissioner and the commissioner of the department of environmental protection
4920277.agency: the commissioner, the fire commissioner and the commissioner of the department of environmental protection
4920277.agency_full: the commissioner, the fire commissioner and the commissioner of the department of environmental protection
4920277.action_summary: Establish a procedure to share information regarding violations issued as a result of inspections of buildings meeting agreed-upon criteria that are relevant to each department's responsibilities.
4920277.quote: The commissioner, the fire commissioner and the commissioner of the department of environmental protection shall share information regarding violations issued as a result of inspections of buildings meeting agreed-upon criteria that are relevant to the responsibilities of each department.

4920277.action_summary: Create and make publicly available in print and on the department website a manual explaining flood construction and protection requirements and standards in plain English, Spanish, and other languages.
4920277.quote: The commissioner shall create and make publicly available, in print and on the department's website, a manual explaining in detail the flood construction and protection requirements and standards applicable to the city. Such manual shall be made available in plain English and Spanish and in other languages as determined by the commissioner and shall be updated as necessary to reflect changes to applicable flood construction requirements and standards.

4920277.action_summary: Develop an outreach program through or in cooperation with other city agencies to manufacturers, installers, and business groups regarding security grille permit requirements, penalties, and available financial assistance.
4920277.quote: The commissioner shall, through or in cooperation with the department of small business services, the department of consumer affairs, and other city agencies deemed appropriate, develop an outreach program to manufacturers and installers of security grilles, business improvement districts, local development corporations, chambers of commerce and community boards to alert these groups and the businesses that utilize security grilles of the permit requirements and the requirements of this section, the penalties associated with violation thereof and the availability of any business loans, grants or tax subsidies related to the installation or use of such security grilles.

4920277.action_summary: Post on the department website on a monthly basis in machine-readable format a list of every incident on construction sites resulting in a fatality or injury requiring emergency medical services.
4920277.quote: The commissioner shall, by January 2018 and on a monthly basis thereafter, post on the department's website, in a machine-readable format, a list of every incident, reported to the department in accordance with section 28-103.21.1, that occurred on every construction site where construction work subject to permitting by the commissioner resulted in (i) a fatality to any individual, including a member of the general public or a construction worker, or (ii) an injury to any individual, including a member of the general public or a construction worker, that requires transport by emergency medical services or requires immediate emergency care at a hospital or offsite medical clinic, regardless of whether such incident involved a violation of this code or any other law or rule.

4920277.action_summary: Conduct inspections of occupied multiple dwellings with immediately hazardous complaints related to work without a permit within 12 hours of receipt, or by 10:00 a.m. the next day if received after 8:00 p.m.
4920277.quote: For immediately hazardous complaints related to work without a permit in occupied multiple dwellings, the real time enforcement unit shall conduct inspections of such occupied multiple dwellings within 12 hours of the receipt of such complaints, except that complaints received after 8:00 p.m. shall be inspected by 10:00 a.m. on the following day.

4920277.action_summary: Conduct initial inspections of no fewer than five percent of occupied multiple dwellings with valid permits for alteration or addition within 20 days of commencement of work.
4920277.quote: The real time enforcement unit shall also conduct initial inspections of no fewer than five percent of occupied multiple dwellings with valid permits for alteration or addition as described in section 28-103.30.2, within 20 days of commencement of work for such alterations or additions and shall conduct periodic unannounced inspections thereafter until such work is complete.
4920277.deadline_text: within 20 days of commencement of work

4920277.action_summary: In October of each year, submit electronically to the city council and post on the department website a report containing specified information regarding site safety manager and site safety coordinator certifications.
4920277.quote: In October of each year, the commissioner shall electronically submit to the city council and post on the department's website a report that includes the following information regarding site safety managers and site safety coordinators: 1. The (i) number of active site safety manager certificates and (ii) number of active site safety coordinator certificates; 2. The (i) number of active site safety manager certificates on the last day of the preceding year and (ii) number of active site safety coordinator certificates on the last day of the preceding year; 3. The (i) number of sites for which a site safety manager was required by this code during the preceding year and (ii) number of such sites for which a site safety manager was required by this code but for which a site safety coordinator may be designated in lieu of such manager pursuant to the exception to section 3310.5 of the New York city building code; 4. The (i) number of site safety manager certificates issued in the preceding year and (ii) number of site safety coordinator certificates issued in the preceding year; 5. The (i) number of applicants for site safety manager certificates who submitted applications during the preceding year and (ii) number of applicants for site safety coordinator certificates who submitted applications during the preceding year; 6. The (i) average length of time for an applicant who submitted an application for a site safety manager certificate during the preceding year to receive such certificate, measured from the date a completed application is submitted to the department and (ii) average length of time for an applicant who submitted an application for a site safety coordinator certificate during the preceding year to receive such certificate, measured from the date a completed application is submitted to the department; and 7. The (i) average length of time for an applicant who submitted an application for a site safety manager certificate during the preceding year to complete a background check, if any, for such certificate, measured from the date such applicant submitted all documentation necessary to complete such check, (ii) average length of time for an applicant who submitted an application for a site safety coordinator certificate during the preceding year to complete a background check, if any, for such certificate, measured from the date such applicant submitted all documentation necessary to complete such check (iii) the main three reasons for completions of background checks for applicants who submitted applications for site safety manager certificates during the preceding year exceeding the average length of time for completion of such background checks and (iv) the main three reasons for completions of background checks for applicants who submitted applications for site safety coordinator certificates during the preceding year exceeding the average length of time for completion of such background checks.

4920277.action_summary: Conduct education and outreach to increase awareness of single-occupant toilet room requirements under the plumbing code, in conjunction with other city agencies, tailored to business owners.
4920277.quote: The department, in conjunction with (i) the mayor's office of immigrant affairs, (ii) the commission on human rights, (iii) the department of consumer affairs, (iv) the department of health and mental hygiene, (v) the department of small business services, (vi) the department of citywide administrative services and (vii) any other office or agency designated by the mayor, shall conduct education and outreach to increase awareness of sections 403.2.1 and 403.4 of the New York city plumbing code, regarding single-occupant toilet room requirements. Such education and outreach shall be tailored to business owners, and shall, at a minimum, include educational materials concerning such single-occupant toilet room requirements and the related posting and signage requirements, including samples of acceptable signage.

4920277.action_summary: Submit to the mayor and speaker of the council and post on the department website an annual report on education and outreach conducted regarding single-occupant toilet room requirements through April 1, 2023.
4920277.quote: In April of each year until April 1, 2023, the commissioner of buildings shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and post on the department's website, a report on: 1. The education and outreach conducted as required by section 28-103.32 including a description of how such outreach was conducted and the number of business owners reached through the outreach; 2. The number of complaints related to sections 403.2.1 and 403.4 of the New York city plumbing code reported to 311, disaggregated by online complaints and phone complaints; 3. The number of violations issued as a result of such complaints; 4. The total amount of penalties imposed as a result of such violations for the immediately preceding year; and 5. Whether subsequent inspections were conducted by the department to ensure future compliance with such sections of the New York city plumbing code.
4920277.deadline_text: In April of each year until April 1, 2023

4920277.action_summary: Establish a program to assist with technical review and approval of alternative energy project applications, provide guidance to applicants, support technical research, and receive and respond to comments and complaints.
4920277.quote: The duties of the office of alternative energy include, but need not be limited to: 1. Establishing a program to (i) assist with the technical review and approval of applications and other documents submitted to the department in connection with alternative energy projects, (ii) provide guidance to applicants in connection with such projects, (iii) support technical research for advancing energy legislation and policy within the city and (iv) receive and respond to comments, questions and complaints with respect to such program; 2. Coordinating with the office of long-term planning and sustainability, fire department, department of small business services, department of housing preservation and development, and other relevant agencies to ensure that policies are in place to encourage the installation and maintenance of alternative energy projects, and seeking cooperation and assistance from the city university of New York with respect to such policies; and 3. Making recommendations to the commissioner and the heads of other agencies with respect to streamlining the process for obtaining the necessary approvals to install and maintain alternative energy projects.

4920277.actor_raw: the head of the office of the alternative energy
4920277.action_summary: Submit an annual report to the commissioner and other relevant agencies describing comments, questions and complaints received, coordination actions taken, and recommendations regarding alternative energy projects.
4920277.quote: The head of the office of the alternative energy shall submit an annual report to the commissioner and to the head of any other relevant agency providing (i) a description of the most commonly received comments, questions and complaints received with respect to such office, (ii) a description of actions undertaken by such office to coordinate with other agencies and the results of such coordination, (iii) recommendations made pursuant to section 28-103.33.2 and (iv) recommendations with respect to expanding the definition of alternative energy project. By no later than three months after the end of each fiscal year, such office shall submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the city council that includes a summary of the actions taken by any agency as a result of any comment, question, complaint or recommendation from or forwarded by such office.
4920277.deadline_text: By no later than three months after the end of each fiscal year

4920277.action_summary: Maintain a website with contact information and post information regarding installation of green roof systems and other related resources and materials.
4920277.quote: The office of alternative energy shall further post and maintain links on its website to information regarding the installation of green roof systems and other resources and materials regarding green roof systems.

4920277.action_summary: Provide free of charge a service allowing users to register to receive automated email notifications when the status of construction projects changes.
4920277.quote: The department shall provide, free of charge, a service allowing users to register to receive an automated e-mail notification each time a change in status is recorded with respect to one or more construction projects, selected by such user. Such electronic mail notifications shall include any update to work permits issued by the department for each such selected construction project, including issuance of any stop work order issued pursuant to section 28-207.2.

4920277.action_summary: On a weekly basis, send council members and community boards by email and post on the website a report of all applications that were approved for new buildings or alterations requiring new certificates of occupancy.
4920277.quote: The department shall, on a weekly basis, send council members and community boards, by electronic mail, and post on its website, a report of all applications that were approved during the prior week, disaggregated by community board, for: 1. A new building or an alteration that will require a new certificate of occupancy for a building; and 2. Work at a building or part thereof for which construction and related documents shall not be accepted with less than full examination by the department pursuant to the exception to section 28-104.2.1.

4920277.action_summary: On a weekly basis, send council members and community boards by email and post on the website a report of all rejections of applications for new buildings or alterations requiring new certificates of occupancy.
4920277.quote: The department shall, on a weekly basis, send council members and community boards, by electronic mail, a report of all rejections of applications for a new building or an alteration that will require a new certificate of occupancy for a building, during the prior week, disaggregated by community board. In addition, the department shall post such information on its website on a weekly basis.

4920277.action_summary: On a weekly basis, send council members and community boards by email a copy of all completed applications for new buildings or alterations requiring new certificates of occupancy received during the prior week, disaggregated by community board.
4920277.quote: The department shall, on a weekly basis, send council members and community boards, by electronic mail, a copy of all completed applications for a new building or an alteration that will require a new certificate of occupancy for a building, received during the prior week, disaggregated by community board. In addition, the department shall post such information on its website on a weekly basis.

4920277.action_summary: Create and maintain a database of all registered design professionals who have been excluded, suspended or otherwise sanctioned, and post information on the department website.
4920277.quote: The department shall create and maintain a database of all registered design professionals who have been excluded, suspended or otherwise sanctioned by the department, all current firms of employment or affiliation of such professionals, if known or readily ascertainable, and the firm that employed such professionals, or with which such professional was affiliated, at the time such professionals were sanctioned, and the status of such sanction or sanctions. Within 7 business days of the date a sanction is imposed, the department shall post on its website, in a non-proprietary machine-readable format that permits automated processing, and shall make available upon request, the name of the registered design professional, and the firm that employed such professionals, or with which such professionals were affiliated, at the time such professionals were sanctioned, and a description of the sanction, the initial date of the sanction, the reinstatement date, if applicable, the address of the premises for which the application associated with the sanction was submitted, and whether the sanction was imposed after a hearing or a settlement.
4920277.deadline_text: Within 7 business days of the date a sanction is imposed

4920277.action_summary: Provide requested information concerning the exclusion, suspension or other sanction of a specific registered design professional within 30 days of such request.
4920277.quote: The department shall provide requested information concerning the exclusion, suspension or other sanction of a specific registered design professional and the firm of employment of such professionals, or the firm with which such professionals were affiliated, when such professionals were sanctioned, within 30 days of such request.

4920277.action_summary: Receive and track all complaints related to work without a permit in occupied multiple dwellings and retain records of such complaints.
4920277.quote: The real time enforcement unit shall receive and track all complaints related to work without a permit in occupied multiple dwellings. The unit shall retain records of such complaints.

4920277.action_summary: Approve fire protection plans for new building and alteration applications of covered buildings and submit such plans for fire department review and approval prior to issuance of certificates of occupancy.
4920277.quote: New building and alteration applications for covered buildings as set forth in section 28-109.2 shall include a fire protection plan prepared by or under the supervision of a registered design professional who shall professionally certify such plan. Such plan shall be submitted for review and approval by the fire department for compliance with this code prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy, a temporary certificate of occupancy or a letter of completion, as applicable.

4920277.action_summary: Ensure that streets are suitably improved in accordance with the standards prescribed by the department of transportation.
4920277.quote: The commissioner shall insure that streets are suitably improved in accordance with the standards prescribed by the department of transportation as required by subdivision 2 of section 36 of the New York state general city law and shall otherwise carry out the provisions of such subdivision.

4920277.action_summary: Audit on a monthly basis no less than 25 percent of construction documents for multiple dwellings where 25 percent or more of units are occupied and subject to rent regulation or affordable housing programs.
4920277.quote: On a monthly basis, the commissioner shall audit no less than 25 percent of construction documents which are for multiple dwellings where 25 percent or more of the dwelling units are occupied and such multiple dwellings, in whole or in part, either (i) are subject to rent regulation, (ii) are being rehabilitated or maintained as affordable housing through a department of housing preservation and development program, (iii) are subject to a city regulatory agreement mandating the creation or preservation of a certain number of affordable units, (iv) contain affordable housing units created, sponsored or preserved through other city programs or initiatives, or (v) where the department knows or has reason to know, are the subject of a rent overcharge application which is in the process of being investigated by the New York State division of housing and community renewal.

4920277.action_summary: Report to the federal occupational safety and health administration as soon as practicable after issuance of an immediately hazardous or major violation of chapter 33 of the building code.
4920277.quote: As soon as practicable after the issuance of an immediately hazardous or major violation of chapter 33 of the New York city building code, the commissioner shall report such violation to the federal occupational safety and health administration.

4920277.action_summary: Post on the department website by October 1, 2020 bird friendly building design and construction requirements and information about compliance with section 1403.8 of the building code.
4920277.quote: The department shall issue, and update as necessary, bird friendly building design and construction requirements. No later than October 1, 2020, the department shall post on its website such requirements and information about compliance with section 1403.8 of the New York city building code.

4920277.action_summary: Convene and provide staff for an SST task force composed of 14 members appointed by the mayor and speaker, representing various sectors of the construction industry and with expertise in construction safety or safety training.
4920277.quote: The commissioner shall convene and provide staff for an SST task force in accordance with the following: 1. Such task force shall be composed as follows: 1.1. The commissioner, or the designee of such commissioner, shall serve as the chairperson of such task force. 1.2. The task force shall consist of 14 members, in addition to the chairperson. Seven of the additional members of such task force shall be appointed by the mayor or the mayor's designee, and seven of the additional members of such task force shall be appointed by the speaker of the council. Such task force shall include members who represent (i) parts of the construction industry that are represented by labor unions or labor organizations, (ii) parts of such industry that are not represented by such unions or organizations, (iii) minority-owned business enterprises or women-owned business enterprises that are certified in accordance with section 1304 of the New York city charter and primarily engaged in construction work and (iv) day laborers.

4920277.action_summary: Report annually on implementation of site safety training requirements including SST providers, cards issued, violations, and enforcement mechanisms.
4920277.quote: No later than three months after the end of each fiscal year, the commissioner shall report to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and make publicly available online, a report on implementation of section 3321 of the New York city building code.
4920277.deadline_text: No later than three months after the end of each fiscal year

4920277.action_summary: Periodically audit SST providers and training provided in connection with site safety training requirements to ensure integrity and compliance.
4920277.quote: In addition to any other enforcement mechanisms, the department shall periodically audit SST providers and training provided in connection with section 3321 of the New York city building code by such providers in order to ensure the integrity of such training and compliance with such section and any rules or department requirements relating to such training.

4920277.action_summary: Publish an annual report online with information on the effectiveness of the real time enforcement unit regarding complaints and inspections.
4920277.quote: The department shall publish online an annual report with the following information related to the effectiveness of the real time enforcement unit: (i) the number of complaints received disaggregated by building; (ii) the average time taken to respond to complaints; (iii) the number of monitored occupied multiple dwellings with valid permits for alteration or addition as described in section 28-103.30.2; (iv) the number of initial and periodic inspections conducted disaggregated by building; and (v) the number and type of violations issued disaggregated by building.

4085848.action_summary: Develop a comprehensive 10-year food policy plan containing recommendations on hunger reduction, nutrition improvement, healthy food access, food waste reduction, food and farm economies, and urban agriculture and sustainability, along with implementation strategies for agencies and benchmarks to measure progress.
4085848.quote: The office of food policy shall develop a comprehensive 10 year food policy plan no later than 180 days after the effective date of this section.
4085848.deadline_text: no later than 180 days after the effective date of this section

4085848.action_summary: Prepare and submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and post on the office's website, a report describing the city's progress toward food policy recommendations.
4085848.quote: the office of food policy shall prepare and submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and post on the office's website, a report that describes the city's progress toward the recommendations made
4085848.deadline_text: No later than two years after the submission of the report required pursuant to this subdivision and every two years thereafter

3973110.action_summary: Keep a record of and transmit to the law department any workers' compensation claim filed by an employee concerning an injury sustained in the course of duty.
3973110.quote: Each agency shall keep a record of, and shall, as soon as practicable, transmit to the law department, any workers' compensation claim filed by an employee

3973110.action_summary: Collect and report to the law department detailed workers' compensation data including employment counts, lost time, wages, medical expenses, injuries by job title, and claim information.
3973110.quote: Each agency shall collect and report to the law department, no later than February 15 of the year following the reporting year, the following information
3973110.deadline_text: no later than February 15 of the year following the reporting year

3973110.action_summary: Ensure that an annual report is prepared utilizing workers' compensation data received from each city agency and transmit it to the department of records and information services, the comptroller, the public advocate and the speaker of the council by May 1st.
3973110.quote: the mayor, in coordination with the law department, shall ensure that an annual report is prepared utilizing the data received from each city agency pursuant to paragraphs (2) and (3) of this subdivision. Such report shall be transmitted to the department of records and information services pursuant to section 1133 of the charter, the mayor, the comptroller, the public advocate and the speaker of the council by the first day of May
3973110.deadline_text: by the first day of May, covering the previous calendar year

3973110.action_summary: Develop and implement an annual accident and illness prevention program designed to reduce injuries and illnesses identified in the annual workers' compensation report.
3973110.quote: Each agency shall develop and implement an annual accident and illness prevention program designed to reduce injuries and illnesses identified in the report required pursuant to paragraph (4) of this subdivision.

3973110.action_summary: Submit to the comptroller, the public advocate and the speaker a report on steps the city will take to develop programs to mitigate injury and illness based on workers' compensation data collected.
3973110.quote: No later than 90 days after submission of the report required pursuant to paragraph (4) of this subdivision, the mayor shall submit to the comptroller, the public advocate and the speaker a report on steps the city will take to develop programs to mitigate injury and illness
3973110.deadline_text: No later than 90 days after submission of the report required pursuant to paragraph (4) of this subdivision

3973110.action_summary: Take appropriate steps to ensure that collection and reporting of workers' compensation information does not violate applicable federal, state or local privacy or confidentiality laws.
3973110.quote: The law department may take appropriate steps to ensure the collection and reporting of information required pursuant to paragraphs (2) and (3) of this subdivision shall not violate any applicable federal, state or local law

3086321.action_summary: Adopt rules prescribing specific time frames for inspections in response to after hours noise complaints to ensure inspections occur when alleged noise is continued or likely to be repeated.
3086321.quote: The commissioner shall adopt rules prescribing specific time frames for inspections in response to after hours noise complaints received by the department in order to ensure that such inspections are most likely to occur at (i) a time that the alleged noise is continued from the time of the complaint or (ii) at a time when the alleged noise is likely to be repeated.

3086321.action_summary: Publish on the city's website the manner by which noise levels shall be measured during inspections conducted pursuant to section 24-207 and in accordance with section 24-217.1.
3086321.quote: The commissioner shall publish on the city's website the manner by which noise levels shall be measured during inspections conducted pursuant to this section and in accordance with section 24-217.1 which shall be available online

3086321.action_summary: Submit annually to the mayor and council, and publicly post on its website, a report containing the number of inspectors employed, complaints received by type, after hours noise complaints responded to within prescribed time, duplicative complaints, non-violation resolutions, violations issued, dismissed violations, civil penalties paid, approved alternative noise mitigation plans, and written stop work orders issued.
3086321.quote: By no later than January 31 of each year, the department shall submit to the mayor and the council, and publicly post on its website, a report, containing, at a minimum, for the previous calendar year: (i) the number of inspectors employed by the department; (ii) the number of complaints regarding noise received by the department, disaggregated by the type of noise; (iii) the number of after hours noise complaints responded to within the amount of time prescribed by rule as well as the number of duplicative after hours noise complaints; (iv) the number of non-violation resolutions to complaints; (v) the number of noise related violations issued; (vi) the number of such violations which were dismissed; (vii) the amount of civil penalties which were paid pursuant to such violations; (viii) the number of alternative noise mitigation plans approved pursuant to section 24-221 of this code; and (ix) the number of written stop work orders issued pursuant to section 24-223.1 of this code.
3086321.deadline_text: By no later than January 31 of each year

3086321.action_summary: Adopt rules prescribing noise mitigation strategies, methods, procedures and technology to be used at construction sites where specified construction devices or activities are employed or performed.
3086321.quote: The commissioner shall adopt rules prescribing noise mitigation strategies, methods, procedures and technology that shall be used where construction is occurring at any location (sites) whenever any one or more of the construction devices or activities listed below are employed or performed:

3086321.action_summary: Provide notice and opportunity to be heard within 14 days of filing of an appeal of a stop work order and determine whether issuance was proper or lift the order upon proof of compliance.
3086321.quote: A stop work order issued pursuant to subdivision a of this section may be appealed in accordance with the rules of the department, and the commissioner shall provide notice and an opportunity to be heard within 14 days of the filing of such appeal.
3086321.deadline_text: within 14 days of the filing of such appeal

3086321.action_summary: Issue stop work orders when work is being performed in violation of noise regulations and poses a threat to human health and safety.
3086321.quote: Whenever the department finds that any work is being performed in violation of section 24-222 or section 24-228 or any rules promulgated thereunder, and such work poses a threat to human health and safety, the department may issue a stop work order with respect to such work or solely with respect to the equipment used for work being performed in violation of section 24-222 or 24-228.

3086321.action_summary: Take measures necessary for the implementation of the local law, including the promulgation of rules, prior to the effective date.
3086321.quote: the department of environmental protection may take such measures as are necessary for the implementation of this local law, including the promulgation of rules, prior to such date
3086321.deadline_text: prior to the effective date of this local law

2813485.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
2813485.action_summary: Verify complaints of ponding conditions on roadways under its jurisdiction within 45 days, except where weather or other circumstances prevent timely completion.
2813485.quote: Upon receiving a complaint of a ponding condition on a roadway under its jurisdiction, the department shall verify such complaint within 45 days, except where weather conditions or other circumstances do not permit the timely completion of such verification.
2813485.deadline_text: within 45 days, except where weather conditions or other circumstances do not permit the timely completion of such verification

2813485.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
2813485.action_summary: Assess roadways with verified ponding conditions to determine what work may be necessary to repair such conditions, conducting assessments jointly with the Department of Environmental Protection where necessary.
2813485.quote: Upon verification, the department shall assess the roadway to determine what work may be necessary to repair such ponding condition. Such assessment shall be conducted jointly with the department of environmental protection, where necessary.

2813485.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
2813485.action_summary: Prioritize resurfacing of roadways with ponding conditions to be performed either when the department's next resurfacing operations take place in the community district or within 18 months from the date of assessment, whichever is earlier.
2813485.quote: If such assessment concludes that such ponding condition can be repaired through resurfacing, such resurfacing shall be prioritized by the department to be performed (i) when department resurfacing operations next take place in the community district where such ponding is located, or (ii) within 18 months from the date of such assessment, whichever is earlier.
2813485.deadline_text: within 18 months from the date of such assessment, whichever is earlier

2813485.actor_raw: the department or the department of environmental protection
2813485.action_summary: Prioritize work to repair ponding conditions on roadways that can only be repaired through means other than resurfacing.
2813485.quote: If such assessment concludes that such ponding condition can only be repaired through work other than resurfacing, such work shall be prioritized by the department or the department of environmental protection.

2813485.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
2813485.action_summary: Notify in writing council members or community boards of the results of ponding condition assessments within 10 days of conducting such assessments.
2813485.quote: In instances where a council member or a community board has made a complaint in writing to the department of a ponding condition on a roadway under the department's jurisdiction, within 10 days of conducting an assessment of such location as required by paragraph 1 of subdivision c of this section, the department shall notify, in writing, such council member or community board in whose district the ponding condition is located of the results of such assessment.
2813485.deadline_text: within 10 days of conducting an assessment of such location

2473919.action_summary: Make the tenant protection plan publicly available on the department's website upon issuance of a permit.
2473919.quote: Upon issuance of a permit for work containing a tenant protection plan, the department shall make the tenant protection plan publicly available on its website.

2473919.action_summary: Create or approve a form of notice to occupants regarding tenant protection plans.
2473919.quote: The notice shall be in a form created or approved by the department and shall include:

2473919.action_summary: Conduct inspections to determine compliance with the tenant protection plan for buildings undergoing required work.
2473919.quote: For buildings undergoing work for which a tenant protection plan is required by section 28-104.8.4 of the administrative code, inspections shall be made by the department to determine compliance with the tenant protection plan.

2473919.action_summary: Conduct an inspection of five percent of sites within seven days after commencement of work requiring a tenant protection plan, and conduct inspections upon receipt of complaints.
2473919.quote: The department shall conduct an inspection of five percent of such sites within seven days after the commencement of such work to verify compliance with the tenant protection plan. Thereafter, the department shall conduct an inspection upon the receipt of a complaint concerning such work.
2473919.deadline_text: within seven days after the commencement of such work

2473919.action_summary: Promulgate rules as necessary for implementation of the local law.
2473919.quote: the commissioner of buildings may take such measures as are necessary for its implementation, including the promulgation of rules, prior to such effective date.

2735469.action_summary: Serve as chair of the interagency foster care task force and ensure members are appointed within 60 days of enactment.
2735469.quote: the commissioner of children's services, or their designee, who shall serve as chair
2735469.deadline_text: All members shall be appointed within 60 days of the enactment of this local law.
affected_groups: youth aging out of foster care

2735469.action_summary: Submit a report of findings and recommendations addressing education, housing, financial literacy, health and mental health services, parenting, decreasing youth aging out of foster care, post-permanency services, and permanent family placements.
2735469.quote: Such task force shall submit a report of its findings and recommendations to the mayor and the council no later than 14 months after the effective date of the local law that added this section.
2735469.deadline_text: no later than 14 months after the effective date of the local law that added this section
affected_groups: youth aging out of foster care

2735469.action_summary: Submit annual reports on the implementation of recommendations to the mayor and council no later than 12 and 24 months following submission of the initial report.
2735469.quote: Annual reports on the implementation of such recommendations shall be submitted to the mayor and the council no later than 12 and 24 months following the submission of the initial report
2735469.deadline_text: no later than 12 and 24 months following the submission of the initial report
affected_groups: youth aging out of foster care

2735469.action_summary: Post each report required by Section 1(d) on the administration for children's services' website.
2735469.quote: Each report required pursuant to this section shall be posted on the administration for children's services' website.
affected_groups: youth aging out of foster care

2735481.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a five-year plan to address barriers to permanency for youth in foster care, including a case study of a statistically significant sample of children in foster care and an analysis of how ACS plans to address systemic barriers to permanency.
2735481.quote: By December 31, 2017, ACS shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a five-year plan to address barriers to permanency for youth in foster care.

2735481.action_summary: Review and update the five-year plan annually and submit the updated version to the speaker of the council and post online one year following submission of the initial five-year report and annually thereafter.
2735481.quote: The five-year plan shall be reviewed and updated by ACS annually and the updated version shall be submitted to the speaker of the council and posted online one year following the submission of the initial five-year report and annually on such date thereafter.
2735481.deadline_text: one year following the submission of the initial five-year report and annually on such date thereafter

2735481.action_summary: In the fifth year covered by each five-year plan, submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a new five-year plan to address barriers to permanency for the next succeeding five-year period, and maintain the previous five-year report on ACS' website.
2735481.quote: In the fifth year covered by each such five-year plan, ACS shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a new five-year plan to address barriers to permanency for the next succeeding five-year period not later than six months prior to the last day of such fifth year.
2735481.deadline_text: not later than six months prior to the last day of such fifth year

2683896.action_summary: Establish a municipal division of transitional services, which may be established in the executive office of the mayor, as a separate division, or within any other office or department of the mayor.
2683896.quote: The mayor shall establish a municipal division of transitional services. Such division may, but need not, be established in the executive office of the mayor or as a separate division or within any other office of the mayor, or within any department the head of which is appointed by the mayor.
affected_groups: individuals released from department of correction custody
individuals in need of reentry services

2683896.actor_raw: the mayor or the head of such department
2683896.action_summary: Appoint a coordinator of the municipal division of transitional services.
2683896.quote: Such division shall be headed by a coordinator who shall be appointed by the mayor or the head of such department.

2683896.action_summary: Ensure, by necessary means including coordination with relevant city agencies, the availability of effective reentry services to individuals released from the department of correction and other individuals in need of reentry services.
2683896.quote: ensure, by such means as necessary, including coordination with relevant city agencies, the availability of effective reentry services to individuals residing in New York city who have been released from the custody of the New York city department of correction after having served a period of criminal incarceration or criminal detention and other individuals in need of reentry services that have served a period of criminal incarceration or criminal detention
affected_groups: individuals released from department of correction custody
individuals in need of reentry services

2683896.action_summary: Create a coordinated system for the administration of reentry services, ensuring access in areas where substantial numbers of such individuals reside, and integrating and coordinating similar services provided by other city agencies.
2683896.quote: create a coordinated system for the administration of reentry services. Such system shall ensure access to reentry services in areas where a substantial number of such individuals reside. To the extent that the coordinator deems appropriate, such system may also include integration and coordination with similar services provided by other city agencies, and existing facilities operated by city agencies may be utilized for the purpose of such integration and coordination
affected_groups: individuals in need of reentry services

2683896.action_summary: Administer contracts for the provision of reentry services as appropriate, review the budget requests of all agencies for programs related to reentry services, and recommend to the mayor budget priorities among such services.
2683896.quote: administer contracts for the provision of reentry services as appropriate, and to the extent required by paragraph 1 of this subdivision, review the budget requests of all agencies for programs related to reentry services, and recommend to the mayor budget priorities among such services and assist the mayor in prioritizing such requests
affected_groups: individuals in need of reentry services

2683896.action_summary: Provide outreach and education on the availability of reentry services.
2683896.quote: provide outreach and education on the availability of reentry services
affected_groups: individuals in need of reentry services

2683896.action_summary: Prepare and submit to the mayor and council an annual report of the activities of the division and its progress in ensuring the delivery of effective reentry services, including populations served, types of programs created or provided, geographic areas served, and outreach efforts.
2683896.quote: By October 31, 2017, and by October 31 of every year thereafter, the coordinator shall prepare and submit to the mayor and council a report of the activities of the division and its progress in ensuring the delivery of effective reentry services. Such report shall include the (i) populations served; (ii) types of programs created or provided and who created or provided such programs; (iii) geographic areas served; and (iv) outreach efforts.
2683896.deadline_text: By October 31, 2017, and by October 31 of every year thereafter

2683896.action_summary: Prepare and submit to the mayor and council a biennial report of reentry services for city residents, including assessment of reentry service needs, identification and assessment of efficacy and capacity of existing reentry services, and identification of areas or populations with concentrated reentry service needs.
2683896.quote: By October 31, 2017, and by October 31 of every second year thereafter, the coordinator shall prepare and submit to the mayor and the council a report of reentry services for those city residents who need such services. Such report shall include (i) an assessment of the reentry service needs of city residents, as well as the type and frequency of resources needed, including but not limited to matters concerning housing, health insurance, medical expenses and debts relating thereto, behavioral health treatment, personal finances, employment, job training, education, immigration, and public benefits, (ii) identification and assessment of the efficacy and capacity of existing reentry services available for city residents, and (iii) identification of the areas or populations within the city in which city residents with reentry service needs are concentrated and the corresponding availability of reentry services.
2683896.deadline_text: By October 31, 2017, and by October 31 of every second year thereafter
affected_groups: city residents in need of reentry services

2683896.action_summary: Prepare and submit to the mayor and council a four-year plan for providing reentry services to city residents who need such services, including recommendations for approaches to serving such residents, identification of obstacles, and description of additional resources necessary.
2683896.quote: Within one year after the completion of the first biennial report required by subdivision d of this section, and in every fourth calendar year thereafter, the coordinator shall prepare and submit to the mayor and the council a four-year plan for providing reentry services to those city residents who need such services.
2683896.deadline_text: Within one year after the completion of the first biennial report required by subdivision d of this section, and in every fourth calendar year thereafter
affected_groups: city residents in need of reentry services

2576390.action_summary: Develop and conduct a survey of unpaid caregivers and providers offering services to unpaid caregivers to identify their needs and assess existing caregiver services.

3498450.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

6632239.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
6632239.action_summary: Establish a pilot program to deploy rat contraceptives and other technology in designated rat mitigation zones to reduce the rat population.
6632239.quote: The department, in consultation with the department of sanitation and at least 1 expert in rodent control, shall establish a pilot program to deploy rat contraceptives and, as appropriate, any other technology recommended by at least 1 expert in rodent control to reduce the rat population.
6632239.deadline_text: no later than 180 days after the effective date of this local law

6632239.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
6632239.action_summary: Designate at least 2 pilot program areas, each covering at least 10 city blocks, that include primarily residential buildings required to use waste receptacles and are located within rat mitigation zones.
6632239.quote: The pilot program shall be installed in areas to be designated by the department, provided that each area: (i) include buildings a majority of which are residential; (ii) include buildings a majority of which are required to set out waste in receptacles pursuant to rules promulgated by the department of sanitation; and (iii) be located within a rat mitigation zone. There shall be at least 2 pilot program areas, each of which shall cover at least 10 city blocks in surface area
6632239.deadline_text: no later than 180 days after the effective date of this local law

6632239.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
6632239.action_summary: Designate at least 1 pilot program comparison area with similar building types and implement similar mitigation efforts, excluding rat contraceptive deployment, to allow controlled comparison with pilot program areas.
6632239.quote: The department shall designate at least 1 pilot program comparison area that includes building types similar to those included in the pilot program areas, and shall make reasonable efforts to implement similar mitigation efforts, other than the deployment of rat contraceptive, across the pilot program areas and the pilot program comparison area or areas to allow for a controlled comparison
6632239.deadline_text: no later than 180 days after the effective date of this local law
affected_groups: residents in pilot program comparison areas

6632239.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
6632239.action_summary: Deploy rat contraceptive at locations in the pilot program areas determined in consultation with the Department of Sanitation.
6632239.quote: The department shall deploy rat contraceptive at locations in the pilot program areas determined in consultation with the department of sanitation
6632239.deadline_text: no later than 180 days after the effective date of this local law

6632239.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
6632239.action_summary: Perform monthly inspections for no less than 12 months of each pilot program area and comparison area, tallying all rat signs observed and tracking rat contraceptive amounts in dispensers.
6632239.quote: For no less than 12 months immediately after the deployment of the rat contraceptive, the department shall perform monthly inspections of each pilot program area and each pilot program comparison area and shall tally all rat signs observed in each area, disaggregated by type of rat sign. During such monthly inspections of the pilot program areas, the department shall track the amount of rat contraceptive in each rat contraceptive dispenser.
6632239.deadline_text: no later than 180 days after the effective date of this local law

6632239.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
6632239.action_summary: Verify any data provided by a vendor that supplies rat contraceptive or other technology for the pilot program through an independent entity.
6632239.quote: Any data provided by a vendor that supplies the department with rat contraceptive or other technology for the pilot program pursuant to this section shall be verified by an independent entity.

6632239.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
6632239.action_summary: Develop a plan for the safe removal of rat contraceptive from pilot program areas to minimize any increase in the rat population and impact on residents.
6632239.quote: Prior to the end of the pilot program, the department shall develop a plan for the safe removal of rat contraceptive from the pilot program areas to minimize, to the extent practicable, any increase in the rat population and any impact on residents living in such areas.

6632239.actor_raw: the commissioner of health and mental hygiene
6632239.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
6632239.action_summary: Prepare and submit to the mayor and speaker of the council a comprehensive report on the outcomes of the rat contraceptive pilot program, including program costs, market research, implementation challenges, harm to non-target species, opportunities to reduce rodenticide use, resource needs, and detailed tables of pilot areas, inspections, and interventions.
6632239.quote: No later than 180 days after the end of the pilot program established pursuant to this section, the commissioner of health and mental hygiene, in consultation with the commissioner of sanitation and at least 1 expert in rodent control, shall prepare and submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a report regarding the outcomes of such pilot program and inspections during the period of such program.
6632239.deadline_text: No later than 180 days after the end of the pilot program

3877883.action_summary: Post online business tools and resources on the city's website, including accounting and bookkeeping resources, and a searchable interactive guide to city laws and rules applicable to particular business types.
3877883.quote: The commissioner shall post on the city's website online business tools and resources, including but not limited to: 1. Tools provided by the department, which may include accounting, recordkeeping and bookkeeping resources; 2. A searchable and interactive guide to aid current or prospective business owners in understanding city laws and rules applicable to such business

3877883.action_summary: Inform the department of small business services within 30 days after any change to a law or rule referenced in the online business guide.
3877883.quote: Within 30 days after the effective date of a change to a law or rule referenced in the guide described in paragraph 2 of subdivision a of this section, the agency having primary jurisdiction over such law or rule shall inform the department of such change.
3877883.deadline_text: Within 30 days after the effective date of a change to a law or rule referenced in the guide

3877883.action_summary: Update the online business guide within 30 days of being informed of any change to a law or rule referenced in the guide.
3877883.quote: Within 30 days of being informed of such change, the department shall update the guide accordingly.
3877883.deadline_text: Within 30 days of being informed of such change

3877883.actor_raw: the department of small business services
3877883.action_summary: Take necessary measures for the implementation of this local law, including the promulgation of any rules, before the effective date.
3877883.quote: the department of small business services shall take such measures as are necessary for the implementation of this local law, including the promulgation of any rules, before such date.

2240482.action_summary: Publish findings demonstrating that any alternative green building standards are not less stringent than LEED standards for gold or certified rating achievement.
2240482.quote: If the mayor elects to utilize green building standards other than the LEED green building rating system, the mayor shall publish findings demonstrating that such other green building standards are not less stringent than the LEED standards described above

2240482.action_summary: Review and update green building standards used by the city, as necessary, no less often than once every three years.
2240482.quote: The green building standards utilized by the city in accordance with this section shall be reviewed and updated, as necessary, by the mayor no less often that once every three years.

2240482.actor_raw: the mayor, or an office or agency designated by the mayor
2240482.action_summary: Establish alternative low energy intensity targets for buildings designed and constructed for particular uses or for additions to or substantial reconstructions of existing buildings, and submit a report to the council within 60 days describing the target, affected buildings, and if less stringent, the reasons compliance would be impracticable or unduly burdensome.
2240482.quote: Where the mayor or such designated office or agency adopts such an alternative target, the mayor or such designated office or agency shall, no later than 60 days after such adoption, submit to the council and make publicly available online a report describing such alternative target and the types of buildings or work to which it will apply.
2240482.deadline_text: no later than 60 days after such adoption

2240482.actor_raw: the mayor, or an office or agency designated by the mayor
2240482.action_summary: Submit annually to the council a report stating whether alternative low energy intensity targets continue to be necessary, and if so, describing the reasons and whether targets can be made more stringent.
2240482.quote: in each fiscal year thereafter, the mayor or such designated office or agency shall submit to the council and make publicly available online a report stating whether the mayor or such designated office or agency has determined that such alternative targets continue to be necessary and, if so, a description of the reasons therefor and whether such targets can reasonably be made more stringent.

2240482.action_summary: Submit a plan to the speaker of the council ensuring that by 2030 capital projects subject to low energy intensity building requirements will achieve specified source energy use intensity targets, including policies, programs and actions the city will undertake.
2240482.quote: No later than January 1, 2017, the mayor shall submit to the speaker of the council and make publicly available online a plan for ensuring that by 2030 capital projects subject to paragraph (2) of this subdivision will be designed and constructed so that new buildings have a source energy use intensity no greater than 38 kBTU/yr per square foot of floor area

2240482.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council a report containing recommended practices for designing and constructing low energy intensity buildings.
2240482.quote: In 2019 and every third year thereafter, the mayor shall, by June 30 of such year, submit to the speaker of the council and make publicly available online a report containing, at a minimum, recommended practices for designing and constructing low energy intensity buildings.

2240482.action_summary: Submit annually to the speaker of the council by December 1 a comprehensive report on capital projects completed in the preceding fiscal year, containing specified information about project descriptions, locations, LEED certification levels, costs, low energy intensity building status, onsite energy generation feasibility, additional costs, and health and environmental benefits.
2240482.quote: By no later than December 1 of each year, the mayor shall submit to the speaker of the council a report, in accordance with the procedure and format established by the department of design and construction, containing, at a minimum, the following information
2240482.deadline_text: By no later than December 1 of each year

2598202.action_summary: Post on its website information relating to street tree maintenance and sidewalk repair, including upcoming and completed tree work, planned sidewalk repairs, and inspection results.
2598202.quote: The department shall post on its website certain information relating to street tree maintenance and sidewalk repair. Such information shall be updated not less frequently than quarterly

5983600.action_summary: Designate by rule the edition of the energy standard ASHRAE 90.1 to be used for buildings.
5983600.quote: ASHRAE 90.1. The term "ASHRAE 90.1" means the edition of the energy standard for buildings except low-rise residential buildings published by the American society of heating, refrigerating and air conditioning engineers (ASHRAE) as indicated by rule of the mayor.

5983600.action_summary: Approve the version of the LEED for building design and construction or another version of the LEED water efficiency indoor water use reduction credit.
5983600.quote: LEED water efficiency: indoor water use reduction credit. The term "LEED water efficiency: indoor water use reduction credit" means the credit to achieve points under the LEED for building design and construction version 4, or another version as approved by the mayor, intended to achieve water use reduction.

5983600.action_summary: Approve the selected green building rating system, which may be LEED versions or other not less stringent alternatives.
5983600.quote: Selected green building rating system. The term "selected green building rating system" means LEED building design and construction version 4, building operations and maintenance version 4 or interior design and construction version 4, whichever is most appropriate for the project under United States green building council guidelines, or other not less stringent versions of such building rating systems as approved by the mayor.

5983600.action_summary: Publish findings demonstrating that any alternative green building standard selected is not less stringent than the LEED standards for achievement of a LEED gold or certified rating, if the mayor elects not to use the LEED rating system.
5983600.quote: If the mayor elects to utilize a green building standard other than the LEED green building rating system for compliance with paragraph (1) of this subdivision, the mayor shall publish findings demonstrating that such other green building standards are not less stringent than the LEED standards described above for achievement of a LEED gold or, if applicable, a LEED certified rating.

5983600.action_summary: Review and update green building standards utilized by the city no less often than once every three years.
5983600.quote: The green building standards utilized by the city in accordance with this subdivision shall be reviewed and updated, as necessary, by the mayor no less often than once every three years.

5983600.action_summary: Determine the methodology for measuring existing building energy use intensity for substantial reconstruction projects involving buildings not classified in occupancy groups F or H.
5983600.quote: For such capital projects that are substantial reconstructions of existing buildings, the energy use intensity shall be no less than 25 percent below the existing building's energy use as determined in accordance with a methodology determined by the mayor.

5983600.action_summary: Determine the methodology for measuring existing building energy use for substantial reconstruction projects involving buildings classified in occupancy groups F or H.
5983600.quote: For such capital projects that are for substantial reconstruction of existing buildings, energy usage shall be no less than 25 percent below the existing building's energy usage as determined in accordance with a methodology determined by the mayor.

5983600.action_summary: Determine the methodology for measuring existing building energy use intensity for substantial reconstruction projects involving buildings not classified in occupancy groups F or H requiring 30 percent energy reduction.
5983600.quote: For such capital projects that are for substantial reconstruction of existing buildings, design energy use intensity shall be no less than 30 percent below the existing building's energy use intensity measured in accordance with a methodology determined by the mayor

5983600.action_summary: Determine the methodology for measuring existing building energy usage for substantial reconstruction projects involving buildings classified in occupancy groups F or H requiring 30 percent energy reduction.
5983600.quote: For such capital projects that are for substantial reconstruction of existing buildings, energy usage of the base building systems shall be no less than 30 percent below the existing building's energy usage as measured in accordance with a methodology determined by the mayor

5983600.action_summary: Designate the methodology for determining energy use reduction for HVAC system installation or replacement, or adopt the New York City energy conservation code standard.
5983600.quote: shall be designed and constructed to reduce energy use by a minimum of 10 percent from the standard as determined by the New York city energy conservation code, or other methodology designated by the mayor.

5983600.action_summary: Inform the city council of any exemptions granted from green building and energy standards at the conclusion of each year.
5983600.quote: At the conclusion of each year, the mayor shall inform the city council of any exemption granted pursuant to this subdivision.
5983600.deadline_text: At the conclusion of each year

5983600.action_summary: Establish an alternative certification process for capital projects complying with alternative standards promulgated by the mayor.
5983600.quote: The mayor shall establish an alternative certification process for capital projects that are complying with alternative standards promulgated by the mayor pursuant to subdivision c.

5983600.action_summary: Submit an annual report to the speaker of the council by December 1 each year detailing completed capital projects subject to green building standards, including project descriptions, locations, LEED certification levels, energy performance, and environmental benefits.
5983600.quote: No later than December 1 of each year, the mayor shall submit to the speaker of the council a report, containing, at a minimum: (1) For each capital project subject to this section completed during the preceding fiscal year:
5983600.deadline_text: No later than December 1 of each year

5983600.action_summary: Publish online and submit a report to the speaker of the council within 12 months of establishing alternative standards, and every three years thereafter, describing the standards, provisions less stringent than prior standards, reasons for necessity, and stringency comparisons.
5983600.quote: The mayor shall publish online and submit a report to the speaker of the council within 12 months of establishing any alternative standards pursuant to subdivisions c or f, and every three years thereafter.
5983600.deadline_text: within 12 months of establishing any alternative standards

5983600.actor_raw: the department of housing preservation and development
5983600.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
5983600.action_summary: Designate by rule the version of the New York City overlay of the enterprise green communities criteria for residential buildings subject to green building standards.
5983600.quote: or, with respect to buildings classified in occupancy group R, to comply with the version of the New York city overlay of the enterprise green communities criteria designated by rule of the department of housing preservation and development.

5983600.action_summary: For each capital project subject to subdivision d, study the feasibility of achieving the required energy performance, including a life cycle cost analysis and an assessment of alternative standards.
5983600.quote: the design agency shall

5983600.action_summary: Establish by rule alternative design and construction standards that may be less stringent than green building standards for buildings classified in occupancy groups E, F, H, I-2 or R, in coordination with relevant offices or agencies.
5983600.quote: the mayor may, in coordination, when relevant, with the New York city economic development corporation, the New York city school construction authority or any other relevant office or agency, establish by rule alternative design and construction standards that may be less stringent than the green building standards described in subdivision b of this section

5983600.action_summary: Establish alternative energy intensity requirements for buildings in particular occupancy groups that may be less stringent than the energy intensity requirements prescribed.
5983600.quote: For capital projects required to comply with subdivision d or e, the mayor may establish an alternative energy intensity requirement for new buildings, or additions to or substantial reconstructions of existing buildings classified in a particular occupancy group that may be less stringent than the energy intensity requirements described in subdivision d or e.

5983600.action_summary: Exempt capital projects accounting for up to 20 percent of the capital dollars in each fiscal year from green building and energy standards, in the mayor's sole judgment when exemption is necessary for the public interest.
5983600.quote: The mayor may exempt from each provision of this section a capital project accounting for up to 20 percent of the capital dollars in each fiscal year subject to such provision if, in the mayor's sole judgment, exemption from such provision is necessary for the public interest.

5983600.action_summary: Designate the version of the New York City green schools guide for buildings classified in occupancy group E subject to alternative green building standards.
5983600.quote: For buildings classified in occupancy group E, such alternative standards may be the version of the New York city green schools guide designated by the mayor

3332134.action_summary: Provide a free-of-charge service allowing users to register to receive automated email notifications for construction project status updates.
3332134.quote: The department shall provide, free of charge, a service allowing users to register to receive an automated e-mail notification each time a change in status is recorded with respect to one or more construction projects

3332134.action_summary: Take such measures as are necessary for the implementation of this local law, including the promulgation of rules.
3332134.quote: the commissioner of buildings shall take such measures as are necessary for the implementation of this local law, including the promulgation of rules, before such date
3332134.deadline_text: before such date (180 days after the local law becomes law)

3509916.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
3509916.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing criteria for selection of class A multiple dwellings subject to heat inspection and temperature reporting device requirements.
3509916.quote: The department shall select such class A multiple dwellings pursuant to criteria set forth in rules of the department, which shall include, but need not be limited to: (i) the number of violations of subdivision a of section 27-2029 over the preceding two years

3509916.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
3509916.action_summary: Select 50 class A multiple dwellings subject to heat inspection and temperature reporting requirements, initially by July 1, 2020, and every two years thereafter.
3509916.quote: No later than July 1, 2020, and every two years thereafter, the department shall select 50 class A multiple dwellings that shall be subject to the requirements of this subdivision.

3509916.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
3509916.action_summary: Conduct inspections of each selected class A multiple dwelling at least once every two weeks during heat season for compliance with heat and temperature reporting requirements, absent prior violation issuance.
3509916.quote: Annually, for the duration of heat season, the department shall conduct inspections of each class A multiple dwelling selected pursuant to this subdivision at least once every two weeks, without receipt of complaints, for compliance with the requirements of this section

3509916.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
3509916.action_summary: Promulgate rules describing the time and manner for owners to notify tenants regarding temperature reporting device installation, access instructions, and tenant refusal rights.
3509916.quote: Notify all tenants, at a time and manner described in rules promulgated by the department, regarding the requirements of this section, including installation of such devices

3509916.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
3509916.action_summary: Promulgate rules prescribing the records that owners must maintain relating to installation, maintenance, and heat data collection from temperature reporting devices.
3509916.quote: Maintain such records as the commissioner shall prescribe by rule relating to the installation and maintenance of such internet capable temperature reporting devices and collection of heat data from such devices

3509916.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
3509916.action_summary: Submit annual reports to the mayor and speaker of the council on implementation of heat inspection and temperature reporting device requirements, including selected dwellings, complaint and violation data, device information evaluation, and recommendations.
