3509916.quote: On August 1, 2021, and annually thereafter, the department shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a report containing, at a minimum: 1. Information about the implementation of the requirements of this section

2537056.action_summary: Establish a sexual health education task force consisting of at least nine members appointed after consultation with the speaker of the council.
2537056.quote: There shall be established a sexual health education task force consisting of at least nine members. Members of the task force shall be appointed by the mayor after consultation with the speaker of the council.

2537056.action_summary: Designate one member of the sexual health education task force as chairperson after consultation with the speaker of the council.
2537056.quote: One member shall be designated as chairperson by the mayor after consultation with the speaker.

2537056.actor_raw: the sexual health education task force
2537056.action_summary: Meet at least quarterly to review sexual health education curricula and implementation.
2537056.quote: Such task force shall meet at least quarterly.

2537056.actor_raw: the sexual health education task force
2537056.action_summary: Review information provided by the department regarding sexual health education curricula currently recommended by the department, including alignment with national standards, age-appropriateness, medical accuracy, sexual abuse prevention coverage, healthy relationships and consent coverage, and coverage of non-heterosexual issues.
2537056.quote: review information provided by the department and other stakeholders regarding the sexual health education curricula currently recommended by the department, including but not limited to, information on (a) whether such recommended curricula align with national standards, (b) whether such recommended curricula are age-appropriate and medically-accurate, (c) whether such recommended curricula cover the issue of sexual abuse prevention, (d) whether such recommended curricula cover the issues of healthy relationships and consent and (e) whether such recommended curricula cover issues pertaining to individuals and relationships other than heterosexual

2537056.actor_raw: the sexual health education task force
2537056.action_summary: Review the implementation of sexual health education for students, including participation rates, instruction time, instructor types, and assessment of curricula in use against national standards, age-appropriateness, medical accuracy, and coverage of sexual abuse prevention, healthy relationships, consent, and non-heterosexual issues.
2537056.quote: review the implementation of sexual health education for students, including but not limited to, (a) the number and percentage of students in each grade receiving sexual health education, (b) the amount of instruction time dedicated to sexual health education in each grade, (c) whether the instruction is provided by a teacher, other staff member, community group or other instructor, (d) whether curricula other than the sexual health education curricula recommended by the department are being used for instruction, and for each such curriculum (1) whether such curriculum aligns with national standards, (2) whether such curriculum is age-appropriate and medically-accurate

2537056.actor_raw: the sexual health education task force
2537056.action_summary: Submit a comprehensive report to the mayor and speaker of the council describing sexual health curricula coverage of sexual abuse prevention, healthy relationships, consent, and non-heterosexual issues; alignment with national standards; and recommendations for improvement, expansion, replacement, and professional development.
2537056.quote: issue a report that: (a) describes the extent to which the sexual health curricula recommended by the department include the topics of sexual abuse prevention, healthy relationships and consent and issues pertaining to individuals and relationships other than heterosexual, including but not limited to, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and gender non-conforming; (b) describes the extent to which such curricula align with national standards, are age-appropriate and medically-accurate; (c) makes recommendations for the improvement and expansion, or the replacement, of the recommended sexual health curricula for students
2537056.deadline_text: No later than December 1, 2017, the task force shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a report including the findings and recommendations of the task force pursuant to subdivision c of this section.

2537056.actor_raw: the sexual health education task force
2537056.action_summary: Provide opportunities for students and parents to submit comments and feedback during the review and recommendation process.
2537056.quote: The task force shall, in conducting its review and making recommendations pursuant to subdivision c of this section, provide an opportunity for students and parents to provide comments and feedback to the task force.

3458228.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
3458228.action_summary: Produce a consumer bill of rights regarding bail bond agents and provide it in downloadable format on the department's website in English and the designated citywide languages.
3458228.quote: The department shall produce a consumer bill of rights regarding bail bond agents. The department shall provide the consumer bill of rights in a downloadable format on the department's website in English and in the designated citywide languages.

3458228.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
3458228.action_summary: Determine the size and style for signs that bail bond agents must post at their business locations.
3458228.quote: in a size and style to be determined by the commissioner

6067643.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a quarterly report regarding LGBTQ homeless persons, beginning July 31, 2024, and quarterly thereafter.
6067643.quote: Beginning July 31, 2024, and quarterly thereafter, the department shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a report regarding LGBTQ homeless persons for the reporting period ending 1 month prior.

6067643.action_summary: Collaborate with the Department of Homeless Services to produce a quarterly report regarding LGBTQ homeless persons, beginning July 31, 2024.
6067643.quote: The department shall collaborate with the department of youth and community development to produce such report.

6067643.action_summary: In collaboration with the Department of Youth and Community Development, make best efforts to obtain information to prepare the required quarterly report, including provision of voluntary questionnaires at shelters, safe havens, drop-in centers, and runaway and homeless youth crisis services programs.
6067643.quote: The department, in collaboration with the department of youth and community development, shall make best efforts to obtain information to prepare the report required in this section, but shall not require any person to provide information for such purposes. Such efforts shall include the provision of voluntary questionnaires at shelters, safe havens, drop-in centers, and runaway and homeless youth crisis services programs.

6305639.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council, the public advocate, and the mayor, and publish on the department's website in machine-readable format, a quarterly report on removals conducted during the prior month, including details on removal type, location, initiation source, personnel, affected individuals, and costs.
6305639.quote: No later than 1 month after the effective date of the local law that added this section, and quarterly thereafter, the commissioner, in consultation with the police commissioner, the commissioner of sanitation, and the commissioner of parks and recreation, shall submit to the speaker of the council, the public advocate, and the mayor, and publish on the department's website, in a machine readable format, a report on removals conducted during the prior month.
6305639.deadline_text: No later than 1 month after the effective date of the local law that added this section, and quarterly thereafter

6305639.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council, the public advocate, and the mayor, and publish on the department's website in machine-readable format, a quarterly report on same-day outcomes for individuals experiencing homelessness involved in removals during the prior month, including data on housing offers, services, detentions, and arrests.
6305639.quote: No later than 1 month after the effective date of the local law that added this section, and quarterly thereafter, the commissioner shall submit to the speaker of the council, the public advocate, and the mayor and publish on the department's website, in a machine readable format, a report on the same-day outcomes for individuals experiencing homelessness involved in a removal during the prior month.
6305639.deadline_text: No later than 1 month after the effective date of the local law that added this section, and quarterly thereafter

6305639.action_summary: Include a data dictionary in the reports required by subdivisions b and c of section 21-152.
6305639.quote: The reports required by subdivisions b and c of this section shall include a data dictionary.

3903498.action_summary: Order repair of storm water disposal systems that no longer provide adequate drainage, or require installation of alternative approved methods of storm water disposal.
3903498.citation: Section PC 104.2 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: the commissioner shall order repair of such system as required by Section 28-301.1 of the Administrative Code; or if, in the judgment of the commissioner, repair of such system is not sufficient to ensure adequate drainage of storm water from such lot or development, the commissioner shall order that one of the methods of storm water disposal set forth in Chapter 11 shall be used to provide such drainage.

3903498.action_summary: Require inspection of any plumbing system to determine compliance with maintenance and operational requirements.
3903498.citation: Section PC 102.3.1 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: To determine compliance with this provision, the commissioner shall have the authority to require any plumbing system to be inspected.

3903498.action_summary: Require submittal of evaluation reports by approved agencies on prefabricated construction assemblies before approval and permit issuance.
3903498.citation: Section PC 108.2.2 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: Prior to the approval of a prefabricated construction assembly having concealed work and the issuance of a permit, the department shall require the submittal of an evaluation report by an approved agency on each prefabricated construction assembly, indicating the complete details of the installation, including a description of the system and its components, the basis upon which the system is being evaluated, test results and similar information and other data as necessary for the commissioner to determine conformance to this code.

3903498.action_summary: Prescribe qualifications for individuals authorized to witness backflow prevention assembly tests on behalf of approved agencies.
3903498.citation: Section PC 312.1.2 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: The department shall prescribe qualifications for individuals who are authorized to witness such tests on behalf of approved agencies, including but not limited to the requirement that such individuals shall be licensed master plumbers or registered design professionals with not less than 5 years experience in the inspection and testing of piping systems.

3903498.action_summary: Determine requirements necessary for strength, stability, proper operation, or public safety and welfare not specifically covered by the plumbing code.
3903498.citation: Section PC 102.9 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: Requirements necessary for the strength, stability or proper operation of an existing or proposed plumbing system, or for the public safety, health and general welfare, not specifically covered by this code, shall be determined by the commissioner.

3903498.action_summary: Determine on-site stormwater disposal system design and construction compliance.
3903498.citation: Section PC 107.6.2.2 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: Construction documents for such system shall be subject to the approval of the department.

3903498.action_summary: Approve proposed on-site stormwater disposal systems that meet applicable laws and rules for small alterations.
3903498.citation: Section PC 107.6.2.2, Exception 2 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: on-site disposal of stormwater conforming to the provisions of the applicable laws and rules as determined by the department is proposed for such enlargement and/or increase in impervious surface.

3903498.action_summary: Approve and oversee plumbing work in mental health centers where pipes must be concealed and fixtures bolted through walls.
3903498.citation: Section PC 405.6 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: In mental health centers, pipes or traps shall not be exposed, and fixtures shall be bolted through walls.

3903498.action_summary: Provide standardized inspection forms for annual inspections of backflow prevention assemblies that property owners must retain for five years.
3903498.citation: Section PC 312.10.1 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: Annual inspections shall be made of all backflow prevention assemblies, air gaps, spill-proof vacuum breakers, pressure vacuum breaker assemblies, and hose connection backflow preventers to determine whether they are operable on forms provided by the department.

3903498.action_summary: Determine acceptable use of commercial food waste disposer units only where approved by the Department of Environmental Protection.
3903498.citation: Section PC 413.3 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: Commercial food waste disposers shall be prohibited unless approved for use by the Department of Environmental Protection.

3903498.action_summary: Approve individual water supplies and oversee their connection to plumbing systems in coordination with other agencies.
3903498.citation: Section PC 602.3 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: No well or individual water supply shall be installed for any purpose without approval of the commissioner, the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene and the Department of Environmental Protection.

3903498.action_summary: Establish acceptance criteria for mechanical joint installations in water supply systems.
3903498.citation: Section PC 605.11.2 and PC 605.13.2 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: Mechanical joints shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and in conformance with acceptance criteria established by the commissioner.

3903498.action_summary: Provide forms and guidance for applicants to submit certifications of sewer availability and feasibility to the Department of Environmental Protection.
3903498.citation: Section PC 107.6.1.1 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: Applications for such certification shall be made to the Department of Environmental Protection on forms specified by such department (Department of Environmental Protection "house/site connection proposal application" or other form as specified in the rules of such department)

3903498.action_summary: Render interpretations of the plumbing code, adopt rules, and establish policies and procedures to clarify and implement the code's provisions.
3903498.citation: NYC Admin. Code § 28-601.2; Section PC 104.1 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: The commissioner shall have the authority to render interpretations of this code, adopt rules, and establish policies[,] and procedures in order to clarify and implement its provisions.

3903498.action_summary: Determine on-site disposal system design and construction compliance for sewage where public sewer is unavailable.
3903498.citation: Section PC 107.6.1.2 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: Construction documents for such system shall be subject to the approval of the department.

3903498.action_summary: Approve or accept written certification from licensed master plumbers that plumbing work was performed in compliance with code requirements in lieu of inspection for certain work types.
3903498.citation: Section PC 108.4.1 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: For ordinary plumbing work, the department may accept written certification from a licensed master plumber that the job was performed in compliance with the requirements of this code and rules of the department .

3903498.action_summary: Authorize temporary connection of buildings or systems to utility sources for testing plumbing systems or temporary occupancy.
3903498.citation: Section PC 108.6 of the New York City Plumbing Code
3903498.quote: The commissioner shall have the authority to authorize the temporary connection of the building or system to the utility source for the purpose of testing plumbing systems or for use under a temporary Certificate of Occupancy.

3022112.action_summary: Submit a quarterly report to the speaker of the council containing an anonymized compilation or summary of disclosures of identifying information made in violation of this chapter, and make such report available online.
3022112.quote: The chief privacy officer shall submit a quarterly report containing an anonymized compilation or summary of such disclosures to the speaker of the council and shall make such report available online.

3022112.action_summary: Submit a quarterly report to the speaker of the council containing an anonymized compilation or summary of collections or disclosures of identifying information under exigent circumstances, and make such report available online.
3022112.quote: The chief privacy officer shall submit a quarterly report containing an anonymized compilation or summary of such disclosures to the speaker of the council and make such report available online.

3754267.actor_raw: the department of citywide administrative services
3754267.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council a comprehensive plan revision for provisional employees required by civil service law.
3754267.quote: the department of citywide administrative services shall submit to the speaker of the council its comprehensive plan revision for provisional employees required pursuant to paragraph c-4 of subdivision 5 of section 65 of the civil service law

3754267.actor_raw: the department of citywide administrative services
3754267.action_summary: Notify the speaker of the council of the final decision from the state civil service commission, including any recommended changes to the provisional employee reduction plan.
3754267.quote: Such department shall notify the speaker of the council of the final decision, including any recommended changes to the plan, by the state civil service commission within 30 days of such decision

3331869.action_summary: Appoint four members to the charter revision commission within 60 days of enactment.
3331869.quote: four members appointed by the mayor
3331869.deadline_text: within 60 days of the enactment of this local law

3331869.actor_raw: the speaker of the city council
3331869.action_summary: Appoint four members to the charter revision commission within 60 days of enactment.
3331869.quote: four members appointed by the speaker of the city council
3331869.deadline_text: within 60 days of the enactment of this local law

3331869.action_summary: Appoint one member to the charter revision commission within 60 days of enactment.
3331869.quote: one member appointed by each borough president
3331869.deadline_text: within 60 days of the enactment of this local law

3331869.action_summary: Appoint one member to the charter revision commission within 60 days of enactment.
3331869.quote: one member appointed by the public advocate
3331869.deadline_text: within 60 days of the enactment of this local law

3331869.agency_full: Office of the New York City Comptroller
3331869.action_summary: Appoint one member to the charter revision commission within 60 days of enactment.
3331869.quote: one member appointed by the comptroller
3331869.deadline_text: within 60 days of the enactment of this local law

3331869.actor_raw: the speaker of the city council
3331869.action_summary: Appoint from among the commission membership a chairperson.
3331869.quote: The speaker of the city council shall appoint from among the membership a chairperson.

3331869.action_summary: Review the entire charter and prepare a draft of a proposed new or revised charter.
3331869.quote: The commission shall review the entire charter and prepare a draft of a proposed new or revised charter.

3331869.action_summary: Conduct not less than one public hearing in each of the five boroughs of the city.
3331869.quote: The commission shall conduct not less than one public hearing in each of the five boroughs of the city

3331869.action_summary: Conduct an extensive outreach campaign that solicits ideas and recommendations from a wide variety of civic and community leaders, and which encourages the public to participate in such hearings.
3331869.quote: shall conduct an extensive outreach campaign that solicits ideas and recommendations from a wide variety of civic and community leaders, and which encourages the public to participate in such hearings

3331869.action_summary: Maintain a website that includes public hearing agendas and transcripts, as well as webcasts of public hearings.
3331869.quote: The commission shall maintain a website that includes its public hearing agendas and transcripts, as well as webcasts of its public hearings.

3331869.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
3331869.action_summary: Make appropriations for the support of the commission.
3331869.quote: The city shall make appropriations for the support of the commission

3331869.action_summary: Complete and file in the office of the city clerk its proposed new or revised charter in time for submission to the electors not later than the second general election after the date of the enactment of this local law.
3331869.quote: shall complete and file in the office of the city clerk its proposed new or revised charter in time for submission to the electors not later than the second general election after the date of the enactment of this local law
3331869.deadline_text: not later than the second general election after the date of the enactment of this local law

2636744.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
2636744.action_summary: Issue ticket seller licenses to applicants upon approval of applications.
2636744.quote: Upon the approval of an application, the commissioner shall issue a ticket seller license to the applicant.

2636744.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
2636744.action_summary: Begin a study of pedestrian mobility and safety in locations where ticket sellers vend.
2636744.quote: No later than September 1, 2016, the department shall begin a study of pedestrian mobility and safety in locations where ticket sellers vend.

2636744.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
2636744.action_summary: Issue recommendations to the mayor and council regarding whether to restrict sidewalk portions for ticket vending, limit to curb areas, limit the number of licenses, and/or limit vending locations to improve pedestrian mobility and public safety.
2636744.quote: No later than February 1, 2017, the commissioner, in consultation with the commissioners of the department of transportation and the police department, shall issue to the mayor and to the council recommendations regarding whether it is advisable to restrict the portions of the sidewalk where ticket sellers may vend, limit such vending to the portion of the sidewalk that is at or near the curb, limit the number of ticket seller licenses, and/or limit the locations in which ticket sellers may vend in order to improve pedestrian mobility and public safety.

2636744.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
2636744.action_summary: Take all actions necessary for implementation of the ticket seller licensing law, including promulgation of rules and processing of applications, prior to the effective date.
2636744.quote: the commissioner shall take all actions necessary for its implementation, including the promulgation of rules and the processing of applications pursuant to section 20-551, as added by section one of this local law, prior to such effective date.

2636744.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
2636744.action_summary: Enforce all provisions of the ticket seller licensing subchapter and any rules promulgated pursuant to it.
2636744.quote: Authorized officers and employees of the department, and any department designated by the commissioner, as well as any police or peace officer, shall have the power to enforce any provision of this subchapter or any rule promulgated pursuant to this subchapter.

1681040.action_summary: Promulgate rules necessary for implementation of fire sprinkler requirements for animal service facilities.
1681040.quote: the commissioner of buildings shall take such measures as are necessary for its implementation, including the promulgation of rules, prior to its effective date
affected_groups: animal service facility owners and operators

2513780.action_summary: Choose and announce the deadline date for organizations to submit debate sponsorship applications in any year an election is held for city-wide offices.
2513780.quote: not later than a date chosen by the board in any year in which an election is held for city-wide offices

2404420.agency_full: Not specified in the law text
2404420.action_summary: Include in publicity materials information regarding the availability of wheelchair accessibility, communication access real-time translation, sign language interpretation, assistive listening systems, and other accommodations for people with disabilities at events open to the public, designated by appropriate symbols.
2404420.quote: All materials described in subdivision c of this section, to the extent practicable for the selected form of media, shall include information regarding the availability of: 1. wheelchair accessibility at the venue or venues for the event, which shall be designated by the symbol provided for in section one hundred one of the executive law, or successor symbol; 2. communication access real-time translation, which shall be designated by the letters "C-A-R-T"; sign language interpretation at the event for persons who are deaf or hard of hearing, which shall be designated by the international symbol or successor symbol to indicate the availability of sign language interpretation; or any other technology or service for persons who are deaf or hard of hearing, at the venue or venues for the event; 3. assistive listening systems for people with hearing loss at the venue or venues for the event, which shall be designated by the international symbol of access for hearing loss or successor symbol, and when available, the specific kind of system, including, but not limited to, induction loop assistive listening systems; and 4. any other accommodations for people with disabilities that will be available at the venue or venues for the event, which shall be indicated by the relevant international symbol if applicable.

2404420.actor_raw: the mayor's office for people with disabilities
2404420.agency_full: Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities
2404420.action_summary: Develop, make available on its website, and distribute to each agency and members of the public a guide to assist agencies in notifying the public about availability of and responding to requests for reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities.
2404420.quote: The mayor's office for people with disabilities shall develop, make available on its website, and distribute to each agency, and members of the public upon request, a guide to assist agencies in notifying the public about the availability of, and responding to requests for, reasonable accommodations described in subdivision d of this section.

2404420.actor_raw: the mayor's office for people with disabilities
2404420.agency_full: Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities
2404420.action_summary: Periodically update the guide containing a comprehensive list of common disability access symbols.
2404420.quote: The guide shall contain a comprehensive list of common disability access symbols, and shall be periodically updated as appropriate.

2404420.actor_raw: the mayor's office for people with disabilities
2404420.agency_full: Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities
2404420.action_summary: Promulgate rules necessary for implementation of this section.
2404420.quote: the mayor's office for people with disabilities shall take such actions as are necessary for its implementation, including the promulgation of rules, prior to such date.

2404420.action_summary: Comply with the open data technical standards manual when publishing data sets.
affected_groups: users of the open data portal

4918743.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
4918743.action_summary: Specify the particular manner in which a temporary truck loading zone for an affected street segment or intersection should be maintained when a permittee's work obstructs an existing truck loading zone.
4918743.quote: The department shall specify the particular manner in which the temporary truck loading zone for such street segment or intersection should be maintained.

4918743.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
4918743.action_summary: Regulate commercial parking meter areas with a parking meter, mobile payment system, parking reservation system, or other means.
4918743.quote: The department shall regulate commercial parking meter areas with a parking meter, mobile payment system, a parking reservation system, or other means as determined by the department.

4918743.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
4918743.action_summary: Evaluate paid commercial parking rules and determine whether there are locations where time limits of more than three hours are appropriate based on curb access needs and delivery consolidation impacts.
4918743.quote: The department shall evaluate its paid commercial parking rules and determine whether there are locations where time limits of more than three hours are appropriate based on curb access needs and if such changes encourage delivery consolidation or reduction of truck trips.

4918743.agency_full: New York City Department of Transportation
4918743.action_summary: Promulgate rules and take such measures as are necessary for implementation of this local law.
4918743.quote: the department shall take such measures as are necessary for the implementation of this local law, including the promulgation of rules, before such date.
4918743.deadline_text: before 180 days after it becomes law

6632607.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
6632607.action_summary: Create and make available notices containing information about safe/sick time rights and post them in downloadable format on the department's website in multiple languages.
6632607.quote: The department shall create and make available notices that contain the information required pursuant to subdivision a of this section concerning safe/sick time and such notices shall be posted in a downloadable format on the department's website in Chinese, English, French-Creole, Italian, Korean, Russian, Spanish and any other language deemed appropriate by the department.

6632629.action_summary: Appoint members to the youth board, ensuring at least 3 members are between ages 16 and 24, and making efforts to identify persons with demonstrated experience in organizations or activities directly concerned with the welfare of youth.
6632629.quote: at least 3 members of the youth board shall be between the age of 16 and 24. No member of the board shall be removed or required to step down due to reaching 25 years of age. If a vacancy arises and no remaining member of the board is between the age of 16 and 24, such vacancy must be filled by a person between the age of 16 and 24.

6632629.action_summary: Make recommendations for the appointment of 14 members to the youth board, making efforts to identify persons with demonstrated experience in organizations or activities directly concerned with the welfare of youth.
6632629.quote: The youth board shall consist of up to 28 members, appointed by the mayor, 14 of whom shall be appointed upon recommendation of the city council. In making such appointments and recommendations, the mayor and the city council shall make efforts to identify persons who have demonstrated experience with organizations or activities directly concerned with the welfare of youth.

5656557.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
5656557.action_summary: Select 50 class A multiple dwellings to be subject to heat sensor installation and inspection requirements every year.
5656557.quote: No later than July 1, 2024, and every year thereafter, the department shall select 50 class A multiple dwellings that shall be subject to the requirements of this subdivision.
5656557.deadline_text: No later than July 1, 2024, and every year thereafter
affected_groups: tenants in class A multiple dwellings
property owners of class A multiple dwellings

5656557.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
5656557.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing criteria for selecting class A multiple dwellings subject to heat sensor requirements, including violation history and heat complaints.
5656557.quote: The department shall select such class A multiple dwellings pursuant to criteria set forth in rules of the department, which shall include, but need not be limited to: (i) the number of violations of subdivision a of section 27-2029 over the preceding two years, and (ii) whether the department has received heat complaints from more than one dwelling unit in such class A multiple dwelling.
affected_groups: property owners of class A multiple dwellings

5656557.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
5656557.action_summary: Conduct inspections of each selected class A multiple dwelling at least twice each month during heat season for compliance with heat and temperature reporting device requirements.
5656557.quote: Annually, for the duration of heat season, the department shall conduct inspections of each class A multiple dwelling selected pursuant to this subdivision at least twice each month, without receipt of complaints, for compliance with the requirements of this section, section 27-2028 and subdivision a of section 27-2029, consistent with applicable law and in accordance with rules of the department.
affected_groups: tenants in class A multiple dwellings
property owners of class A multiple dwellings

5656557.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
5656557.action_summary: Inspect during heat season inspections to ensure internet capable temperature reporting devices are installed in accordance with department rules.
5656557.quote: In the course of such inspections, the department shall also inspect to ensure the device is installed in accordance with subparagraph (b) of paragraph 3 of this subdivision.
affected_groups: tenants in class A multiple dwellings
property owners of class A multiple dwellings

5656557.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
5656557.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing procedures for property owner notification of heat sensor requirements, installation deadlines, tenant rights, and device placement options.
5656557.quote: Notify all tenants, at a time and manner described in rules promulgated by the department, regarding the requirements of this section, including installation of such devices, instructions on how to access the information collected by such devices, the tenant's right of refusal, and the tenant's right to request that such device be installed in a living room of the tenant's choice within the dwelling in accordance with subparagraph (b) of this paragraph
affected_groups: tenants in class A multiple dwellings
property owners of class A multiple dwellings

5656557.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
5656557.action_summary: Prescribe by rule the records property owners must maintain relating to installation, maintenance, and heat data collection from internet capable temperature reporting devices.
5656557.quote: Maintain such records as the commissioner shall prescribe by rule relating to the installation and maintenance of such internet capable temperature reporting devices and collection of heat data from such devices, and make such records available to the commissioner upon request, consistent with applicable law and in accordance with rules of the department
affected_groups: property owners of class A multiple dwellings

5656557.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
5656557.action_summary: Post notices in designated citywide languages in prominent places of selected multiple dwellings informing tenants of heat sensor requirements, inspection frequency, opt-out rights, and heat complaint procedures.
5656557.quote: Upon selection of a multiple dwelling pursuant to paragraph 1 of this subdivision, the department shall post a notice in each of the designated citywide languages in section 23-1101 in a prominent place of such multiple dwelling, notifying tenants of the requirements of this section, a tenant's option to refuse the installation of such device in their dwelling unit, the requirement of twice monthly inspections by the department, and a tenant's option to call 311 to file a complaint relating to inadequate heat and to check the department's website for the issuance of heat violations.
affected_groups: tenants in class A multiple dwellings

5656557.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
5656557.action_summary: Monitor that required notices are posted throughout the time period that each multiple dwelling is subject to inspection under the heat sensor program.
5656557.quote: The department shall monitor that such notice is posted throughout the time period that such multiple dwelling is subject to inspection by the department pursuant to paragraph 2 of this subdivision.
affected_groups: tenants in class A multiple dwellings

5656557.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
5656557.action_summary: Submit an annual report to the mayor and speaker of the council by August 1 of each year documenting heat sensor program implementation, selected dwellings, violations, complaints, and temperature data analysis.
5656557.quote: On or before August 1 of each year, the department shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a report containing, at a minimum: 1. Information about the implementation of the requirements of this section; 2. A list of the class A multiple dwellings selected in the most recent selection cycle pursuant to subdivision b of this section; 3. The number of heat complaints from each of the two immediately preceding heat seasons associated with each class A multiple dwelling on such list; 4. The number of violations of section 27-2028 and subdivision a of section 27-2029 issued in each of the two immediately preceding heat seasons to each class A multiple dwelling on such list; 5. Where such information is available to the department, whether the owner of a class A multiple dwelling on such list corrected the condition that resulted in any violation of section 27-2028 or subdivision a of section 27-2029; 6. An evaluation of information that was collected from internet capable temperature reporting devices installed pursuant to this section; 7. The number of complaints received and violations issued during the period of time that the internet capable temperature reporting device was installed pursuant to this section
5656557.deadline_text: On or before August 1 of each year
affected_groups: tenants in class A multiple dwellings
property owners of class A multiple dwellings

5656557.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
5656557.action_summary: Include in the August 1, 2025 annual report a recommendation as to whether the heat sensor requirements should remain in effect based on temperature data collected.
5656557.quote: For the report due August 1, 2025, a recommendation based on the information required by paragraph 6 of this subdivision as to whether the requirements of this section should remain in effect.
affected_groups: tenants in class A multiple dwellings
property owners of class A multiple dwellings

5656557.agency_full: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
5656557.action_summary: Establish by rule a discharge process allowing property owners to be relieved of heat sensor requirements upon meeting specified compliance criteria.
5656557.quote: An owner of a multiple dwelling selected pursuant to this subdivision who has not complied with the requirements of paragraph 3 of this subdivision but is otherwise eligible for discharge pursuant to subparagraph (a) of this paragraph may be discharged from the requirements of this section upon payment of a penalty of $500 as the department shall provide by rule for each violation of this section.
affected_groups: property owners of class A multiple dwellings

5188250.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
5188250.action_summary: Receive, review and approve applications for permits, certificates and approvals; review design and installation documents; issue permits; inspect buildings, structures and premises; and administer and enforce the fire code provisions.
5188250.quote: the department shall receive, review and, if satisfactory, approve, applications for permits, certificates and other approvals, and design and installation documents required to be submitted to the department by this code or the construction codes, issue permits, inspect buildings, structures, facilities, premises, marine vessels, watercraft and motor vehicles for the purpose of enforcing compliance with the requirements of this code, and otherwise administer, implement and enforce the provisions of this code.

5188250.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
5188250.action_summary: Maintain a current list of all testing services and laboratories acceptable for testing articles, equipment and devices, and a current list of all acceptable articles, equipment and devices, and make such lists available for public inspection.
5188250.quote: A current list of all testing services and laboratories acceptable to the department for the purpose of testing articles, equipment and devices, and a current list of all acceptable articles, equipment and devices shall be maintained by the department and made available for public inspection.

5188250.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
5188250.action_summary: Revoke or suspend certificates for good cause, providing notice and opportunity to be heard prior to suspension or revocation except in circumstances of imminent threat to public safety.
5188250.quote: The commissioner may, at any time, revoke or suspend a certificate for good cause. The certificate holder shall be afforded notice and an opportunity to be heard prior to any such suspension or revocation except that, in the circumstance of an imminent threat to public safety, such notice and opportunity to be heard may be given promptly after such revocation or suspension.

5188250.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
5188250.action_summary: Authorize the Department of Buildings to review construction documents for compliance with design and installation requirements for stationary energy storage systems, fire apparatus access roads, rooftop access and obstructions, and other design requirements as the commissioner determines facilitate the design and construction process.
5188250.quote: The commissioner may authorize the Department of Buildings to review construction documents filed with that agency for compliance with the design and installation requirements of this code for stationary energy storage systems, fire apparatus access roads, rooftop access and obstructions, and such other design and installation requirements as the commissioner, in consultation with the Commissioner of Buildings, may determine facilitates the design and construction process.

5188250.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
5188250.action_summary: Adopt rules setting forth penalties for submission of false or fraudulent documents certifying compliance with fire code and rules, including penalties such as disqualification from submission of professionally certified applications.
5188250.quote: The commissioner may adopt rules setting forth the penalty for submission of false or fraudulent documents certifying compliance with the requirements of this code and the rules. Penalties may include disqualification from submission of professionally certified applications.

5188250.agency_full: Fire Department of the City of New York
5188250.action_summary: Grant applications for certificates of approval upon determination that the article, equipment or device is designed for its intended purpose and can be safely operated in accordance with the fire code, rules and other applicable laws.
5188250.quote: The commissioner may grant an application for a certificate of approval upon a determination that the application article, equipment or device is designed for the purpose for which it is to be used and can be safely operated in accordance with this code, the rules and other applicable laws, rules and regulations.

3927504.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website an annual report on the demographics of students in grades kindergarten through eight, including enrollment numbers disaggregated by special education services, English language learner status, free or reduced price meals eligibility, temporary housing status, out-of-zone and out-of-district attendance, grade level, race or ethnicity, gender, primary home language, and test performance levels.
3927504.quote: the department shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a report regarding the following: a. For each community school district, school within such district, special program within such school, and grade within such school, the total number of public school students enrolled in the preceding school year in grades kindergarten through eight
3927504.deadline_text: by December 1 of each year thereafter
affected_groups: students in grades kindergarten through eight

3927504.action_summary: Report for each school and special program the admissions process used, criteria or methods used to supplement the admissions process, a side-by-side comparison of racial and ethnic demographics with the applicable attendance zone and community school district, and whether the school or program is becoming more or less similar to the demographics of the applicable attendance zone and community school district.
3927504.quote: For each school and special program set forth in subdivision a of this section, the department shall report: 1. The admissions process used by such school or special program, including but not limited to, whether admission to such school or special program is based on a lottery; a geographic zone; an audition; a screening of candidates for such school; including a detailed description of such screening; or a standardized test; and
3927504.deadline_text: by December 1 of each year thereafter

3927504.action_summary: Report for each community school district on efforts made to encourage a diverse student body in schools and special programs, including details such as strategic site selection, recommendations to the community education council regarding attendance zones, resource allocation, and targeted outreach and recruitment efforts.
3927504.quote: For each community school district, the department shall report on whether the department made any efforts in such community school district during the preceding school year to encourage a diverse student body in its schools and special programs and, if so, the details of such efforts, including, but not limited to, strategic site selection of new schools and special programs, making recommendations to the community education council to draw attendance zones with recognition of the demographics of neighborhoods, the allocation of resources for schools and special programs, and targeted outreach and recruitment efforts.
3927504.deadline_text: by December 1 of each year thereafter

3927504.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website an annual report on the demographics of high school students, including enrollment numbers disaggregated by special education services, English language learner status, free or reduced price meals eligibility, temporary housing status, over-the-counter enrollment, grade level, race or ethnicity, gender, English language learner status, primary home language, and test performance levels.
3927504.quote: the department shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a report regarding the following: a. For each public high school, the total number of students enrolled in grades nine through twelve in the preceding school year and the number and percentage of such students who:
3927504.deadline_text: by December 1 of each year thereafter
affected_groups: high school students in grades nine through twelve

3927504.action_summary: Report for each high school the admissions process used and other criteria or methods used for admissions, including preferences established under the department's diversity in admissions pilot, over-the-counter admissions, waitlists, and principal's discretion.
3927504.quote: For each high school set forth in subdivision a of this section, the department shall report: 1. The admissions process used by such school, such as whether admissions to such school is based on a lottery; a geographic zone; an audition; a screening of candidates for such school, including a detailed description of such screening; or a standardized test; and
3927504.deadline_text: by December 1 of each year thereafter

3927504.action_summary: Report on an individual high school level on efforts each high school has taken to encourage a diverse student body, including strategic site selection of new schools and special programs, allocation of resources, and targeted outreach and recruitment efforts.
3927504.quote: The department shall report, on an individual high school level, on efforts each individual high school has taken during the preceding school year to encourage a diverse student body including, but not limited to, strategic site selection of new schools and special programs, the allocation of resources for schools and special programs, and targeted outreach and recruitment efforts.
3927504.deadline_text: by December 1 of each year thereafter

3927504.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website an annual report on the demographics of students in pre-kindergarten programs operated by the department, disaggregated by race or ethnicity and gender.
3927504.quote: the department shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on its website a report regarding the following: a. For each school that offers a pre-kindergarten program, the total number of students enrolled in the preceding school year in such program, disaggregated by race or ethnicity and gender.
3927504.deadline_text: by December 1 of each year thereafter

3013584.action_summary: Establish and administer the excise tax on tobacco products, collect tax returns from wholesale dealers, and enforce tax collection.
3013584.quote: an excise tax on the sale of tobacco products is hereby imposed and shall be paid on all tobacco products possessed in the city for sale. Any dealer or distributor who pays the tax to the commissioner of finance shall collect the tax from the purchaser or consumer.

3013584.action_summary: Notify wholesale dealer license holders of violations and provide opportunity for hearing before suspension or revocation.
3013584.quote: Before the commissioner of finance suspends or revokes a wholesale tobacco license or notifies the commissioner of consumer affairs of a finding of a violation of this chapter with respect to a retail tobacco license pursuant to paragraph (1) of this subdivision, the commissioner of finance shall notify the holder and the holder shall be entitled to a hearing, if desired, if the holder, within ninety days from the date of such notification

3013584.action_summary: Require dealers to maintain and produce invoices and records of cigarettes and tobacco products received and delivered for three years.
3013584.quote: At the time of delivering cigarettes to any person in the city, each agent or wholesale dealer shall make a true duplicate invoice showing the date of delivery, the number of packages and the number of cigarettes contained therein in each shipment of cigarettes delivered. At the time of delivering tobacco products to any person in the city, each wholesale dealer shall make a true duplicate invoice showing the date of delivery, the number of packages and the number of tobacco products contained therein as well as any tobacco products not in packages in each shipment of tobacco products delivered

3013584.action_summary: Investigate failures to pay tobacco tax and enforce compliance with the chapter and promulgated rules.
3013584.quote: The commissioner of finance shall investigate any failure to pay the tax required by this chapter or any other failure to comply with this chapter or the rules or regulations promulgated thereunder, and shall take the necessary steps to enforce compliance therewith.

3013584.action_summary: Determine the amount of unpaid tobacco tax based on available information and external indices when a person fails to pay or file a required return.
3013584.quote: If any person fails to pay the tax, or to file a return required by this chapter, or if a return, when filed, is insufficient and the maker fails to file a corrected or sufficient return within ten days after the same may be required by notice from the commissioner of finance, the commissioner of finance shall determine the amount of tax due from such information as may be obtainable or on the basis of external indices, such as number of cigarettes purchased or sold, number of tobacco products purchased or sold, stock on hand, volume of sales by similar dealers and/or other factors.
3013584.deadline_text: within ten days after the same may be required by notice from the commissioner of finance

3013584.action_summary: Refund erroneous, illegal, or unconstitutionally collected taxes and process refund applications.
3013584.quote: In the manner provided in this subdivision the commissioner of finance shall refund, without interest, any tax, interest or penalty erroneously, illegally or unconstitutionally collected or paid.

3013584.action_summary: Seize and forfeit untaxed tobacco products discovered by peace officers or police officers.
3013584.quote: Whenever a police officer designated in section 1.20 of the criminal procedure law or a peace officer employed by the department of finance, including but not limited to the sheriff, undersheriff or deputy sheriffs of the city designated as peace officers in subdivision two of section 2.10 of the criminal procedure law, discovers any tobacco products subject to any tax provided by chapter 13 of this title, and upon which the tax has not been paid, he or she is hereby authorized and empowered forthwith to seize and take possession of such tobacco products, together with any vending machine or receptacle in which such tobacco products are held for sale. Such tobacco products, vending machine or receptacle seized by such police officer or such peace officer shall be turned over to the commissioner of finance.

3013584.action_summary: Conduct hearings to determine propriety of seizures of untaxed tobacco products and issue decisions.
3013584.quote: The seized tobacco products and any vending machine or receptacle seized therewith, but not the money contained in such vending machine or receptacle, shall thereupon be forfeited to the city, unless the person from whom the seizure is made, or the owner of such seized tobacco products, vending machine or receptacle, or any other person having an interest in such property, shall within ten days of such seizure, apply to the commissioner of finance for a hearing to determine the propriety of the seizure, or unless the commissioner of finance shall on his own motion release the seized tobacco products, vending machine or receptacle. After such hearing the commissioner of finance shall give notice of his or her decision to the petitioner.
3013584.deadline_text: within ten days of such seizure
affected_groups: persons from whom tobacco was seized

3013584.action_summary: Seize and forfeit taxed tobacco products sold or possessed by unlicensed dealers.
3013584.quote: Whenever a police officer designated in section 1.20 of the criminal procedure law or a peace officer employed by the department of finance, including but not limited to the sheriff, undersheriff or deputy sheriffs of the city designated as peace officers in subdivision two of section 2.10 of the criminal procedure law, discovers any tobacco products, other than flavored tobacco products, subject to any tax provided by chapter 13 of this title, and upon which the tax has been paid, but such tobacco products are sold, offered for sale or possessed by a person in violation of section 11-1303, 17-703 or 20-202, he or she is hereby authorized and empowered forthwith to seize and take possession of such tobacco products, together with any vending machine or receptacle in which such tobacco products are held for sale. Such tobacco products, vending machine or receptacle seized by such police officer or such peace officer shall be turned over to the commissioner of finance.

3013584.actor_raw: the department of health and mental hygiene
3013584.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3013584.action_summary: Enforce the provisions of subchapter 17-701 et seq. regarding tobacco product sales and pricing.
3013584.quote: The department of health and mental hygiene and the department of finance shall enforce the provisions of this subchapter.

3013584.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
3013584.action_summary: Enforce sections 17-703, 17-703.1, 17-704, 17-704.1, 17-705 and 17-706 regarding retail tobacco dealer licensing and sales regulations.
3013584.quote: The department of consumer affairs shall enforce sections 17-703, 17-703.1, 17-704, 17-704.1, 17-705 and 17-706.

3013584.actor_raw: the department of health and mental hygiene, the department of consumer affairs and the department of finance
3013584.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3013584.action_summary: Notify each other within thirty days of final determination that a retail dealer has violated tobacco sales or licensing provisions.
3013584.quote: The department of health and mental hygiene, the department of consumer affairs and the department of finance shall notify each other within thirty days of a final determination that a retail dealer has been found to be in violation of section 17-703, 17-703.2, 17-704, 17-704.1, 17-705 or subdivision a or b of section 17-706 of this subchapter.
3013584.deadline_text: within thirty days of a final determination

3013584.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection

3013584.quote: The department of health and mental hygiene, the department of consumer affairs and the department of finance shall notify each other within thirty days of a final determination that a retail dealer has been found to be in violation of section 17-703, 17-703.2, 17-704, 17-704.1, 17-705 or subdivision a or b of section 17-706 of this subchapter.
3013584.deadline_text: within thirty days of a final determination

3013584.action_summary: Notify the department of health and mental hygiene and department of consumer affairs within thirty days of final determination that a retail dealer violated tobacco provisions.
3013584.quote: The department of health and mental hygiene, the department of consumer affairs and the department of finance shall notify each other within thirty days of a final determination that a retail dealer has been found to be in violation of section 17-703, 17-703.2, 17-704, 17-704.1, 17-705 or subdivision a or b of section 17-706 of this subchapter.
3013584.deadline_text: within thirty days of a final determination

3013584.action_summary: Suspend or revoke wholesale tobacco dealer licenses after hearing when holder fails to comply with chapter provisions or commissioner rules.
3013584.quote: After a hearing, the commissioner of finance may suspend or revoke a wholesale tobacco license and the commissioner of consumer affairs, upon notice from the commissioner of finance, may suspend or revoke a retail tobacco license whenever the commissioner of finance finds that the holder thereof has failed to comply with any of the provisions of this chapter or any rules of the commissioner of finance prescribed, adopted and promulgated under this chapter.

3013584.action_summary: Examine books, papers, invoices, records, and stock of cigarettes and tobacco products at dealer premises to verify tax compliance.
3013584.quote: the commissioner of finance or the commissioner's duly authorized representatives are hereby authorized to examine the books, papers, invoices and other records, and stock of cigarettes or tobacco products in and upon any premises where the same are placed, stored and sold, and equipment of any such agent or dealer pertaining to the sale and delivery of cigarettes or tobacco products taxable under this chapter.

3013584.action_summary: Issue warrants to collect unpaid tobacco taxes through seizure and sale of property.
3013584.quote: In addition to all other remedies for the collection of any taxes, penalties or interest due under the provisions of this chapter, the commissioner of finance may with respect to any tax imposed under section 11-1302 or any penalties or interest related thereto issue a warrant, directed to the city sheriff commanding the sheriff to levy upon and sell the real and personal property of the person liable for the tax which may be found within the city

3013584.action_summary: Destroy forfeited tobacco products or use them for law enforcement purposes, with notice publication.
3013584.quote: The commissioner of finance may, within a reasonable time after the forfeiture to the city of such vending machine or receptacle under this section, upon publication of a notice to such effect for at least five successive days, in a newspaper published or circulated in the city, sell such forfeited vending machine or receptacle at public sale and pay the proceeds into the general fund of the city. Tobacco products forfeited to the city under this section shall be destroyed or used for law enforcement purposes, except that tobacco products that violate, or are suspected of violating, federal trademark laws or import laws shall not be used for law enforcement purposes. If the commissioner determines the tobacco products forfeited under this section may not be used for law enforcement purposes, the commissioner of finance must, within a reasonable time after the forfeiture to the city of such cigarettes, upon publication of a notice to such effect for at least five successive days, prior to destruction, in a newspaper published or circulated in the city, destroy such forfeited tobacco products.

3013584.action_summary: Permit redemption of seized vending machines or receptacles upon payment of civil penalties and costs.
3013584.quote: In the alternative, the commissioner of finance, on reasonable notice by mail or otherwise, may permit the person from whom a seizure of tobacco products under this section was made, to redeem any vending machine or receptacle seized with such tobacco products, or may permit the owner of any such vending machine or receptacle to redeem the same, upon the payment of any civil penalty imposed pursuant to chapter 7 of title 17 or subchapter 1 of chapter 2 of title 20 of this code and the costs incurred in such proceeding.
affected_groups: persons from whom tobacco was seized

3013584.action_summary: Destroy forfeited tobacco products from unlicensed dealers or use for law enforcement, with notice publication.
3013584.quote: The commissioner of finance may, within a reasonable time after the forfeiture to the city of such vending machine or receptacle under this section, upon publication of a notice to such effect for at least five successive days, in a newspaper published or circulated in the city, sell such forfeited vending machine or receptacle at public sale and pay the proceeds into the general fund of the city. Tobacco products forfeited to the city under this section shall be destroyed or used for law enforcement purposes, except that tobacco products that violate, or are suspected of violating, federal trademark laws or import laws shall not be used for law enforcement purposes. If the commissioner determines the tobacco products forfeited under this section may not be used for law enforcement purposes, the commissioner of finance must, within a reasonable time after the forfeiture to the city of such tobacco products, upon publication of a notice to such effect for at least five successive days, prior to destruction, in a newspaper published or circulated in the city, destroy such forfeited tobacco products.

3013584.action_summary: Permit redemption of seized vending machines from unlicensed dealers upon payment of civil penalties and costs.
3013584.quote: In the alternative, the commissioner of finance, on reasonable notice by mail or otherwise, may permit the person from whom a seizure of tobacco products under this section was made, to redeem any vending machine or receptacle seized with such tobacco products, or may permit the owner of any such vending machine or receptacle to redeem the same, upon the payment of any civil penalty imposed pursuant to chapter seven of title 17 or subchapter one of chapter two of title 20 of this code and the costs incurred in such proceeding.

3013584.agency_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
3013584.action_summary: Upon notice from the commissioner of finance, suspend or revoke retail tobacco licenses when holder fails to comply with chapter provisions or commissioner rules.
3013584.quote: the commissioner of consumer affairs, upon notice from the commissioner of finance, may suspend or revoke a retail tobacco license whenever the commissioner of finance finds that the holder thereof has failed to comply with any of the provisions of this chapter or any rules of the commissioner of finance prescribed, adopted and promulgated under this chapter.

3013584.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
3013584.action_summary: Modify by rule the price floors for tobacco products to account for changes in the New York-northern New Jersey-Long Island consumer price index and tax changes.
3013584.quote: The department may modify by rule the price floors described in this subdivision to account for changes in the New York--northern New Jersey--Long Island consumer price index, adjusted for inflation, or changes in taxes for any of these products.

3013584.actor_raw: the department of finance, the department of health and mental hygiene and the department of consumer affairs
3013584.action_summary: Take measures necessary for implementation of this law, including promulgation of rules, prior to the effective date.
3013584.quote: the department of finance, the department of health and mental hygiene and the department of consumer affairs may take such measures as are necessary for the implementation of this local law, including the promulgation of rules, prior to such date.
3013584.deadline_text: prior to the effective date, which is the first day of the calendar month next following the 270th day after it becomes law

3913336.action_summary: Publish a finding by September 1, 2019 if there is insufficient capacity to provide site safety training required by Section 3321 of the New York city building code to workers who would need such training, and if so, establish a later second compliance date not later than June 1, 2020.
3913336.citation: Section 1, amending NYC Building Code § 3302.1 (SITE SAFETY TRAINING (SST) SECOND COMPLIANCE DATE)
3913336.quote: if the department publishes a finding by September 1, 2019 that there is insufficient capacity to provide the training required by Section 3321 of the New York city building code to the workers who would need such training, a later date established by the department, provided that such date is not later than June 1, 2020.

2537046.actor_raw: the mayor, or an agency designated by the mayor
2537046.action_summary: Analyze data from other agencies to estimate the number of vacant residential buildings and vacant lots in areas zoned to permit residential use, excluding coastal flood zones.
2537046.quote: The mayor, or an agency designated by the mayor, shall analyze data provided under subdivisions b and c of this section to provide an estimate of the number of vacant residential buildings and vacant lots located in areas zoned to permit residential use.
2537046.deadline_text: no later than 90 days after the effective date of the local law that added this section and shall be completed within three years thereafter

2523139.action_summary: Submit an agency utilization plan annually to the commissioner for minority and women-owned business enterprise participation, and upon approval, publish the plan on the City's website.
2523139.quote: each agency which, during the fiscal year which ended on June 30 of the preceding fiscal year, has made procurements in excess of five million dollars, without counting procurements that are exempt pursuant to paragraph two of subdivision q of this section, shall submit an agency utilization plan for the fiscal year commencing in July of the year when such plan is to be submitted to the commissioner. Upon approval by the commissioner, such plan shall be submitted to the speaker of the council, and shall be published on the City's website.

2637106.action_summary: Discontinue retail dealer licensing and comply with the prohibition on new or renewed retail dealer licenses after the enactment date.
2637106.quote: After the date of enactment of this local law, a pharmacy shall not be allowed to apply for a license to engage in business as a retail dealer

2240514.action_summary: Publish findings demonstrating that any alternative green building standards utilized are not less stringent than the LEED standards described in the law.
2240514.quote: If the mayor elects to utilize green building standards other than the LEED green building rating system, the mayor shall publish findings demonstrating that such other green building standards are not less stringent than the LEED standards described above

2240514.action_summary: Review and update green building standards as necessary, no less often than once every three years.
2240514.quote: The green building standards utilized by the city in accordance with this section shall be reviewed and updated, as necessary, by the mayor no less often that once every three years.

2240514.actor_raw: the mayor or an office or agency designated by the mayor
2240514.action_summary: Submit to the council and make publicly available online a report within 60 days after adopting alternative design and construction standards, describing the standards, occupancy groups, less stringent provisions, and how the standards comply with LEED certified rating standards.
2240514.quote: Within 60 days after adopting such alternative standards, submit to the council and make publicly available online a report that, at a minimum: (A) Describes such standards and the occupancy groups to which they will apply; (B) Identifies any provisions in such standards that are less stringent than the standards described in paragraph (1)
2240514.deadline_text: Within 60 days after adopting such alternative standards

2240514.actor_raw: the mayor or an office or agency designated by the mayor
2240514.action_summary: Submit to the council and make publicly available online a report every third fiscal year thereafter regarding whether less stringent alternative standards continue to be necessary.
2240514.quote: If such alternative standards are less stringent than the standards described in paragraph (1) of this subdivision, in every third fiscal year thereafter, submit to the council and make publicly available online a report that, at a minimum, states whether the mayor or such designated office or agency has determined that such less stringent standards continue to be necessary

2240514.action_summary: Report to the council at the conclusion of each fiscal year the exemptions from green building standards granted pursuant to subdivision f.
2240514.quote: At the conclusion of each fiscal year the mayor shall report to the council the exemptions granted pursuant to this section.

2240514.actor_raw: the mayor or an office or agency designated by the mayor
2240514.action_summary: By rule, establish an alternative certification process for capital projects complying with alternative standards promulgated for certain occupancy groups.
2240514.quote: The mayor or an office or agency designated by the mayor shall by rule establish an alternative certification process for capital projects that are complying with alternative standards promulgated by the mayor or such designated office or agency

2240514.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council by no later than December 1 of each year a report containing information about completed capital projects, agency findings on energy efficiency investments, and exemptions granted.
2240514.quote: By no later than December 1 of each year, the mayor shall submit to the speaker of the council a report, in accordance with the procedure and format established by the department of design and construction, containing, at a minimum, the following information
2240514.deadline_text: By no later than December 1 of each year

2240514.action_summary: Promulgate rules to carry out the provisions of section 224.1 regarding green building standards for capital projects.
2240514.quote: The mayor shall promulgate rules to carry out the provisions of this section.

2240464.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
2240464.action_summary: Conduct an annual community air quality survey measuring pollutants at street-level monitoring sites across all seasons, analyzing variation across neighborhoods, identifying major local pollution sources, and producing maps of pollutant concentrations.
2240464.quote: The department shall conduct a community air quality survey on an annual basis. Such survey shall: 1. Measure pollutants at street-level at monitoring sites across the city of New York over every season of the year

2240464.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
2240464.action_summary: Write an annual report summarizing the results of community air quality survey activities including pollutant measurement, variation analysis, source identification, geographic and seasonal patterns, concentration maps, health surveillance findings, and scientific methodology.
2240464.quote: Write an annual report summarizing the results of the activities described in paragraphs one through five of this subdivision; 7. Include in such report the findings of any completed or ongoing health surveillance or research studies using community air quality survey data to estimate population exposure to pollutants; and 8. Describe in the report the scientific methodology used to select monitor locations

2240464.agency_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
2240464.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council an annual report with community air quality survey results and post a machine-readable copy on the department's website.
2240464.quote: Beginning April 22, 2016, and on or before April 22 annually thereafter, the department shall submit to the speaker of the council a report with the results of the annual community air quality survey for the most recently available year's analysis. The department shall post a copy of such annual report on the department's website. The data included in such posted report shall be in a machine-readable format.
2240464.deadline_text: Beginning April 22, 2016, and on or before April 22 annually thereafter

2460488.actor_raw: an office or agency designated by the mayor
2460488.action_summary: Conduct a series of examinations and verifications of mayoral agencies' compliance with open data requirements and make recommendations to improve disclosure and inclusion of public data sets on the single web portal.
2460488.quote: An office or agency designated by the mayor shall conduct a series of examinations and verifications, as described in subdivision c, and make recommendations to improve the disclosure and inclusion of all public data sets required to be on the single web portal

2460488.actor_raw: an office or agency designated by the mayor
2460488.action_summary: Present a plan for conducting examinations and verifications to the commissioner of investigation.
2460488.quote: Within 60 days of the effective date of this local law, an office or agency designated by the mayor shall present to the commissioner of investigation a plan for conducting the examinations and verifications described in subdivision c.

2460488.action_summary: Review the plan presented by the designated office or agency to ensure it conforms with a generally accepted auditing process or a process the Department of Investigation would use.

2460488.action_summary: Report to the mayor and the council when a plan for conducting examinations and verifications has been approved.
